title: Luokanopettaja
description:
Haettavana on luokanopettajan viransijaisuus ajaksi 4.1.2027-5.6.2027 Lähemäen koulussa.

Valittavalta edellytetään luokanopettajan kelpoisuutta asetuksen 986/1998 mukaan. Eduksi luetaan myönteinen suhtautuminen inklusiiviseen opetukseen.

Perusopetusta tai esiopetusta antavalla opettajalla tulee olla koulun opetuskielessä erinomainen suullinen ja kirjallinen taito.

Valittavalta toivotaan kiinnostusta ja monipuolista ammattitaitoa opetuksen ja koulun kehittämiseen, kehitys- ja yhteistyöhakuisuutta sekä rohkeutta tarttua uusiin asioihin.

Haastatteluun tulee ottaa mukaan alkuperäiset tutkinto- ja työtodistukset sekä oikeaksi todistetut kopiot tutkintotodistuksista, jotka jätetään haastattelijalle.

Virkasuhteeseen otettavan henkilön on ennen viran vastaanottamista esitettävä työnantajalle lääkärinlausunto terveydentilastaan sekä nähtäväksi rikosrekisterilain 6 §:n 2 momentissa tarkoitettu rikostaustaote (ns. lasten kanssa työskentelevien rikostaustaote). Valituksi tuleminen edellyttää hakijan suostumusta huumausainetestaukseen. Valitulle asetetaan koeaika.

Virkaa haetaan sähköisellä hakulomakkeella määräaikaan 30.10.2026 klo 15.00 mennessä Kuntarekryn kautta. Hakemukseen tulee liittää pdf-tiedostona tutkintotodistukset ja kelpoisuuden osoittava todistus.

title: Work Package Owner (E&I / Automation / Information Technology)
description:
About Company:

JC Automation Corp. (JCA) was founded in 1997 with the mission of filling a gap between technology and regulatory requirements in the life science manufacturing industry. The company offers highly capable resources at an affordable cost to build solutions and execute projects in: Automation, Control Systems Integration, Information Technology, System Integration and Regulatory Compliance.

JCA is a HUBZone Certified Small Business Firm, NMSDC Certified Minority Business Enterprise, and Certified Critical Industry Supplier. It’s mission is to add value by delivering quality services & solutions on time all the time by transforming processes & technology into business advantages.


ABOUT THE ROLE

A Work Package Owner is responsible for a defined scope area of the project from an Owner governance and integration perspective. The WPO maintains visibility of contractor performance, identifies risks and constraints, coordinates stakeholder interfaces, drives issue resolution, and ensures the package progresses toward mechanical completion and turnover in accordance with project objectives.

The WPO acts as the Owner's advocate in the field, ensuring decisions are made promptly, interfaces are properly managed, and risks are identified early while maintaining clear alignment among design, procurement, construction, systems completion, and CQV teams.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Base Work Package Ownership

  • Serve as the Owner representative for an assigned Base Work Package from field mobilization through mechanical completion and turnover.
  • Maintain overall awareness of package safety, quality, schedule, cost, productivity, and risk performance.
  • Establish and maintain package-level execution readiness and interface tracking plans.
  • Ensure Owner obligations and deliverables are completed in accordance with project requirements.

Contractor Performance Monitoring

  • Monitor contractor performance against approved safety, quality, schedule, and productivity goals.
  • Participate in field walks, coordination meetings, readiness reviews, and contractor progress discussions.
  • Identify emerging performance issues and escalate concerns through appropriate project governance channels.
  • Verify contractor-reported progress and support project controls reporting activities.

Constraint Management

  • Identify and track constraints impacting package execution.
  • Coordinate timely resolution of Owner-driven and cross-functional constraints.
  • Facilitate decisions related to design clarifications, procurement issues, access requirements, permits, turnover priorities, and operational interfaces.
  • Escalate unresolved constraints to project leadership when required.

Interface Management

  • Coordinate package interfaces with adjacent work packages, utility systems, infrastructure, commissioning activities, and operational stakeholders.
  • Ensure interface risks are identified, documented, tracked, and resolved.
  • Support planning and execution of tie-ins, shutdowns, energizations, and system integration activities.

Safety Oversight

  • Promote project safety culture and Owner HSE expectations.
  • Participate in safety observations, field engagements, audits, and leadership walks.
  • Monitor contractor compliance with project safety requirements.
  • Track and escalate significant safety concerns, trends, and recurring issues.

Quality Oversight

  • Monitor field quality performance and implementation of approved quality plans.
  • Support inspection readiness and adherence to project quality requirements.
  • Participate in quality reviews and issue resolution activities.
  • Track quality trends, deficiencies, punch list status, and corrective action closure.

Owner Equipment & Vendor Integration

  • Coordinate installation readiness and integration of Owner-furnished equipment and systems.
  • Interface with equipment suppliers and vendor representatives to support successful installation, startup, and turnover activities.
  • Track supplier deliverables, technical support requirements, and commissioning readiness.

Schedule & Progress Management

  • Support package-level progress assessment and forecasting activities.
  • Review contractor look-ahead plans and identify risks to upcoming work.
  • Coordinate Owner actions necessary to support planned execution activities.
  • Monitor milestone achievement and turnover readiness.

Turnover & CQV Readiness

  • Ensure package execution supports the project's systems-based turnover strategy from the earliest stages of construction.
  • Monitor progress against mechanical completion, systems completion, turnover, and CQV readiness milestones.
  • Coordinate with Construction Management, System Owners, Turnover Leads, CQV, Operations, and contractors to identify and remove barriers to system handover.
  • Promote construction sequencing and workface planning that enables phased turnover and efficient CQV execution.
  • Track and drive closure of deficiencies, punch list items, documentation gaps, testing activities, and turnover deliverables affecting system readiness.
  • Advocate for turnover and startup priorities during package planning and interface discussions.
  • Escalate risks that could impact mechanical completion, turnover milestones, commissioning activities, qualification schedules, or startup objectives.

Reporting & Communication

  • Provide routine package status updates including risks, constraints, safety trends, quality concerns, schedule impacts, and interface issues.
  • Maintain package dashboards, action-item logs, and issue trackers.
  • Present package status and recommendations to project leadership as required.

REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, or related technical discipline; equivalent construction and industry experience considered.
  • Minimum 10 years of experience supporting complex industrial, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, semiconductor, or similar capital projects.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating multi-disciplinary construction, startup, and turnover activities.
  • Strong understanding of contractor management, construction execution, quality systems, and project controls.
  • Experience with systems completion, mechanical completion, turnover, and CQV processes preferred.
  • Strong stakeholder management, interface management, and problem-solving skills.
  • OSHA 30 preferred.
  • English required; Spanish strongly preferred for projects located in Puerto Rico

Work Package Owner Roles


E&I / Automation / Information Technology

  • Focus on power distribution, instrumentation, controls, automation systems, network infrastructure, system integration, startup readiness, and commissioning support.

title: Supply Chain Director
description:
Position Summary

The Supply Chain Director provides strategic and operational leadership for Genie Reconditioning’s end-to-end supply chain function, including purchasing, material planning, scheduling, inventory management, warehousing, tool crib operations, shipping and receiving, vendor management, and distribution of finished equipment.

The position develops and executes supply chain strategies that support production requirements, customer commitments, cost objectives, inventory performance, and organizational growth. The Supply Chain Director establishes performance expectations, operating controls, budgets, policies, and procedures while ensuring critical materials, components, tooling, and services are available when needed to support reconditioning operations.

This role uses forecasting, operational data, supplier performance, production schedules, inventory trends, and key performance indicators to anticipate requirements, identify constraints, improve material flow, and drive continuous improvement across the supply chain.

The Supply Chain Director negotiates with suppliers, develops strategic vendor relationships, manages supply risk, and works closely with Operations, Sales, Engineering, Quality, Finance, and executive leadership to ensure supply chain activities align with company priorities.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Direct the overall Supply Chain function, including purchasing, procurement, material planning, scheduling, inventory control, warehousing, shipping and receiving, tool crib operations, and finished-goods distribution.
  • Develop and execute supply chain strategies aligned with production plans, financial objectives, customer requirements, and organizational growth.
  • Translate production forecasts and sales requirements into material, inventory, supplier, staffing, and logistics plans.
  • Establish and monitor key supply chain performance metrics, including inventory accuracy, material availability, supplier performance, purchase-price variance, schedule attainment, shortages, freight, and inventory turns.
  • Lead inventory and working-capital strategies that ensure material availability while controlling inventory levels and excess stock.
  • Develop sourcing strategies and lead the evaluation, selection, negotiation, and performance management of suppliers.
  • Identify and mitigate supplier, material, logistics, capacity, and other supply chain risks that could affect production or customer commitments.
  • Direct production scheduling, material planning, and material-flow activities to support production targets and reduce shortages or constraints.
  • Oversee warehouse, shipping, receiving, material staging, tool crib, and finished-equipment distribution activities.
  • Develop and manage the Supply Chain department budget, spending controls, and cost-reduction initiatives.
  • Partner with Operations, Finance, Engineering, Quality, and Sales to align supply chain decisions with production, cost, quality, customer, and business requirements.
  • Establish Supply Chain policies, procedures, internal controls, systems, and continuous-improvement priorities.
  • Lead, develop, and hold accountable Supply Chain managers, supervisors, group leads, professional staff, and hourly employees, including staffing, performance, training, and succession planning.
  • Provide executive leadership with regular supply chain performance reporting, forecasts, risks, constraints, and recommendations.

Leadership and Decision-Making Authority

The Supply Chain Director operates with significant independence within established company policies, financial controls, and executive direction.

The position:

  • Establishes functional priorities, objectives, processes, policies, and performance expectations for the Supply Chain organization.
  • Makes staffing recommendations and participates in hiring, compensation, performance-management, and succession decisions.
  • Leads and develops managers, supervisors, professional staff, group leads, and hourly employees.
  • Develops and manages departmental budgets and spending within approved financial authority.
  • Approves routine purchasing and supplier decisions within delegated authority.
  • Negotiates commercial terms, pricing, contracts, and supplier agreements within established authority.
  • Determines training and development priorities for the Supply Chain function.
  • Escalates significant contractual, financial, legal, supplier-risk, or non-standard business matters to executive leadership when appropriate.

Education and Experience

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, business administration, operations management, logistics, engineering, or a related field.
  • Minimum of five years of progressively responsible management experience in supply chain, purchasing, materials management, logistics, manufacturing operations, or a closely related function.
  • Demonstrated experience managing a significant supply chain function and leading managers, supervisors, professional staff, and hourly employees.
  • Strong knowledge of purchasing, inventory management, production planning, forecasting, warehousing, logistics, supplier management, and material flow.
  • Experience developing and monitoring departmental budgets and operational KPIs.
  • Demonstrated supplier negotiation and vendor-management experience.
  • Strong analytical ability and experience using operational data to support business decisions.

Preferred

  • Supply chain leadership experience within manufacturing, heavy equipment, automotive, remanufacturing, industrial equipment, or a related environment.
  • Experience supporting high-mix production or reconditioning operations.
  • Experience with ERP, MRP, inventory-control, purchasing, production-scheduling, or manufacturing-execution systems.
  • Professional certification such as APICS CPIM, CSCP, CPSM, or equivalent.
  • Experience implementing Lean, continuous-improvement, material-flow, or inventory-optimization initiatives.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Deep knowledge of supply chain operations with solid understanding of the broader manufacturing and business environment.
  • Ability to develop strategy while maintaining visibility into daily operational execution.
  • Strong financial and business judgment.
  • Ability to analyze large amounts of operational information and translate findings into practical actions.
  • Strong negotiation and supplier-management skills.
  • Ability to anticipate supply constraints and develop effective contingency plans.
  • Strong organizational and prioritization skills.
  • Ability to lead multiple functional areas through subordinate managers and supervisors.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with executive leadership, employees, suppliers, customers, and cross-functional partners.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making capability.
  • Ability to establish accountability and drive measurable improvement.
  • Ability to manage competing production, inventory, cost, and customer priorities.
  • Transportation and logistics partners

Physical and Work Environment Requirements

The position operates in both office and manufacturing environments. The employee must be able to regularly move throughout warehouse, production, shipping, receiving, and material-storage areas to observe operations, evaluate conditions, and support employees.

The position may occasionally require standing, walking, bending, reaching, climbing stairs, and lifting or moving materials consistent with normal manufacturing and warehouse activities. Appropriate personal protective equipment must be worn when entering designated production or operational areas.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

Disclaimer

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by employees assigned to this position. title: Housing Stability Worker
description:
SLCS is currently seeking a full-time Housing Stability Worker for Project Home, a housing first program. Project Home focuses on housing adults and youth who have experienced chronic homelessness, anchoring them in their community, and establishing a sense of belonging through the provision of assertive and intensive housing first case management. As a member of this team, you will provide assessment, crisis intervention, and housing stability/homeless prevention support services to individuals in the city of London.


Working within a multifaceted team, you will manage a caseload, and work directly with program participants to support the establishment of personal goals, which focus on accessing safe, secure housing and remaining stably housed, as well as connecting to community services to support long-term goals. You will be responsible for advocating on behalf of participants and liaising with other services (i.e. emergency shelters, community organizations, health care services, income supports, as well as the legal system) to coordinate care for individuals. As a member of the Project Home team, you will contribute to the ongoing development of the program, and to the broader citywide homeless services system.

As an SLCS employee, you will be responsible for the safety and security of program participants, co-workers and community during your employment. You will work collaboratively with other team members and community partners to complete administrative functions for the program.


This position requires excellent time management, strong organizational skills as well as the ability to multitask. You will also have strong written, verbal and social skills to interact with the many personalities we support on a daily basis. The role is community-based and you will be expected to regularly travel within the London community. The schedule for Project Home would be working mainly Monday – Friday on a rotation of 9am – 5:30pm and 10:30am – 7pm, with one weekend from 10am – 6pm in a 4-week rotation.


Required Qualifications:



  • Post-secondary education from an accredited institution in a related field
  • 1-3 years’ experience working with a diverse population, including individuals impacted by mental illness, justice system involvement, addictions and homelessness
  • Intermediate / Standard First Aid & CPR with AED - Level C
  • Valid Full G Class Driver’s License and access to reliable vehicle
  • Experience using HIFIS 4.0 considered an asset
  • Candidates who are proficient in both official languages of Canada will be considered an asset

What we offer:

  • Employer paid benefits package

  • Employer RRSP contributions
  • Wage grid includes annual wage progression
  • Investment in your professional growth through professional development funds

This position requires a clear Police Check with vulnerable sector screening as a required condition of employment, as per SLCS policy. We adhere to the French Language Services Act and are committed to equity, diversity, and an inclusive, barrier-free workplace under the AODA. If accommodation is needed during recruitment, please inform the contact person. This posting is for an existing vacancy and we do not use AI in screening of applicants.

SLCS values a diverse workforce to achieve our mission. We encourage applications from racialized communities, First Nations, Inuit, Métis, 2SLGBTQIA+ individuals, people with disabilities or chronic illnesses, diverse faith communities, and those with varied lived experiences. title: DME/Orthopedic Technician
description:
Job Title: DME Fitter/Orthopedic Technician Float

This is a Full-Time position, under general supervision, assists physicians with care and treatment of orthopedic patients, including, but not limited to, casting, bracing, and application of traction. DME fitting includes and is not limited to fitting, refitting, custom measurement, education, billing, collection of co-ins/Deductible and patient satisfaction. Who We Are

View the SENS Product Catalog


Summary

The Senior Project Manager – Power Systems (PowerCab2) will lead the execution model for PowerCab2 customer projects from commercial handoff through delivery. This role will serve as the operational quarterback for PowerCab2 orders, ensuring that customer commitments are clearly defined, cross-functional owners are aligned, risks are surfaced early, and projects move through Engineering, Production, Supply Chain, Order Management, and Customer Success with discipline and urgency.

This is not a passive project-tracking role. The successful candidate must be comfortable driving accountability across functions, challenging unclear answers, escalating blockers, and protecting customer outcomes while maintaining credibility with internal teams. The role requires a blend of project management discipline, customer-facing communication, operational rigor, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-growing, high-change environment.

Responsibilities

Project Delivery & Governance

  • Lead PowerCab2 customer projects from order acceptance through final shipment and customer delivery.
  • Own the current portfolio and project execution rhythm for assigned PowerCab2 orders, including timeline, status, blockers, risks, customer commitments, and internal follow-through.
  • Serve as the primary cross-functional coordinator between Sales, Sales Operations, Order Management, Customer Success, Engineering, Production, Supply Chain, Finance, and other required teams.
  • Ensure each PowerCab2 project has clear scope, committed delivery expectations, defined owners, and documented handoffs.
  • Help build and refine the scalable PowerCab2 execution model, including process flows, swim lanes, handoffs, milestone definitions, escalation points, and ownership rules.
  • Support the transition from engineered-to-order work toward configured-to-order execution where appropriate.
  • Partner with Engineering and Commercial teams to operationalize PowerCab2 configuration rules, approved options, “Lego block” standards, and quote-to-build requirements.
  • Help define how PowerCab2 projects move through standard, repeatable, configurable, and engineered lanes.
  • Identify recurring process breakdowns and partner with functional leaders to eliminate root causes.


Customer and Project Communication

  • Communicate professionally with customer project managers, construction managers, switchgear OEMs, contractors, and internal account owners as needed.
  • Proactively identify customer needs, document expectations and desired outcomes early, and hold the customer/project manager accountable to agreed inputs, decisions, and timelines so SENS can operationally deliver the intended customer experience.
  • Translate internal project realities into clear, credible customer-facing updates.
  • Protect the customer experience by ensuring changes, delays, risks, and decisions are communicated clearly and timely.
  • Hold customers accountable when customer-driven changes, late inputs, unclear requirements, or scope changes create schedule or cost risk.
  • Balance customer advocacy with operational credibility, ensuring SENS does not make commitments that cannot be supported.


Cross-Functional Accountability

  • Drive internal teams toward clear commitments, timely decisions, and early escalation when delivery, scope, or customer commitments are at risk.
  • Hold Engineering, Production, Supply Chain, Sales, and other stakeholders accountable to agreed project requirements, timelines, and escalation paths.
  • Identify gaps between what was sold, what was ordered, what was engineered, what can be built, and what was promised to the customer.


Operating Model Development

  • Help build and refine the scalable PowerCab2 execution model, including process flows, swim lanes, handoffs, milestone definitions, escalation points, and ownership rules.
  • Support the transition from engineered-to-order work toward configured-to-order execution where appropriate.
  • Partner with Engineering and Commercial teams to operationalize PowerCab2 configuration rules, approved options, “Lego block” standards, and quote-to-build requirements.
  • Help define how PowerCab2 projects move through standard, repeatable, configurable, and engineered lanes.
  • Identify recurring process breakdowns and partner with functional leaders to eliminate root causes.
  • Identify recurring process breakdowns across the PowerCab2 quote-to-delivery lifecycle and partner with functional leaders to eliminate root causes.


Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, engineering, supply chain, project management, or a related field.
  • 8+ years of experience in project management, program management, service delivery, operations, customer project delivery, order management, or commercial execution.
  • Experience managing cross-functional projects involving Sales, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, and customer-facing teams.
  • Strong ability to drive accountability without direct authority.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage customer commitments, timelines, risks, escalations, and executive-level visibility.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to simplify complex issues and provide clear, direct status updates.
  • High attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple active projects simultaneously.
  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with evolving processes and incomplete structure.
  • Ability to challenge assumptions, ask direct questions, and push teams toward decisions and commitments.
  • Proficiency with project tracking tools, CRM/ERP systems, Microsoft Office, Teams, Excel, and reporting tools.


Preferred Qualifications

  • PMP, CAPM, Six Sigma, Lean, or related project/process certification.
  • Experience in manufacturing, electrical systems, power systems, switchgear, data centers, utility, industrial, or engineered product environments.
  • Experience with configured-to-order or engineered-to-order product delivery.
  • Experience working with customer-side project managers, construction managers, OEMs, contractors, or channel partners.
  • Experience with HubSpot, Syteline, CPQ tools, Smartsheet, Microsoft Project, Planner, Power BI, or similar platforms.
  • Understanding of quote-to-cash, order-to-delivery, and customer success/service delivery processes.

title: Resident Advisor
description:
Resident Advisor

Salary Range: $21.00

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt Level: Entry

CLASSIFICATION PURPOSE

Performs a variety of administrative and client-centered wellness and safety activities at an assigned interim and family housing sites.


ALLOCATION STANDARDS

Positions allocable to this entry-level class report to a site program manager and perform various administrative, wellness and safety, and client support activities requiring knowledge and understanding of housing first, harm reduction and trauma-informed principles. Position incumbents work independently and carry out assignment responsibilities within an established framework of program policies and operating procedures. Position responsibilities involve regular client interactions requiring the use of good judgment, empathy, compassion, situational awareness, and collaboration in order to address and resolve routine and complex issues surrounding client behavior, medical and housing needs. Position incumbents maintain regular communication with Care Coordinators in order to support their efforts in assisting clients with legal, health, personal, recovery, and other issues, during their assigned shift. Resident Advisors also provide for the general welfare and safety of all persons that visit the interim housing and family site or its grounds and engage in activities that promote positive relationships with neighboring residents, businesses, and organizations.


ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES

  • Conducts inspections at assigned interim and family housing sites in accordance with established procedures in order to identify and address potential security issues, safety hazards, health and fire code violations, and maintenance repair needs.
  • Performs and documents wellness rounds at assigned and family interim housing facilities following established procedures in order to check on client health and safety needs, administer overdose antidotes, monitor and enforce compliance with occupancy agreements.
  • Participates in daily meetings with Program Management, Care Coordinators, and other Resident Advisors at the start of a new shift in order to discuss client activity, behavior and needs, perimeter and wellness check observations, and incident reports.
  • Maintains a welcoming, clean, and supportive environment for clients and visitors by following established protocols in place at the assigned interim and family housing facility.
  • Enforces interim and family housing safety requirements in order to minimize and prevent hazardous or potentially violent conditions that could result in client or structural harm by following pre-approved protocols and methods.
  • Performs regular walks through the surrounding neighborhood at designed interim and family housing facilities in order to build relationships with residents, foster positive relations, and mitigate escalation of community concerns.
  • Ensures compliance with interim and family housing facility policies and rules by monitoring client behavior, addressing violations, and implementing corrective actions as needed to maintain a safe and orderly living environment.
  • Maintains a variety of documents containing client and visitor data following established interim housing facility procedures in order to comply with record keeping requirements.
  • Assists with the orderly and efficient receipt, storage, and distribution of meals to interim housing clients in a manner consistent with operating procedures.
  • Provides as needed administrative and facility set-up assistance in support of volunteer activities at assigned interim housing facilities.
  • Attends on-site and off-site trainings, team meetings, and occasional events as required, in order to participate in discussions and activities, obtain information to enhance professional development, and contribute to the overall effectiveness of interim housing operations.


KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Ability to serve the homeless community with an inherent desire that demonstrates empathy, compassion, and a commitment to supporting their well-being and quality of life.
  • Basic active listening skills in order to understand and engage with clients, visitors, co-workers, and others.
  • Ability to demonstrate empathy in order to understand and share the feelings of clients when interacting on sensitive matters.
  • Ability to demonstrate compassion when interacting with clients so as to recognize and respond to their needs and struggles with kindness and understanding.
  • Ability to discern such things as behavior, body language, and tone in order apply appropriate approaches and de-escalation techniques when interacting with clients on delicate, sensitive or potentially dangerous situations.
  • Ability to assert authority with tact, diplomacy and collaboration in order to effectively address and resolve situations involving client violations of policies and procedures.
  • Ability to remain calm and composed in challenging situations involving client interactions, medical emergencies, and incidents requiring law enforcement intervention.
  • Ability to demonstrate sensitivity to diverse cultural backgrounds, mental health needs, substance use, and other individual circumstances affecting homeless populations in order to engage clients with respect and compassion.
  • Ability to learn and apply new concepts and protocols on a continuous basis in order to adapt to changing requirements.
  • Basic written and oral expression skills in order to effectively communicate in writing and/or via in-person verbal interactions.
  • Basic customer service excellence skills in order to establish and maintain positive, friendly, and professional interactions with guests, visitors, and staff.
  • Basic skill in the application of office software, such as electronic mail, word processing, scanning software (Adobe, PDF) in order to open and respond to email, type or prepare written materials, and scan documents.
  • Basic skill in the operation of office equipment and machines, such as desktop or laptop computers, printers, and scanners.


Essential Physical Characteristics

The physical characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential job duties of this classification. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of a job, on a case-by-case basis.


  • Continuous: walking, standing, bending and twisting of neck, bending and twisting of waist, squatting, simple grasping, reaching above and below shoulder level, and lifting and carrying of materials over 25 pounds.
  • Frequent: sitting, repetitive use of hands to operate computers, printers and copiers. Exposure to outdoor weather, noise, dust, fluctuating temperature, and lighting.


Workplace Hazard Exposure

The workplace hazard exposure conditions described here are representative of those that an employee may likely encounter in the performance of the essential job duties of this classification.

  • Exposure to potential physical and verbal attacks by clients
  • Death threats
  • Exposure to controlled substances and paraphernalia
  • Exposure to fumes from controlled substances
  • Exposure to smoke from cigarettes
  • Exposure to communicable diseases, such as tuberculosis, scabies, lice
  • Exposure to clients using weapons, such as knives and guns
  • Exposure to bed bugs
  • Exposure to the sun and heat
  • Exposure to vicarious trauma
  • Exposure to vehicle traffic conditions
  • Exposure to bodily fluids (urine, blood, saliva, and fecal matter)
  • Exposure to dog bites


EDUCATION, TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE

No experience required.

All new hires are required to complete a 90-day introductory period during which they must complete an initial 40-hour training program. The training will cover Union Station Homeless Services’ housing first, harm reduction and trauma-informed program model, interim and family housing policies and procedures, client wellness and safety protocols, and other key people management policies. All new hires must also complete CPR and Security Guard training within 60-days of their hire date.


HIRING ASSESSMENTS

The hiring process for this classification will consist of two parts. Part I: online assessment to evaluate basic software application, written expression, and customer service skills scored on a pass/fail basis. Part II: oral interview to evaluate interest and motivation to work in the homeless services sector, oral expression, interpersonal effectiveness, empathy, compassion, situational awareness, and problem solving. Applicants must achieve a score of 70% or higher in order to be placed on the hiring list.


PREEMPLOYMENT BACKGROUND CHECK

Following an offer of employment, all candidates will be required to pass background check consisting of a criminal and references check.

title: Senior Product Manager, Consumer - Audiobooks
description:
We design Spotify's consumer experience - end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints - from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.

We're looking for a strategic, detail-oriented Senior Product Manager to join the Books Vertical and lead end-to-end book experiences on Spotify: from discovery and conversion through to listening, and from the creator pipeline through to the consumer shelf. This role is about connecting the dots across our core experiences, conversion flows, content pipeline, and creator tooling to make books work seamlessly on Spotify.

Books are a major focus for Spotify, and we need someone who can look holistically across the book ecosystem to identify gaps, reduce friction, and make sure our experiences are coherent end-to-end. You'll focus on making the full books journey work better for listeners, creators, and rights-holders, not just shipping new features. You'll partner closely with Personalization, Subscriptions, Experience, and creator-facing teams to strengthen and evolve book experiences across surfaces, and help shape a product strategy that directly improves how listeners discover and enjoy books.

What You'll Do

  • Shape and execute product strategy across core book experiences, conversion flows, content pipeline, and creator tooling.

  • Partner with teams across Spotify to identify and close gaps across book surfaces, creating a coherent end-to-end experience from content pipeline through to the consumer experience.

  • Collaborate with Design, Engineering, Product Insights, and Program Management to lead improvements across discovery, conversion, listening, and creator-facing surfaces.

  • Conduct, commission, and use research to understand listener behavior, creator needs, book consumption patterns, and market trends.

  • Use qualitative and quantitative insights to identify the most impactful opportunities across the book ecosystem and prioritize accordingly.

  • Define and track success metrics across the book experience, connecting upstream pipeline health with downstream listener outcomes.

  • Identify systemic friction points and opportunities across the book ecosystem, and advocate for improvements that strengthen the end-to-end experience.

Who You Are

  • You have 4+ years of experience in product management, ideally working across complex product ecosystems with multiple surfaces, partners, and dependencies.

  • You have a track record of improving multi-surface product experiences, not just launching new features but making existing systems work better together.

  • You use analytics, A/B testing, and user research to guide product decisions.

  • You're comfortable working across both consumer-facing and platform or tooling surfaces, and can move between listener needs and creator needs.

  • You communicate clearly and build shared understanding across teams that don't always see each other's work, translating between consumer, pipeline, and creator perspectives.

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity and managing complexity across multiple teams and partners.

  • You think in systems and map how changes in one part of the ecosystem (content pipeline, creator tooling, conversion flows, consumer surfaces) affect the rest.

  • You look for the most impactful fix rather than optimizing surfaces in isolation.

Where You'll Be

  • This role is based in London or Stockholm
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.
Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

title: Product Manager
description:
We're making energy fair, clean, and simple for all using technology.
Octopus Energy started with a bold idea: to build Britain’s first truly digital energy supplier. By combining world-class tech with brilliant humans who care deeply about customers and driving the renewable energy transition, we made it happen and in 2025, we became Britain’s largest energy supplier.

Octopus Energy Group is a global energy transition collective. 10 businesses working across 4 continents to tackle energy transformation at nearly every front.

And we constantly push to make energy better. Tirelessly campaigning for fair protections for customers. And building innovative technologies that forge a path to a green energy system.

We’re made up of 10,000+ authentic, committed people working around the world on stuff you'd never expect. We're united by a shared goal: to drive the global green energy revolution. Read our Spotlight series to meet some of the team.

About the role

OE Tech is the engineering and product organisation inside Octopus Energy. Here you’ll have real ownership, variety, and the chance to shape products that make a tangible difference in people’s lives: lowering bills, enabling greener living, and delivering experiences customers genuinely love. You’ll work side by side with teams across services, marketing, operations, and data, and see the impact of your work in the real world, fast.

In North America, Octopus recently invested in Uplight. We are looking for a Product Manager to join our OE Tech team, focused on our North American work at Uplight.

Uplight makes software that manages energy resources in homes and businesses, including things like smart thermostats, electric vehicles, solar panels, storage batteries, heat pumps, and even people’s behaviour, to generate, shift, or save energy to balance the grid, making it more efficient and reliable. This creates clean energy capacity that can be used by the power grid instead of burning more fossil fuels. These solutions are accelerating the transition to clean energy and saving money for energy customers.

Our goal is to ensure scaling up never means slowing down or compromising on a world-class customer journey for low carbon tech. In this role, you will be responsible for the core user experience of optimising smart devices - ensuring it’s seamless for customers and for the program managers managing demand response programs at scale. You’ll enable energy companies to predictably rely on the load shed of aggregated smart devices, such as smart thermostats, to ensure dispatch is scalable, resilient, and easy to use.

You’ll work side by side with engineers, customer operations, and field teams to shape the digital products that scale up electro-tech in homes.

We embrace flat hierarchies and an open, agile culture that fosters innovation, flexibility, and creativity. We don’t hang our personalities up with our coats and nor should you.

At Octopus, we hire great people who get stuff done, all whilst being themselves.

What you'll do

  • You’ll work across one of our products and run a clear, forward-looking roadmap that prioritises the biggest opportunities while proactively keeping an eye on dependencies across different teams.

  • Take full ownership of planning, running, delivering and monitoring key missions in your area, keeping things on track and making sure everything hands off smoothly.

  • Day to day execution - you’ll break things down so engineering teams can ship quickly and smoothly, write PRDs, and run rituals that ensure different teams are beautifully aligned.

  • Be a product discovery champion, rapidly experimenting, vibe coding prototypes before passing them over to engineering.

  • Keep your roadmap flexible and driven by fresh insights, getting feedback on new opportunities, risks, and trade-offs and running data analysis to inform your approach.

  • Map out and manage your stakeholder network, ensuring everyone has a shared understanding of what we're building and the customer value we expect to bring.

  • Put yourself in the customer’s shoes, working across UX, data, and engineering to uncover hidden pain points and turn them into great user experiences.

  • Keep our product documentation in great shape, keep an eye on market trends, and help Group PMs out with commercial agreements and external suppliers.

What you'll have

  • 3+ years of product management experience with some great stories about taking an idea from initial discovery all the way to launch and user adoption.

  • Experience in startups or fast-moving scale-ups where you've had to figure things out without a rigid playbook.

  • Real care for customers. You think about their experience constantly and push the team to get the details right.

  • Comfort with AI to vibe code prototypes, and with data to write your own queries so you can grab data and test ideas independently.

  • A natural urge to discover and experiment, meaning you're entirely comfortable working alongside UX and engineering to test assumptions and build lean MVPs fast.

  • Experience navigating busy stakeholder environments, building trust, and keeping different teams aligned around a shared vision.

  • Plenty of flexibility and focus, meaning you stay calm when things are ambiguous, juggle competing priorities well, and know how to weigh risk against business value.

  • A healthy curiosity about the wider market, competitor movements, and how business cases and ROI tie into your product decisions.

  • A deeply collaborative spirit that naturally bridges the gaps between UX, data, and engineering, keeping the customer's real-world experience at the center of every single decision.

Nice to haves

  • Familiarity with energy, flexibility, utilities, or other regulated industries.

  • Experience working in data-science driven products

Why else you'll love it here

• Wondering what the salary for this role is? Just ask us! On a call with one of our recruiters it's something we always cover as we genuinely want to match your experience with the correct salary. The reason why we don't advertise is because we honestly have a degree of flexibility and would never want salary to be a reason why someone doesn't apply to Octopus - what's more important to us is finding the right octofit!
• Octopus Energy Group is a unique culture. An organisation where people learn, decide, and build quicker. Where people work with autonomy, alongside a wide range of amazing co-owners, on projects that break new ground. We want your hard work to be rewarded with perks you actually care about! We were named the UK's top company to work for in 2025, and we ranked in the top ten in the Sunday Times Best Places to Work 2026. Our Group CEO, Greg has recorded a podcast about our culture and how we empower our people. We’ve also been placed in the top 10 companies for senior leadership
• Visit our UK perks hub - Octopus Employee Benefits
If this sounds like you then we'd love to hear from you, tell us what you care about, why Octopus feels right and most importantly, bring us the real you! Applying for jobs can be a bit scary so have a nose through some of our tips first 🚀
P.S. Our process usually takes up to 4 weeks, but we’ll always do our best to flex around what works for you. Along the way, you’ll chat with our recruitment team and your Recruiter will help you throughout different stages. Got any burning questions before then? Drop us a message at talent@octoenergy.com and we’d love to help!
Are you ready for a career with us? We want to ensure you have all the tools and environment you need to unleash your potential. Need any specific accommodations? Whether you require specific accommodations or have a unique preference, let us know, and we'll do what we can to customise your interview process for comfort and maximum magic!
Studies have shown that some groups of people, like women, are less likely to apply to a role unless they meet 100% of the job requirements. Whoever you are, if you like one of our jobs, we encourage you to apply as you might just be the candidate we hire. Across Octopus, we're looking for genuinely decent people who are honest and empathetic. Our people are our strongest asset and the unique skills and perspectives people bring to the team are the driving force of our success. As an equal opportunity employer, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute. Our commitment is to provide equal opportunities, an inclusive work environment, and fairness for everyone.

title: Key Holder
description:
ABOUT US

For over 40 years, Brahmin has been designing luxury handbags that spark confidence in the people who carry them. Our croc-embossed Melbourne leather has been our signature since our start in 1982 and is well-loved for its one-of-a-kind texture. It all starts with a design. Each product is thoughtfully engineered for fashion and functionality. Then we hit the road to source the finest materials from around the globe. Be a part of our Retail team to deliver an elevated customer experience across our store fleet while driving profitable, scalable growth.


ABOUT THE TEAM

You will report directly to the Store Manager and Assistant Store Manager, partnering closely to lead a dedicated staff of fellow key holders and sales associates. Together, this team fosters a collaborative, high-energy environment focused on exceeding daily sales targets. As a keyholder on this team, you will directly influence performance, champion a culture of shared success, and be eligible for a sales commission that rewards your ability to drive the store's financial growth.

YOUR IMPACT

As a Part-Time Key Holder, you will play a pivotal role in driving store success by owning sales goals and unlocking extra earning potential through our competitive commission structure. Partnering closely with management, you will deliver an exceptional luxury customer experience, execute visual merchandising directions, and directly manage, mentor, and recruit a high-performing sales team to shape a collaborative, result-driven selling culture.


WHAT YOU’LL OWN

Talent Management:

  • Coordinate staff by providing timely coaching and feedback to maximize individual and team performance.
  • Develop and maintain positive working relationships that support a positive work environment.
  • Support the education of the store team fashion trends and product knowledge.
  • Maintain two-way communication with the store Manager to stay abreast of company and store information and brand initiative, as well as inform the manager of
    all store activities.
  • Ensure associates follow dress code and meet appearance standards that professionally represent the brand.
  • Support an environment that positions Brahmin Leather Works as an Employer of Choice.
  • Support effective on boarding and support learning opportunities.
  • Provide basic direction to associates and appropriately delegate tasks.
  • Support Store Manager with recruiting functions: Network and Recruit.
  • Support Store Manger with developing talent: Ensure effective on-boarding.
  • Provide timely coaching and feedback to associates when appropriate: Support the Store Manager with performance issues.


Sales and Service:

  • Achieve sales and service metrics in key measurable areas including: DPTs, UPTs, AURs and Customer Conversion.
  • Use Company resources and personal leadership to facilitate and sustain a strong selling environment that holds associates accountable for
    achieving productivity standards and other sales metrics.
  • Analyze store reports to optimize performance and take action based on business trends.
  • Lead by example and maintain consistent selling and service standards through communication, training and individual accountability. Assist in identifying
    opportunities to maximize sales and ensure financial goals are achieved.
  • Demonstrate a high level of selling and customer service skills to achieve sales.
  • Service multiple customers at a time, multi-task or handle projects simultaneously.
  • Exhibits knowledge of industry trends and our competitions


Building Clientele:

  • Manage and guide associates to consistently market Brahmin brand initiatives and grow key sales and service metrics
  • Ensure exceptional selling interactions that guarantee meaningful experience and build brand relationships.
  • Drive brand loyalty by supporting all service enhancers to build strong relationships, including active use of clients books and marketing initiatives with local
    business for store events.
  • Take an active role in assisting the Store Manager to build store business.


Store Operations:

  • Plan and prioritize tasks and responsibilities to meet the needs of the business.
  • Maintain store cleanliness and housekeeping standards.
  • Protect company assets and maintain a safe work environment.
  • Ensure compliance with all company policies and procedures as well as local, state and federal employment laws.
  • Support the planning and execution of Brahmin brand visual direction.
  • Participate and lead special projects and other duties as assigned.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • Leads with integrity and enthusiasm to motivate total store achievement.
  • Has a strong sense of drive, ambition and passion for selling ensuring the overall store business success.
  • Must be outgoing and assertive with the ability to make store business successful.
  • Ability to communicate professionally and in a timely matter with the Store Manager, customers, associates, and company partners.
  • Ability to lead by example and maintain consistent selling and service standards through communication, training and individual accountability.
  • Ability to partner with management on store issues.
  • Maintain professional appearance that reflects the brand.
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule based on the needs of the business including opening/closing shifts as well as weekends and holidays.
  • High School or General Equivalency Diploma (GED) required and 1-2 years of retail experience, luxury retail is preferred.



PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS


Must be able to stand up to 100% of working time during a work shift standing and moving. This role involves constant moving, communicating, reaching, grabbing and standing for the entire work shift. Occasionally involves stooping, kneeling, crouching and climbing ladders. Must be able to lift up to 40 pounds.

title: VISALIA Gopfert-2 RDC 2nd Assistant 3rd Shift
description:

The Gopfert-2 RDC 2nd Assistant Operator supports the Machine Operator and 1st Assistant in the safe, efficient, and high-quality operation of the Gopfert Rotary Die Cutter (RDC). This position is responsible for assisting in setup, monitoring machine operation, and ensuring smooth workflow throughout production. The 2nd Assistant plays an active role in maintaining productivity, product quality, and compliance with all safety and operational standards.

Key Responsibilities:

· Assist the Operator with machine setup and adjustments as directed to meet production requirements.

· Perform quality checks and inspections per the sampling plan and report any nonconformities promptly.

· Monitor and maintain pallet and dunnage inserter, pallet handling, and waste tracking to support efficient production.

· Participate in clean-up and preventive maintenance (PM) activities to ensure machine reliability and safety.

· Accurately record production data, waste, and other operational information in the computer system.

· Anticipate upcoming needs for materials and supplies to maintain uninterrupted machine operation.

· Work cooperatively with the machine crew to achieve production goals for speed, quality, and uptime.

· Adhere to all safety policies, standard operating procedures, and housekeeping standards.

Qualifications and Requirements:

· Ability to read and interpret factory hard cards, CADs, and production documentation.

· Proficiency with a tape measure and ability to perform basic math functions, including multiplication and division.

· Basic computer literacy for production reporting and data entry.

· Strong communication and teamwork skills with the ability to anticipate crew and machine needs.

· Demonstrated ability to contribute to machine performance and overall production goals.

· Must be able to speak, read, and write English fluently.

· Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and stand for extended periods in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Preferred Skills:

· Minimum 6 months of experience as an Entry-Level Assistant in the flexographic and/or rotary die-cutting industry.

· Working knowledge of flexographic printing and rotary die-cutting operations.

· Familiarity with Gopfert-2 RDC systems or similar converting equipment.

· Commitment to continuous improvement, safety, and 5S/Lean practices.

title: Software Engineer, Frontend
description:
Monumental is automating on-site construction with robotics and software. Our mission is to make construction software-defined and autonomous - a future where beautiful, bespoke buildings go up in a single day, with minimal labour.

We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from companies like Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta and Google DeepMind. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you’ll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural.

Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with an fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house - hardware and software, we're explicitly not a hybrid or remote-first company - you can't build robots or walls from home, so we're onsite five days a week.

Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision and company. You might enjoy our YouTube Channel, Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage, or this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like.

About the role

At Monumental we’re automating on-site construction with robotics and software. Atrium, our operating system for construction, lets us do everything from designing the 3D structures we'll build, to managing our robot fleet, planning operations, and analyzing data.

As we scale our operations and manufacture, deploy, and maintain more robots, the scope of our software keeps growing. We're now building internal apps for scheduling robot operators, planning site logistics and maintenance, and improving manufacturing. We're looking for a frontend engineer to help us build more and better internal tools, and to move manual processes into software.

You won't just be handed requirements. You'll talk to the people who'll use what you build (your colleagues), work out what's actually worth building, implement it, deploy it, and check whether it helped. If you enjoy building software products start to finish on your own, this role is a good fit. You'll get a lot of autonomy and the chance to build software that builds actual robots and houses. For more on how we think about the role, read Tobias’ post on why now is a great time to be a product engineer at Monumental.

What you'll do

  • Taking a problem from a colleague and understanding it, building a prototype, getting it in their hands, and iterating on the solution - often all in the same day.

  • Designing and building tools to manage a growing fleet of robots spread across multiple sites.

  • Extending Fenestra, our Notion-like internal tool for viewing and editing data from different sources.

  • Helping bring prototypes from the ops and manufacturing teams to production, cleaning up the data model and code along the way.

  • Working with hardware engineers, control engineers, and robot operators to find the best product experience for genuinely hard problems.

  • Writing clean, idiomatic, typed production TypeScript and React. We also use Rust in places.

  • Debugging memory leaks, crashes, and other problems, often by digging into the root cause yourself.

  • Deploying and maintaining new backend services your tools need.

What we’re looking for

  • You've built full-featured web apps in idiomatic TypeScript and shipped them. React experience is a plus.

  • Proven experience in building products in a zero-to-one environment, on your own or in a small team. This can be a side-project you’ve worked on, an indie app, or some other project you can show us.

  • An eye for good design, both UI and UX.

  • A strong sense of ownership. You can drive a project from start to finish without anyone managing you, and you're comfortable when things are chaotic.

  • You use coding agents to ship faster and unblock yourself but take full ownership of the features you build with AI.

  • You pick up new languages and tools quickly. Rust experience is a plus.

  • Basic familiarity with Linux systems. E.g., you’re comfortable ssh’ing into other machines to figure out why something isn't working.

Why Monumental?

Joining Monumental means being at the forefront of a movement aimed at making significant strides in the construction industry. Here, your work has the potential to impact not just the company but the future of how we build. If you're driven by innovation, eager to tackle complex challenges, and ready to make a tangible difference, we want to hear from you.

For open applications (where you don’t see an exact role match), please reach out to us at: iwanttojoin@monumental.co - share with us the most interesting or challenging project you’ve worked on, why you want to join and your CV or portfolio.

Unfortunately we do not currently support internships.

If you don’t meet all the qualifications here but are excited about Monumental and feel you’d still be able to help us solve difficult problems, do get in touch. We welcome generalists who focus on outcomes and are eager to learn on the job.

title: IT Associate
description:
IT Associate, Toronto Office

title: Varhaiserityiskasvatuksen lastenhoitaja, Sampolan päiväkoti
description:
Haluatko asteen verran paremman työpaikan? Tulepa töihin Oulun kaupungin varhaiskasvatukseen!
Meillä tutkitusti viihdytään työssä: saat kannustavat ja innostavat työkaverit ja esihenkilön. Saat kehittyä ja kouluttautua, ja halutessasi pääset myös työkiertoon. Olemme aina kansallisen kehittämisen kärjessä. Meistä alkaa oululainen yhtenäisen kasvun ja opin polku. Tule lapsiystävälliseen Ouluun tekemään kulttuuri-ilmastonmuutosta!

Haettavana on VARHAISERITYISKASVATUKSEN LASTENHOITAJAN määräaikainen tehtävä Sampolan päiväkodissa alkaen sopimuksen mukaan mahdollisimman pian ja päättyen 30.6.2027.

Sampolan päiväkoti toimii varhaiskasvatuksen ja opettajankoulutuksen tutkimus- ja kehittämisyksikkönä. Toimintamme perustuu vahvuusperustaiseen, positiiviseen pedagogiikkaan. Työskentelymme on projektiluontoista ja tapahtuu aina pienryhmissä. Toimimme Steam-pedagogiikan toimintamallin mukaisesti. Kannustamme lasta tutkimaan ja löytämään omat vahvuutensa ja oppimisen ilon.

Tehtävänä on toimia varhaiserityiskasvatuksen lastenhoitajana. Tehtävään kuuluu lapsen kehityksen ja oppimisen tukeminen oman tehtäväkuvansa mukaisesti yhteistyössä tiimin varhaiskasvatuksen opettajien ja lastenhoitajan kanssa.

Varhaiserityiskasvatuksen lastenhoitajan kelpoisuusvaatimuksena on varhaiskasvatuslain (540/2018 28§) mukainen kelpoisuus huomioiden varhaiskasvatuslain 540/2018 henkilöstöä koskevan siirtymäsäännöksen (75§) mukaiset hakijat. Sosiaali- ja terveysalan perustutkintoon edellytetään lasten ja nuorten suuntautumisopinnot.

Lisäksi edellytetään kykyä työskennellä tutkimus- ja kehittämisyksikössä oman tehtäväkuvansa mukaisesti. Lisäksi edellytetään motivaatiota ja halua oppia uutta yhdessä monialaisen tiimin kanssa. sekä hyviä tunne- ja vuorovaikutustaitoja. Eduksi luetaan aiempi kokemus varhaiserityiskasvatuksen lastenhoitajan työstä.

Varhaiserityiskasvatuksen lastenhoitajan tehtäväkohtainen palkka muodostuu tasopalkkajärjestelmän sekä osaamisen ja vastuun tasojen mukaisesti 2 512,60 € - 2 625,34 € välille. Varsinainen palkka koostuu tehtäväkohtaisesta palkasta ja mahdollisista muista KVTES:n mukaisista tasolisistä.

Tehtävään valitun on ennen tehtävän vastaanottamista esitettävä nähtäväksi lasten kanssa työskentelevien rikostaustan selvittämisestä annetun lain (504/2002) mukainen rikosrekisteriote. Tartuntatautilain 55 §:n mukaan työnantajan vastuulla on vaatia ennen töiden aloittamista työntekijältä ja harjoittelijalta/opiskelijalta luotettava selvitys siitä, ettei tämä sairasta hengityselinten tuberkuloosia. Selvitys tehdään ennen työsopimuksen tekemistä.

Tehtävässä käytetään koeaikaa.

Tehtävää haetaan ensisijaisesti sähköisellä hakulomakkeella. Mikäli hakemusta ei ole mahdollista jättää sähköisesti, toimita hakemus osoitteeseen Oulun kaupungin kirjaamo, PL 71, 90015 Oulun kaupunki, käyntiosoite Kansankatu 55A. Kirjallisessa hakemuksessa on mainittava tehtäväkohtainen diaarinumero OUKA/14393/2026. Oulun kaupunki ei käytä tekoälyä hakemusten käsittelyssä. Hakijoiden henkilötietoja käsitellään rekrytoinnissa tietosuojalainsäädännön mukaisesti. Julkisena työnantajana hakemusasiakirjojen julkisuus määräytyy viranomaisten toiminnan julkisuudesta annetun lain mukaisesti, ja asiakirjat ovat lähtökohtaisesti julkisia, ellei niiden tai niihin sisältyvien tietojen salassapidosta ole laissa erikseen säädetty. Hakemukseen ei tule sisällyttää sellaisia salassa pidettäviä tai muita henkilötietoja, joita ei ole tarpeen ottaa huomioon valintamenettelyssä. Hakemus on toimitettava 27.10.2026 klo 16.15 mennessä.

description:

title: Grant Controller
description:
YMCA of Greater hartford Job Description


Job Title: Grant Controller

FLSA Status: Exempt Job

Primary Department: Finance

Reports to: Chief Financial Officer

Revision Date: 8/31/2026 Leadership Level: Leader

The YMCA of Greater Hartford is an association open to all committed to helping people reach their potential in spirit, mind, and body. Our commitment is based on the belief that the purpose of this three-fold development is to live out the values of Caring, Honest, Respect and Responsibility.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Grant Controller provides financial leadership and accounting oversight for Greater Hartford YMCA’s portfolio of federal, state, local, foundation, and other restricted grants and contracts. Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer, the position manages the financial lifecycle of grants from proposal development and budget preparation through implementation, accounting, forecasting, financial reporting, compliance, audit support, and closeout. The Grant Controller serves as the primary Finance partner to the Chief Development Officer on grant-related financial matters and works collaboratively with the organizational Controller, Senior Accountant, Program Directors, and program staff.


Location- This position will be split approximately 25% with the Greater Hartford YMCA and 75% with the Waterbury YMCA. The position is expected to be based in Waterbury, with approximately one day per week in Hartford; however, the schedule may vary based on organizational needs.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  1. Collaborate with the Chief Development officer and the Chief Financial Officer on new grant opportunities, renewals, amendments, and funding requests.
  1. Oversee the financial administration of federal, state, local, foundation, and other grant-funded programs.
  2. Establish and maintain grant budgets, financial tracking systems, and internal controls.
  1. Evaluate proposed grants for financial viability, cost recovery, matching requirements, funding restrictions, and potential organizational financial exposure; identify costs that may not be fully reimbursed.
  1. Provide historical financial information, cost analyses, and financial schedules to support grant applications and funding requests in collaboration with the Chief Development Officer and Chief Operations Officer.
  1. Maintain accurate accounting records for assigned grants, contracts, and restricted funding sources and establish appropriate grant, project, cost center, funding source, and reporting structures within the SGA and Daxko Operations.
  1. Prepare grant-related journal entries, accruals, revenue recognition, receivables, deferred revenue, and related accounting entries and reconciliations.
  1. Prepare or oversee reimbursement requests, grant billings, financial drawdowns, and supporting schedules; monitor outstanding grant receivables and coordinate resolution with Finance and Development staff.
  1. Participate in the monthly program financial review process for grant-funded programs in coordination with the Controller and Senior Accountant.
  1. Analyze grant spending relative to the approved budget, available award and percentage of the grant period completed.
  1. Maintain a comprehensive schedule of grant financial reporting requirements, deadlines, funding periods, and fiscal compliance obligations.
  1. Maintain detailed records supporting grant expenditures and ensure documentation is audit-ready.
  1. Support internal, external, and grant-specific audits by providing financial schedules, documentation, and explanations.
  1. Serve as the primary Finance liaison to the Chief Development Officer for grant budgets, cost assumptions, financial information, reporting requirements, and fiscal analysis.
  2. Coordinate with the organizational Controller to ensure grant activity is accurately incorporated into the general ledger, financial statements, organizational budget, forecasts, audit, and internal-control structure.
  1. Maintain confidentiality and safeguard financial and organizational information.



QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • 3–5 years of progressively responsible experience in accounting, grants management, financial management, or a related area.
  • Demonstrated experience managing or monitoring grant-funded budgets.
  • Experience interpreting grant agreements and funding requirements.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.

title: Tool and Die Specialist
description:
Tool & Die Specialist (Stamping Operations)

Join Our High-Performance Stamping Team

Are you a skilled Tool & Die professional who thrives on continuous improvement and precision craftsmanship? We’re looking for a Tool & Die Specialist to join our dynamic stamping team—someone who takes pride in solving complex challenges, optimizing processes, and supporting a culture of excellence.

About the Role

As a Tool & Die Specialist, you will play a critical role in maintaining and improving stamping operations. You’ll collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to troubleshoot issues, refine tooling, and ensure production quality and efficiency.

What You’ll Do

  • Troubleshoot and resolve stamping process issues related to dies, materials, and process controls
  • Set up and adjust equipment, including machine parameters, to ensure optimal performance
  • Perform bench work such as deburring, polishing, and finishing tooling components
  • Repair and modify dies using lathes, milling machines, grinders, and hand tools
  • Manufacture, modify, and repair replacement tooling and machine parts as needed
  • Prepare dies and equipment for production runs and validate tool readiness
  • Conduct preventative maintenance (PM) and complete detailed bench work
  • Analyze and communicate quality and tool performance data
  • Interpret and verify blueprints, dimensions, and tolerances using precision instruments
  • Operate power presses and hydraulic test equipment to support production when required
  • Complete work orders and documentation in CMMS systems
  • Overhaul tooling according to Bill of Materials specifications
  • Mentor apprentices and support ongoing development of team members
  • Communicate status updates, challenges, and solutions effectively across teams

What You Bring

Education

  • High school diploma or GED (required)
  • Associate degree in metalworking or related field (preferred)
  • Completion of a DOL-approved apprenticeship program in metalworking (preferred)
    Equivalent experience will be considered

Experience

  • Minimum 2 years of experience in a medium-sized industrial or manufacturing environment

Technical Expertise

  • Hands-on experience with:
    • Transfer and progressive dies
    • Stamping presses, coil lines, decoilers, feeders, and straighteners
    • Precision machining tools (lathes, mills, surface grinders)
  • Strong understanding of:
    • Metallurgy, material dynamics, and coatings
    • Blueprint reading and technical drawings
    • Quality control, production processes, and cost optimization
    • Mathematics including algebra, geometry, and basic statistics

Key Skills & Attributes

  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities
  • Effective communication—both verbal and written
  • Ability to manage time, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines
  • Collaborative mindset and ability to build strong working relationships
  • Proficiency with basic software tools (Word, Excel, Outlook) and systems such as CMMS or SAP
  • Comfort operating forklifts (stand-up and sit-down)
  • Continuous improvement mindset with a focus on production excellence

Work Environment & Schedule

  • Rotating 3-shift schedule with flexibility to adjust hours as needed (including weekends)
  • Overtime may be required to support operational needs
  • Occasional travel (U.S. and international) may be required
  • Opportunity to work hands-on in both maintenance and production support roles

Why Join Us?

  • Be part of a collaborative, high-performing team
  • Work with advanced equipment and tooling technologies
  • Opportunities for skill development and career growth
  • Make a direct impact on production quality and efficiency


Benefits

Blum USA believes in offering their employees an excellent benefits package that includes:

  • Possible bonus opportunities
  • Hourly Position
  • Health (Medical, dental and vision) & wellness benefit
  • 401(k) with employee matching
  • FSA & Dependent Care
  • Gym and Whitewater Center Reimbursements
  • Three weeks’ vacation starting your second year on the job
  • Paid sick leave (48 hours annually)
  • Life insurance equal to annual salary at no cost to employee
  • Onsite Health clinic


Company Overview

For over 60 years, Blum has been a global leader in manufacturing high-quality hinge systems, drawer runners, and lift systems that enhance user convenience in kitchens and living spaces. Our commitment to innovation and motion perfection drives everything we do.

With eight production plants in Austria and manufacturing sites in Brazil, Poland, China and the United States, Blum employs approximately 9,000 people worldwide. Our mission is to create solutions that make everyday life easier—whether in the kitchen or beyond.
