title: ELECTRICAL HAZARDS TRAINING SPECIALIST / PROGRAM COORDINATOR
description:
Electrical Hazards Training Specialist / Program Coordinator

The Townsend Company, LLC

Location: Muncie, IN | Nationwide Travel Required

Position Type: Full-Time

Travel Requirement: Approximately 75% nationwide, including frequent overnight travel

Help Shape the Future of Electrical Safety Training!

Are you an experienced utility professional with a passion for safety, training, and developing others? Do you enjoy delivering hands-on instruction, working with field teams, and making a meaningful impact on workplace safety?

The Townsend Company, LLC is seeking an Electrical Hazards Training Specialist / Program Coordinator to lead and coordinate our Electrical Hazards Training (EHT) Trailer Program.

This is more than a traditional training position. You will serve as a key resource in delivering electrical hazards education across our operations, combining technical expertise, engaging instruction, and program coordination to help employees recognize hazards and work safely around electrical infrastructure.

From conducting live demonstrations to managing a mobile training program that travels throughout the country, you will play an important role in strengthening our safety culture and supporting the employees who work in some of the industry's most demanding environments.

If you have a strong background in utility operations or line clearance, enjoy teaching others, and are ready to take ownership of a critical safety training initiative, we want to hear from you!

Who We Are

The Townsend Company, LLC is an industry leader in utility vegetation management and right-of-way services, supporting electric utilities and critical infrastructure across the United States.

Headquartered in Muncie, Indiana, Townsend operates across multiple states, providing vegetation management, power line clearance, utility line construction, storm response, and other specialized services.

With a strong commitment to safety, operational excellence, and quality service, Townsend works to protect and maintain critical utility infrastructure while providing rewarding career opportunities and professional growth for our employees.

What We Offer

  • Weekly pay

  • Paid time off

  • Health benefits

  • 401(k) with up to a 4% company match

  • Opportunities for professional growth and development

  • The opportunity to make a direct impact on employee safety across our nationwide operations

What You'll Do

As our Electrical Hazards Training Specialist / Program Coordinator, you will oversee the delivery, coordination, and continuous improvement of our Electrical Hazards Training Trailer Program.

Your responsibilities will include:

Lead Engaging Safety Training

  • Deliver classroom instruction and live electrical hazards demonstrations to employees across company operations.

  • Educate field teams on electrical hazard recognition, safe work practices, and applicable safety standards.

  • Create an engaging, hands-on learning environment that encourages participation and knowledge retention.

  • Evaluate employee understanding and provide coaching to reinforce safe work practices.

  • Support the development and qualification of additional electrical hazards training demonstrators.

Coordinate a Nationwide Training Program

  • Manage the scheduling and coordination of the Electrical Hazards Training Trailer across company locations.

  • Partner with Operations, Safety, Fleet, and regional leadership to plan training events.

  • Coordinate transportation, travel logistics, and equipment readiness for scheduled training.

  • Maintain training calendars, attendance records, certifications, and required documentation.

  • Support Train-the-Trainer initiatives and instructor evaluations.

Maintain Equipment and Training Readiness

  • Conduct inspections of the training trailer and demonstration equipment before and after training sessions.

  • Coordinate equipment maintenance, repairs, testing, and required inspections.

  • Maintain inventory of electrical protective equipment, demonstration materials, and training supplies.

  • Ensure the trailer, electrical systems, PPE, and training equipment remain in safe operating condition.

  • Work with internal teams to resolve equipment concerns and maintain program readiness.

Champion Safety and Continuous Improvement

  • Ensure demonstrations are conducted in accordance with company procedures and applicable OSHA and ANSI requirements.

  • Lead pre-demonstration safety briefings and verify protective systems before operating equipment.

  • Identify potential safety concerns and take appropriate corrective action.

  • Review training feedback and recommend improvements to program content and delivery.

  • Update training materials to reflect evolving industry standards, operational needs, and best practices.

  • Support broader corporate safety initiatives and employee development efforts.

What We're Looking For

We are looking for a safety-focused professional who brings strong technical knowledge, excellent communication skills, and the ability to independently coordinate a nationwide training program.

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent.

  • Minimum of five (5) years of experience in utility vegetation management, electric utility operations, line clearance arboriculture, or a related industry.

  • Experience delivering classroom and field-based training.

  • Strong understanding of electrical hazards and safe work practices within utility environments.

  • Excellent presentation, communication, and public speaking skills.

  • Strong organizational, scheduling, and program coordination abilities.

  • Ability to work independently while collaborating with operational and safety leadership.

  • Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record and ability to meet company driver qualification requirements.

  • Ability and willingness to travel approximately 75% throughout the United States, including frequent overnight stays.

Preferred Qualifications

Candidates with any of the following qualifications are especially encouraged to apply:

  • Associate's or bachelor's degree in Safety, Utility Operations, Education, or a related field.

  • ISA Certified Arborist

  • Certified Treecare Safety Professional (CTSP)

  • Certified Utility Safety Specialist (CUSP)

  • OSHA Outreach Trainer certification

  • Utility line clearance or electrical utility experience

  • Experience with high-voltage training or demonstration equipment

  • Experience managing mobile training programs

  • Background in adult learning, instructional design, or technical training development

Work Environment & Travel Expectations

This position supports Townsend operations nationwide and requires a combination of classroom instruction, field-based training, and hands-on equipment demonstrations.

Approximately 75% nationwide travel is required, including frequent overnight stays. Training will primarily take place at field locations, regional operating facilities, training centers, and other company locations.

Candidates should be comfortable with:

  • Working indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions.

  • Standing, walking, bending, and climbing during training activities.

  • Lifting and carrying equipment weighing up to 50 pounds.

  • Setting up and dismantling training equipment.

  • Wearing required personal protective equipment.

  • Working independently while traveling between training locations.

Why Join Townsend?

At Townsend, safety is more than a priority. It is a responsibility we share across every level of our organization.

In this role, your work will directly influence how employees recognize electrical hazards, respond to potential risks, and protect themselves and their coworkers in the field.

You will have the opportunity to share your expertise, work with teams across the country, contribute to the development of safety training programs, and help strengthen a culture where every employee has the knowledge and tools to work safely.

Ready to Make an Impact?

If you're passionate about electrical safety, enjoy developing others, and are ready for a role that combines technical training, program leadership, and nationwide field engagement, we encourage you to apply.

Join The Townsend Company, LLC and help us build a safer, stronger workforce.

The Townsend Company, LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to qualified applicants without regard to any status protected by applicable law.

title: CSV Engineer
description:
About Company:

JC Automation Corp. (JCA) was founded in 1997 with the mission of filling a gap between technology and regulatory requirements in the life science manufacturing industry. The company offers highly capable resources at an affordable cost to build solutions and execute projects in: Automation, Control Systems Integration, Information Technology, System Integration and Regulatory Compliance.

JCA is a HUBZone Certified Small Business Firm, NMSDC Certified Minority Business Enterprise, and Certified Critical Industry Supplier. It’s mission is to add value by delivering quality services & solutions on time all the time by transforming processes & technology into business advantages.

ABOUT THE ROLE

A Computer System Validation (CSV) Engineer is responsible for ensuring that computerized systems used in regulated environments are properly validated and maintained in compliance with applicable regulatory and quality requirements. They support the complete system lifecycle, including requirements definition, risk assessment, validation planning, testing, implementation, and periodic review.


Focus: Focuses on the validation and lifecycle management of computerized systems to ensure data integrity, regulatory compliance, system reliability, and continued validated state. Emphasizes documentation, risk-based validation, testing, and compliance with pharmaceutical industry standards.


RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Develop and execute computer system validation documentation, including Validation Plans, User Requirements Specifications (URS), Functional/Design Specifications, IQ/OQ/PQ protocols, Traceability Matrices, and Validation Summary Reports.

2. Perform risk assessments to determine validation requirements and testing strategies.

3. Review and approve system requirements, specifications, and configuration documentation.

4. Execute and document validation testing and manage identified discrepancies or deviations.

5. Support system implementation, upgrades, changes, patches, and periodic reviews while maintaining the validated state.

6. Ensure computerized systems comply with applicable data integrity and electronic records/electronic signature requirements.

7. Support Change Controls, Deviations, CAPAs, and investigations related to computerized systems.

8. Collaborate with Quality, Automation, IT, Engineering, and system owners throughout the system lifecycle.

9. Support regulatory inspections and internal or external audits.

.

REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS

Required

1. Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Life Sciences, or related field.

2. Experience with Computer System Validation in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or other regulated industries.

3. Knowledge of GxP requirements and computerized system lifecycle principles.

4. Familiarity with 21 CFR Part 11, data integrity principles, and applicable regulatory guidance.

5. Ability to develop, review, and execute validation protocols and technical documentation.

6. Knowledge of risk-based validation methodologies.

7. Strong technical writing, analytical, documentation, and problem-solving skills.

8. Ability to work independently and collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams.


Preferred

1. Knowledge of GAMP 5 methodology and risk-based Computer System Assurance/Validation approaches.

2. Experience with PLC, SCADA, HMI, DCS, MES, LIMS, ERP, historians, or manufacturing computerized systems.

3. Experience with electronic validation/documentation platforms such as Kneat or similar systems.

4. Familiarity with ALCOA+ and data integrity requirements.

5. Experience supporting regulatory inspections or audits.

6. Knowledge of change control, deviation, CAPA, and quality management processes.

title: Mariposa Transportation Service Clerk 1st Shift

title: Outreach Specialist (Metro)
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The Outreach Specialist conducts outreach and housing navigation activities to individuals experiencing homelessness. The Outreach Specialist assists individuals with collecting documents necessary for housing, and provides linkage to ongoing supportive services. The Outreach Specialist will address the individuals’ immediate needs and work to engage them in services using best practice standards. The Outreach Specialist is the primary point of contact for individuals and provides screening, triage, crisis intervention, access to interim housing, and transportation services, with the goal of assisting individuals experiencing homelessness with moving into permanent housing.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS INCLUDE, but are not limited to the following:

  • Conducts outreach activities to engage individuals experiencing homelessness and support them in pursuing permanent housing options.
  • Receives, assesses and triages referrals from collaborative partners.
  • Conducts standardized screening and triages individuals experiencing homelessness.
  • Provides an appropriate level of services and interventions utilizing best practices and service models to meet the individual needs of each participant.
  • Assists individuals with collecting documents necessary for applying for permanent supportive housing.
  • Connects individuals to supportive services including: mental health, medical care, substance abuse, employment, etc as needed.
  • Provides linkage to mainstream resources, such as DPSS or Social Security Disability.
  • Provides transportation assistance.
  • Assists individuals with accessing permanent housing opportunities including permanent supportive housing, move-in assistance, shared housing, affordable housing, etc.
  • Conducts follow-up activities to ensure completion of the housing plan.
  • Documents services and completes data entry into HMIS database within timeframes outlined by funder and agency.
  • Attends case conferencing meetings to coordinate services with other providers.
  • Attends clinical consultation, individual supervision, team meetings, and trainings as required by the funder and agency.
  • Other duties as assigned.

PHYSICAL AND MENTAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT:

  • Frequently exposed to outdoor weather and driving conditions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.
  • Stand and sit for long periods of time; move and walk to various locations; climb stairs, stoop, kneel, reach, pull, push, bend, twist, and occasionally lift and or move objects. Use hands to finger, handle or feel.
  • See, hear and speak clearly in order to give and receive information and instructions.
  • Ability to interact with other employees, clients, customers and members of the public.
  • Ability to work effectively under time constraints, prioritize work, multi-task, and adapt to changing work demands.
  • Gather, analyze, synthesize, and classify information. Transcribe, enter, and post data.
  • Ability to respond effectively to sensitive inquiries or complaints.
  • Requires use of a computer keyboard.
  • Travel to off-site meetings.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Knowledge of transitional and permanent housing resources throughout Los Angeles County.
  • Knowledge of housing issues in San Gabriel Valley preferred.
  • Knowledge of HUD guidelines and experience working with subsidized housing programs such as Section 8, Shelter Plus Care and others.
  • Current knowledge of interventions, models and principles related to best practice standards.
  • Ability to communicate effectively both verbally and in writing.
  • Proficient in use of laptop computer and Microsoft Windows and Office software programs (Word, Access, Excel, PowerPoint, G-Mail).
  • Ability to accurately enter client data and notes in HMIS Homeless Management Information System.
  • Proficient with office communication equipment and machines (telephone, copier, calculator, fax machine, personal computer, laptop, computer printer and scanner).
  • Possess valid California driver's license and have access to properly registered vehicle.

EDUCATION, TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in human services or similar field preferred.
  • 1 year of experience working with homeless individuals in an outreach/navigation capacity or case management experience.
  • Successful demonstration of required skills through current or past USHS employment may be considered in lieu of the standard required years of experience.

Head of Global Cybersecurity Operations, HSBC

Cyber Security Engineer - Governance Risk & Compliance (GRC) - UK Remote

Immersive is hiring! Could you be our next Cyber Security Engineer?

Due to customer demand and increasing maturity within our platform we have an exciting and challenging opportunity for an experienced cyber professional within the cyber compliance sector - with expertise in conducting governance risk and compliance audits - to join our Product team as Cyber Security Engineer, specialising in Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC).

If successful you will join our Product team working closely with our Cyber Team Leads as we embark on this exciting new phase of product development within our market leading cyber resilience platform.

This isn’t an ordinary GRC role - we know everyone claims this and will tell you their role is super unique…but this one really is.

You are constantly researching, learning, totally geeking out on all things GRC related, from ISO standards, to the latest AI governance, and then taking that knowledge and creating labs and ranges.

You will be a key player in our Cyber team, shaping and influencing the roll out of our offensive security and AI pen test content roadmap, simulating attack paths and helping train our users to counter the latest threats.

You will be educating the world of GRC professionals on how to make sure they are secure in what they do. Now that is a pretty cool legacy to leave behind.

Your mission (if you choose to accept it) is to evolve and disrupt within the governance space by creating emulated environments within our platform that will simulate incidents within highly regulated sectors in an engaging and intuitive way for our community.

You will design, build and deliver practical and theory content to gamify governance, risk and compliance and make it engaging and fun for the end user. You'll shake up traditional training and teach complex concepts in an innovative way.

If you have a passion for cyber security, are experienced in the area of GRC, and want to disrupt how employees build their resilience against the latest threats we will appreciate your input and give you the space to innovate within our market leading platform, Immersive One.

Your main responsibilities (we're scaling fast, so these may change as we grow):

  • Utilising knowledge of Governance, Risk & Compliance to plan, write and improve our security labs, challenges and online learning content on the Immersive One platform.

  • Produce multi-format content utilising various teaching methods; practical exercises, questions & gamification around GRC

  • Peer review cyber labs and ranges to ensure they function as expected

  • Research the latest GRC regulations and standard and compile this research to deliver practical and theory labs to users

  • Compile technical research into understandable concise content for both technical and non-technical audience

  • Act as a GRC subject matter expert for our engineering and product teams, embedding "security and privacy by design" principles into the SDLC

Sounds good? We’d love to hear from you if you have proven experience in the following areas:

  • A number of years of experience working within a heavily regulated industry (e.g., FinTech, Healthcare, or Government), cyber vendor or consultancy. You will have conducted audits and have an understanding of how GRC works in practice and helping companies to comply to these standard

  • In-depth knowledge of the MITRE ATLAS & D3FEND frameworks and how it is used to help enterprises deal with threats to their organisation.

  • Deep understanding of common compliance frameworks and security standards (e.g., NIST SP 800-53, NIST CSF, ISO 27001/27002, SOC 2).

  • Have a strong technical understanding of networking, computing and cyber security concepts

  • Have the ability to use examples and analogies to simplify complex subjects - your content will train real world users to identify and combat the latest threats so you need to be able to inhabit the mindset of your target audience to create realistic simulations

  • Certifications such as CISSP, CISA, CRISC, CISM would be useful to have but not essential

  • Attitude and approach is just as important as technical skills for this role - you will be someone who enjoys tackling complex problems and finding the solution. You'll be a natural problem solver and 'tinkerer' who enjoys prototyping and iteration.

Immersive’s growth has been fuelled by our values that underpin everything we do, here's how they relate to this role:

We exceed our customers and partners' expectations by crafting products, services and experiences that surprise, delight and ensure they feel valued and supported every day.

  • One Team - We are a talented global team working together to achieve our vision. Central to our ethos, resilience means adapting and thriving in adversity. It guides our innovation, ensuring we and our clients are prepared for the future.

We encourage people of all different backgrounds and identities to apply. We are committed to maintaining an inclusive, supportive place for you to be you and do your very best work. Excited by the above? We’re ready to receive your application!


As well as an inclusive, supportive place for you to be you. We offer an extensive range of benefits so you can do your very best work:

  • Career and learning development through the platform, a dedicated professional development fund and our ‘Learn Anything’ fund - which enables you to learn anything that’s not work!

  • We have a vibrant team culture with team events throughout the year. Our socials have included everything from pottery painting and paper mask making, to dungeons and dragons!

  • When you do visit the UK hub, getting there is easy: we’re based in the centre of Bristol, just a 10 minute walk from the train station. We also offer railcard loan and cycle scheme to buy a new bike

title: Substance Use Specialist
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The Substance Abuse Specialist conducts outreach and housing navigation activities with a focus on chronically homeless and highly vulnerable individuals. The Substance Use Specialist is a member of an interdisciplinary team that will provide services to individuals experiencing homelessness. The Substance Abuse Specialist will provide substance abuse counseling services and interventions within their scope of practice.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS INCLUDE, but are not limited to the following:

  • Participate in a rotation with other specialty roles to ensure support to all outreach teams and individuals being served.
  • Use evidence based practices to assess, provide interventions, and establish linkages to substance use disorder treatment programs and other services/programs as needed.
  • Conducts outreach activities to engage chronically homeless individuals toward pursuing permanent housing options.
  • Receives, assesses and triages referrals from walk-ins and other collaborative partners.
  • Conducts standardized screening and triages chronically homeless individuals.
  • Support clients and staff in navigation and linkage to substance use disorder treatment programs. Assists individuals with collecting documents necessary for applying for permanent supportive housing.
  • Attends case conferencing meetings to coordinate services with other providers. Provides substance abuse counseling and linkage to related resources if indicated, using a harm reduction philosophy as basis for interventions
  • Connects individuals to other supportive services as needed such as mental health, health, substance abuse, legal, employment, etc.
  • Document services and complete data entry into HMIS database.
  • Provide linkage to mainstream resources, such as DPSS or Social Security Disability.
  • Provide transportation assistance for the purposes of stabilizing the current housing crisis.
  • Conduct follow-up activities to ensure completion of the crisis housing plan.
  • Identify appropriate interventions to address and resolve the homeless status of program participants.
  • Assists individuals with accessing permanent housing opportunities including permanent supportive housing, move-in assistance, shared housing, affordable housing, etc.
  • Other duties as assigned.

PHYSICAL AND MENTAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT:

  • Work indoors in temperature controlled environment and occasionally exposed to outdoor weather and driving conditions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.
  • Stand and sit for long periods of time; move and walk to various locations; climb stairs, stoop, kneel, reach, pull, push, bend, twist, and occasionally lift and or move objects. Use hands to finger, handle or feel.
  • See, hear and speak clearly in order to give and receive information and instructions.
  • Ability to interact with other employees, clients, customers and members of the public.
  • Ability to work effectively under time constraints, prioritize work, multi-task, and adapt to changing work demands.
  • Gather, analyze, synthesize, and classify information. Transcribe, enter, and post data.
  • Ability to respond effectively to sensitive inquiries or complaints.
  • Requires use of a computer keyboard.
  • Travel to off-site meetings.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Knowledge of emergency housing, transitional and permanent housing resources throughout Los Angeles County.
  • Knowledge of housing issues in San Gabriel Valley preferred.
  • Knowledge of HUD guidelines and experience working with subsidized housing programs such as Section 8, Shelter Plus Care and others.
  • Current knowledge of social work practices and principles related to best practice standards.
  • Ability to communicate effectively both verbally and in writing.
  • Proficient in use of laptop computer and Microsoft Windows and Office software programs (Word, Access, Excel, PowerPoint, G-Mail).
  • Ability to accurately enter client data and notes in HMIS Homeless Management Information System.
  • Proficient with office communication equipment and machines (telephone, copier, calculator, fax machine, personal computer, computer printer and scanner).
  • Possess valid California driver's license and have access to properly registered vehicle.
  • Bilingual Spanish preferred.

EDUCATION, TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE:

Minimum Qualifications

  • Option I: Bachelor’s Degree in human services or similar field (i.e. psychology, sociology, social work)
  • Option II:1-year full-time experience involving counseling or substance abuse counseling.
  • Option III: 1 year of experience with case management service to individuals with substance abuse disorders.

Desirable

  • Professional substance abuse counseling certification, i.e. CADAC preferred.

Union Station Homeless Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer

  • Responsible for the optimization of all Quality processes.

  • Complete inspections according to the quality management system / control plans /agreements with customers
  • Review schedules, production orders to make decisions concerning inventory requirements, staffing requirements, work procedures, and duty assignments.
  • Work with Human Resources to hire, train, evaluate, coach, resolve employee concerns, and process terminations.
  • Prepare and maintain detailed reports for proper action and recording.
  • Assist in developing and implementing production tracking and quality control systems, analyzing production, quality control, maintenance, and other operational reports, to detect production problems.
  • Oversee the performance of layered audits and quality checks as needed throughout the entire cycle of the seat process and all the included parts.
  • Review parts and make determinations if they pass/fail the quality standards
  • Assist in the set-up and calibration of gauging and measuring devices; train Team Members on using gauges and measuring devices

  • Updates job knowledge by participating in educational opportunities; reading technical publications.

  3. Communication: Works to ensure respectful, timely, accurate and appropriate communication across all levels of the organization.
  4. Initiative: Identifies problems and takes action to address current or future problems. Proactively engages to solve issues verses simply thinking about future actions.
  5. Engagement: Engages team members in developing goals, executing plans and delivering results (output). Motivates team members through clear and consistent communication. Models adaptability. Uses collaboration and influence skills to achieve successful outcomes.

Systematically organizes the parts of problems. Makes systematic comparisons of data or aspects, prioritizing, planning, and developing countermeasures.

title: Mining Technician – Drilling and Blasting
description:
About the role

Reporting to the Mine Engineering Supervisor, the incumbent is responsible for designing production stopes related to long-hole drilling and blasting activities. The role also involves conducting field follow-ups, preparing layouts and plans, compiling data, and contributing to operational decision-making.

Essential Duties

Monitor various work areas with respect to drilling and blasting activities.
Design drilling patterns and blasting sequences for production stopes.
Prepare drilling, blasting, and mucking plans, as well as specifications for barricades and access restriction systems.
Ensure drilling and blasting best practices are followed to control dilution and maximize ore recovery. Conduct dilution and recovery analyses for production stopes.
Perform field quality control inspections of drilling operations and analyze drill-hole deviations.
Comply with, understand, and promote company regulations and policies, particularly those related to health and safety.
Perform all other duties related to the position.

Training & Experience

College diploma (DEC) in Mining Operations or Mineral Technology.
Minimum of five (5) years of relevant experience in an underground mining environment.
Practical experience in drilling and blasting is considered an asset.
Completion of Mining Modules 1 to 5 and 7.
Valid General Explosives Permit.
Strong computer skills, including proficiency with Deswik and the Microsoft Office Suite.
Bilingualism (English and French) is considered an asset.

Skills and Competencies

Teamwork in a multicultural environment.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent organizational skills.
Adaptability and flexibility.

Working Conditions

Eleonore mine site (fly-in, fly-out from Montreal, Chibougamau, Matagami, Rouyn-Noranda, Val D'Or and Wemindji)
Schedule: 14 working days followed by 14 days off

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
Senior Product Designer at Beyond Sports

Join Our Team as a Senior Product Designer at Beyond Sports!

Are you passionate about complex product systems, pixel-perfect UI, and leading the design of next-generation digital experiences that capture global audiences?

At Beyond Sports, we don’t just visualize sports, we reinvent how fans experience them. Together with partners like NFL, NHL, FIFA, and Disney, we push the boundaries of real-time sports data, 3D graphics, and AI-driven storytelling across web and native mobile platforms.

If you're an experienced Senior Product Designer with an exceptional visual craft, deep UX strategy expertise, and a desire to lead impactful product initiatives within a fast-moving design and engineering team, this is the perfect next step in your career.



What Your Day Will Look Like

As a Senior Product Designer, you'll play a pivotal role in shaping how some of the most followed clubs and organizations in world sport engage and inspire millions of fans.

Working alongside Lead Designers, Product Managers, and cross-functional delivery squads, you'll take end-to-end ownership of UI and UX solutions for major client initiatives across web and native mobile apps (iOS and Android).

One day you might be architecting complex user journeys and wireframing new live match data features. The next, you could be setting component-driven design system standards in Figma, presenting design rationales to client stakeholders, or mentoring midweight designers within your squad.

You'll serve as a key design lead within delivery teams, driving creative quality, technical feasibility, and seamless developer handoff. Because we thrive on continuous improvement and collaboration, your work will directly define how millions of sports fans interact with digital touchpoints worldwide.



What We Value

At Beyond Sports, we move fast, collaborate closely, and build things that haven't existed before.

You'll fit right in if you:

  • Bring high-level design craft, producing scalable UI architectures and seamless UX workflows

  • Take full end-to-end ownership of project workstreams from discovery through design implementation

  • Drive clarity through exceptional verbal and visual communication skills

  • Confidently lead client discussions, articulate design decisions, and align multi-disciplinary teams

  • Excel at managing your own deliverables, prioritizing high-impact work within active sprint cycles

  • Champion continuous design quality and offer constructive feedback to elevate the wider design team

  • Drive strong, proactive collaboration across creative, product, engineering, and data teams


Your Background

You don't need to tick every box, but we're generally looking for:

  • Minimum 5+ years of commercial product design experience (agency, high-growth tech, or digital sports media)

  • A standout portfolio demonstrating complex end-to-end product design, scalable systems, and polished UI/UX for iOS, Android, and responsive web

  • Advanced mastery of Figma, including advanced prototyping, tokenized component libraries, and design system governance

  • Deep expertise in user-centered design methodologies, information architecture, and responsive design frameworks

  • Proven experience working directly with engineering squads to guide successful design handoff and QA implementation

  • Methodical approach to work management with high attention to detail and quality control

  • Comfortable leading design initiatives and collaborating in an English-speaking environment

Nice to Have (But Not Required)

  • Deep domain knowledge of world sports, live match platforms, sports betting, or real-time data visualization

  • Experience designing for rich media platforms, 3D/interactive graphics, or streaming interfaces

  • Familiarity with design tokens, CSS/component frameworks, or native mobile HIG and Material Design guidelines


Why Level Up Your Career at Beyond Sports

Fast-moving, creative, and innovative — that's our world.

  • High Impact: Your work directly shapes how millions of sports fans interact with digital platforms globally

  • Creative Leadership: Drive key product features autonomously while mentoring midweight designers and setting visual standards

  • Product Variety: Lead design efforts across responsive web, iOS, Android, and emerging digital sports touchpoints

  • Growth Culture: Continuous feedback loops and clear paths for career progression into Lead or Principal roles

  • Real Collaboration: Partner directly with senior product leaders, specialized engineers, and sports domain experts

And we make sure it’s a great place to work:

  • 25 days of paid leave per year

  • Pension program

  • Lunch included

  • Gym card

  • Fresh fruit, great coffee, and Friday drinks

  • Bi-monthly team outings

  • Office games like FIFA, chess, and ping-pong

  • Sony Benefits and much more!

Ready to Bring the Beyond Sports Brand to Life?

If you're excited about building cutting-edge product experiences, leading impactful design initiatives, and contributing to a brand that's helping redefine sports entertainment, we'd love to hear from you.

At Beyond Sports, you won't just design interfaces. You'll help bring sports to life.

title: GLOBAL SOURCING SPECIALIST
description:
Global Sourcing Specialist

Indianapolis, IN or Batesville, IN (Hybrid) | Full-Time, Monday–Friday

About Wood-Mizer

Wood-Mizer is the world's largest manufacturer of portable sawmills, with more than 100,000 mills sold in over 100 countries. We build a complete line of sawmilling, wood processing, and blade equipment for forestry and timber professionals. We're 100% employee-owned, so every team member has a stake in our success, and we put our people and customers at the center of everything we do.

Position Summary

The Global Sourcing Specialist develops and executes sourcing strategies that expand Wood-Mizer's global supply base into lower-cost producing countries, including China, India, greater Asia Pacific, Latin America, and Eastern Europe. The role is accountable for cost reduction and cost avoidance across assigned commodities, qualifying new suppliers, and leading cross-functional cost optimization projects with Engineering, Manufacturing, Procurement, and Finance. This work turns market and commodity trends into pricing forecasts and negotiation strategies that lower product cost and protect supply continuity. This hybrid role travels up to 40%, domestically and internationally. It has no direct reports at the start, with the potential to build a sourcing team over time.

Essential Functions

  • Develops and executes strategic sourcing plans that expand the supply base into China, India, Asia Pacific, Latin America, and other qualified lower-cost countries.
  • Identifies, evaluates, and qualifies new suppliers through capability assessments, on-site audits, and risk evaluations before onboarding.
  • Manages supplier relationships for assigned commodities through performance scorecards, business reviews, and continuous improvement plans, and partners with Quality on supplier corrective actions and periodic audits.
  • Leads cost reduction and cost avoidance initiatives, building should-cost and total-cost-of-ownership (TCO) models and tracking savings in Infor Syteline, Wrike, and Qlik to meet annual savings targets.
  • Monitors global market trends, commodity indexes, currency exposure, and supply risk, and develops forecasts and pricing-impact projections for leadership.
  • Negotiates, drafts, and manages supplier contracts through their lifecycle to secure favorable terms, supply continuity, and compliance with corporate policy.
  • Leads sourcing for new product development, engineering changes, and product cost-outs in close collaboration with Engineering and Manufacturing.
  • Develops dual-sourcing and supply risk mitigation plans for critical components.
  • Plans and procures material for assigned commodities, balancing cost, lead time, inventory, and supply risk.
  • Ensures sourcing decisions and supplier agreements comply with trade regulations (tariffs, duties, Incoterms), corporate compliance requirements, and ethical sourcing standards.
  • Follows all Wood-Mizer safety, quality, and company policies and procedures.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
  • 4+ years of progressive experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, or supply chain management
  • Hands-on international sourcing and supplier relationship management experience, with a focus on China, Asia Pacific, Latin America, India, and other lower-cost regions
  • Proven record of leading cost reduction and cost avoidance initiatives with measurable, documented savings
  • Experience leading supplier identification, qualification, and onboarding in a manufacturing environment
  • Strong contract negotiation, drafting, and vendor management skills
  • Working knowledge of Incoterms, import/export compliance, tariffs, and international logistics
  • Proficiency with ERP/MRP systems (Infor Syteline or comparable) and Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook)
  • Strong analytical skills, including building cost models and turning commodity and market data into actionable forecasts
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior leadership
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to 40%

Preferred

  • CPSM, CPIM, CSCP, or C.P.M. certification
  • Experience sourcing mechanical, metal fabrication, casting, electronics, or engineered components in a manufacturing or industrial equipment environment
  • Ability to read engineering drawings, product prints, and specifications to evaluate supplier capability, support quoting, and identify cost-reduction opportunities
  • Working knowledge of manufacturing processes such as machining, fabrication, casting, welding, and sheet metal
  • Familiarity with Lean/Six Sigma and continuous improvement tools
  • Experience with Wrike, Qlik, or similar project management and business intelligence platforms
  • Mandarin, Spanish, or Portuguese language skills

Physical Requirements & Work Environment

The physical demands below describe the job as it is performed, with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Frequently sit and work at a computer for extended periods
  • Travel by air and ground, domestically and internationally, up to 40% of the time
  • Periodically walk and stand on manufacturing floors during supplier and plant visits

Work environment: Office/hybrid, with periodic time in manufacturing areas at supplier and Wood-Mizer sites.

Required PPE: Standard PPE when on manufacturing sites

What We Offer

  • Employee Ownership – Become a true owner through our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) and share directly in Wood-Mizer's growth and success.
  • Retirement Savings – Save for retirement in our 401(k), with a company match contributed to your ESOP account.
  • Performance Incentives – Earn extra rewards tied to your contributions and results.
  • Flexible Pay Options – Choose from multiple pay methods, including Wages On-Demand, which lets you access earned wages daily.
  • PTO Accrual Starts Day One – Start earning paid time off with your first paycheck, plus paid holidays and additional leave for life events such as marriage, birth, or adoption.
  • Free Health Clinic Access – When enrolled in our medical plan, get free care through Marathon Health, with near-site clinics in Indianapolis, IN and Cincinnati, OH and many services available virtually wherever you live.
  • Comprehensive Insurance – Health, dental, vision, and company-paid life insurance, plus supplemental coverage and short- and long-term disability options.
  • Community Impact – Take part in our Workplace Giving Programs and be recognized for serving others through donations and volunteer work.
  • Education Assistance – Use tuition reimbursement to reach your long-term career and learning goals.
  • Annual Allowances – Reimbursement for safety boots and glasses, plus yearly funds for Wood-Mizer apparel and gear.
  • Everyday Perks – Company events and outings, free coffee and fruit, birthday and anniversary gift cards, referral bonuses, discounted shipping, and more.

Benefits eligibility varies by position and employment status.

If you want a career, not just a job, apply today and see how Wood-Mizer employee-owners are making a difference around the world and right here in Indianapolis and Batesville, IN.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Wood-Mizer is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. We make employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. This applies to all aspects of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, compensation, training, transfers, leaves of absence, and terminations.

Accommodations

Interview Process & Communications

As part of our hiring process, Wood-Mizer may use on-demand phone, video, and AI-enabled interviewing tools. These tools support our team; people make all hiring decisions. Candidates may opt in to receive text messages about their application. Message frequency varies, and standard message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out or HELP for assistance. title: Sub-Investigator (Part-Time)
description:
About Us

At Empathx, we drive equitable access to complex trials at any phase by providing industry-leading patient access, clinical trial management, and analysis across cardiology, psychiatry/neurology, metabolic, and infectious disease studies throughout the therapeutic pipeline.

This is an on-site, part-time position at our Dallas, TX location. The schedule is 3–4 days per week, for a total of 20–24 hours per week. Specific days and hours will be set with the site based on study visit needs.

Position Summary: The Sub-Investigator provides medical oversight for clinical trials under the direction of the Principal Investigator, with a focus on psychiatry/CNS studies across Phases I–IV. This role assesses participant eligibility and safety, performs protocol-required clinical assessments, and ensures studies are conducted in compliance with the protocol, ICH-GCP, and FDA regulations.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Study Oversight & Participant Safety

  • Conduct clinical trials under the direction and delegation of the Principal Investigator in accordance with the protocol, ICH-GCP, FDA regulations (21 CFR Parts 50, 54, 56, and 312), IRB requirements, and company SOPs
  • Provide medical oversight across a portfolio of five or more concurrent studies, Phases I–IV, with a focus on psychiatry/CNS indications
  • Assess participant eligibility by reviewing medical and psychiatric history, concomitant medications, and inclusion/exclusion criteria prior to enrollment and randomization
  • Conduct and document the informed consent process, ensuring participants understand study procedures, risks, and their rights
  • Evaluate, document, and report adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs), including severity and relationship to investigational product, within protocol-required timelines
  • Review psychiatric safety assessments, including suicidality screening, and escalate safety concerns to the Principal Investigator per protocol and company SOPs
  • Ensure participant safety, rights, and well-being are protected throughout study participation

Clinical Assessments & Procedures

  • Perform physical examinations and other protocol-required clinical assessments at screening and study visits
  • Review vital signs, ECGs, and laboratory results for clinical significance and document investigator assessment
  • Perform blood draws and other study procedures as needed, within scope of licensure and delegation
  • Make protocol-driven decisions on investigational product dosing, holds, and discontinuation within scope of licensure and in consultation with the Principal Investigator

Documentation & Data Integrity

  • Document all assessments and investigator decisions in source documents in a timely, accurate manner consistent with ALCOA+ principles
  • Review and sign off on source documents, case report forms (CRFs), and EDC entries as delegated
  • Respond to data queries and monitor findings in a timely manner

Regulatory & Sponsor Communication

  • Perform only those study tasks delegated by the Principal Investigator and documented on the Delegation of Authority log
  • Maintain current regulatory documents, including CV, license, GCP training, financial disclosure, and Form FDA 1572 listing
  • Participate in site initiation visits, investigator meetings, monitoring visits, and sponsor/CRO communications as required
  • Collaborate with Clinical Research Coordinators, Clinical Raters, and research staff to ensure protocol compliance and quality participant care
  • Support audit and inspection readiness, including participation in sponsor audits, regulatory inspections, and internal quality reviews
  • Complete all required SOP training and company-required trainings as assigned and when updated
  • Maintain all required licenses and certifications and ensure they remain current and in good standing
  • Travel to company meetings, site locations, or study-related activities as required
  • Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications:

  • Current and unrestricted licensure as a physician (MD/DO), Nurse Practitioner (NP), or Physician Assistant-Certified (PA-C) in the State of Texas.
  • Master's Degree (MA) or equivalent, or four to ten years of related experience and/or training, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Previous experience as a Sub Investigator or Clinical Research Coordinator in clinical trials.
  • Familiarity with electronic data capture (EDC) systems and clinical trial management software.
  • Prior psychiatry/CNS therapeutic area experience required.
  • Experience with Phase I–IV clinical trials required.

Certificates, licenses and registrations required:

  • ACRP or SOCRA certification (preferred)

Systems & Technology skills required:

  • Spreadsheet Software (Excel);
  • Word Processing Software (Word);
  • Electronic Mail Software (Outlook);
  • Presentation software (PowerPoint);
  • Experience with EDC systems (e.g., Medidata Rave, REDCap)
  • Experience with CTMS and/or eRegulatory/eTMF platforms (e.g., Veeva)
  • Experience with EMR/EHR systems

Other skills required:

  • Fluency in Spanish is preferred.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities
  • Strong organizational and time management skills
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and professionalism
  • Strong problem-solving and critical thinking skills
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment and decision-making
  • Customer service mindset with focus on patient experience
  • Ability to follow protocols, SOPs, and regulatory requirements
  • Ability to handle high-pressure or fast-paced environments

Physical Requirements and/or environmental factors:

  • Frequently required to stand.
  • Frequently required to walk.
  • Frequently required to sit.
  • Continually required to utilize hand and finger dexterity.
  • Frequently required to climb, balance, bend, stoop, kneel or crawl.
  • Continually required to talk or hear.
  • Occasionally works around fumes, airborne particles, or toxic chemicals.
  • Frequently exposed to bloodborne and airborne pathogens or infectious materials.
  • While performing the duties of this job, the noise level in the work environment is usually moderate
  • The employee must
    • Occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include:
    • Close vision
    • Distance vision
    • Color vision
    • Peripheral vision
    • Depth perception
    • Ability to adjust focus
  • Specialized equipment, machines, or vehicles used:
    • Stethoscope, blood pressure monitor, ECG machine, phlebotomy supplies, and other standard clinical equipment
  • This position operates in a clinical research and office setting. The role involves interaction with study participants, healthcare professionals, and research staff. Work may include use of electronic systems and medical equipment, as well as occasional travel to clinical sites or meetings.

Equal Opportunity: Empathx is committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace where all employees and applicants are treated with respect and dignity. title: Data Engineering Lead
description:
Seer Interactive is a digital marketing consultancy that harnesses compassion, data, technology, and AI to make a mark on our communities, our coworkers, our clients, our industry, and our neighbors. We relentlessly pursue (and share) the truth, bringing together millions of data points from quantitative and qualitative sources, enhanced by responsible, human-centered AI. Our purpose is to unlock potential across these communities, envisioning a world where doing the right thing is intuitive and informed.
At Seer, we see AI as a catalyst for innovation, collaboration, and creativity. Regardless of your division or discipline, leveraging AI is a core part of how we deliver smarter, faster, and more strategic outcomes for our clients. Our AI Council drives company-wide integration by focusing on education, purposeful implementation, and continuous learning, ensuring that AI is embedded in how we think, operate, and grow.
If you’re ready to uplift others, challenge your ego, commit to the truth, and be better than yesterday—keep reading.
Seer is a remote-first agency and a Certified B-Corp, with team members across the country. If an office environment is more your style, this position can also sit in our HQ office in Philadelphia. We can only consider candidates based in the US who can work continental US-based hours.

The Role: You, the Data Engineering Lead of our dreams, are the technical architect of Seer’s data platform, and building agentic development workflows is a core part of the job. You'll own the structural data foundation behind our analytics and AI products while finding repetitive data and BI work and designing, shipping, and maintaining agents that take it off people's plates.

At Seer, AI is embedded in how we deliver smarter, faster, and more strategic outcomes, and the modern marketing data stack is evolving past the dashboard. You’re excited to help shape it. You design platforms that let strategists, analysts, and LLMs query the same source of truth and arrive at better answers via a well-governed semantic layer. You make the engineers around you better through mentorship, code review, and pairing, and you teach in a way that sticks long after a project ends.

You’re intellectually curious, systems-minded, and not afraid to refactor a legacy DAG, rewrite a tangled query, or push back on a flawed plan. Knowing which battles to pick as you shape the future of Seer’s data structure is a core part of the job.

Role Highlights

  • Set the technical direction for Seer’s data platform by defining the architecture and the standards that other engineers build toward.
  • Own Seer’s data platform end-to-end across BigQuery, Dataflow, Airflow, Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, Cloud Storage, and ingestion tools like Fivetran, while making the cost, latency, and freshness tradeoffs that let us scale without surprises.
  • Set the standard for how we model and serve data. This runs from dimensional modeling (grain, conformed dimensions, slowly changing dimensions) and dbt incremental models to a governed LookML semantic layer with row-level security, surfaced in our embedded Looker interface and via MCP.
  • Structure data for agents to retrieve correct, deterministic answers to natural language questions from our non-technical team members.
  • Automate the routine work around dbt: generating tests and documentation, assessing the downstream impact of schema changes, and producing migration or backfill plans.
  • Build triage agents that read pipeline failures and data quality alerts, trace the cause through logs and lineage, and fix the issue or recommend a fix within established operational guardrails.
  • Tune what’s expensive: evolve the observability layer from a manual process to ai-powered workflows that hunt down the slow query, the redundant DAG, and the leaky storage policy. Cut BigQuery costs and dashboard load times, and bring the team along with you.
  • Document and teach. Write playbooks that survive system evolution, decision records that explain why not just what, and onboarding paths that help each new hire ramp up faster.
  • Mentor data engineers and analysts across teams, pair on tough problems, and leave PR comments that make people better, not just their code.

Essential Skills

  • Expert-level fluency across the GCP data stack, including BigQuery (partitioning, clustering, materialized views, cost optimization), Dataflow, Airflow, Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, Datastore, and Cloud Storage, with a track record of architecting production pipelines end-to-end.
  • Expert command of the analytics and BI layer: modular dbt projects, reusable LookML, Looker explores, and embedded dashboards that blend our built in-house SERP microservice data, CRM, and ad engine data into proprietary cross-platform data models. You write clean SQL and are just as good at untangling someone else’s.
  • Expert Git and version control skills, which you use to unblock teammates. You’ve designed CI/CD pipelines with multi-stage deploys, automated test gates, and production debug discipline.
  • Comfort working with AI and LLM tools beyond surface-level usage, including crafting layered, context-aware prompts, building evaluation harnesses to compare phrasing and sampling strategies, and integrating LLMs into engineering workflows where they earn their keep.
  • Proactive and clear communication with project managers, supported by strong estimation skills to provide early visibility into deadline feasibility and guide decision-making.
  • Communication range. You can brief an SLT stakeholder on a cost-saving initiative and a junior engineer on a tricky rebase in the same afternoon, and both walk away clearer.
  • A track record of leading through technical authority and mentorship: setting the bar on a data engineering team, raising the level of engineers around you, and earning trust without needing a reporting line to back it up.

This might not be the right role for you if...

  • Marketing context feels foreign or uninteresting to you. At Seer, the why always traces back to a client, a campaign, or a strategist.
  • You want to lead from the conference room. At Seer, leads stay close to the code.
  • Mentorship feels like a tax rather than a craft. At Seer, making the team around you better is the job.
  • You only feel comfortable leading with a reporting line behind you. This role earns its authority through expertise and trust. Titles are not the defining factor in your ability to lead.
  • You see AI as hype rather than a practical tool.
  • You find time management, context-switching, and juggling multiple priorities challenging.
  • You struggle to adapt to new tools and processes.

30/60/90 Day Plan

  • By Day 30, you will have completed division training, gotten oriented in our GCP and Looker environments, built relationships across the data engineering team, and shipped your first reviewed PR through our CI/CD pipeline.
  • By Day 60, you will have led your first architectural decision (owning the design of a new data pipeline, model, or platform improvement), mentored engineers through code review, pair programming, and consulted on a custom engineering client project.
  • By Day 90, you will be up and running at full capacity, owning the technical direction of the data platform, raising the data design bar across the team, and influencing how Seer builds and operates its data stack end-to-end.
Ready to apply? Ditch the cover letter — we don’t need it. We’d rather see your AI chops. Use our Marketing Career AI Self-Assessment GPT to find out where you land on the AI marketing maturity curve and share your results with us. Our team is excited to read your application responses and will be using them to help determine who we’d like to meet with!
Have questions about recruitment at Seer? Check out our Custom GPT: Guide to Talent Acquisition at Seer to drop in your questions! You can ask it anything about our hiring process, and how to best prepare for an interview with us.
As a B-Corp Certified organization, we are committed to creating an inclusive environment and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.
Not ready to apply but want to keep in touch? Stay connected via our monthly Career Update newsletter! We'll share curated content on Seer, open roles, industry insights, career advice, events you don't want to miss, and more (so you never miss a beat).

description:

title: Full-Stack Engineer (Frontend-Leaning) - CreativeMusic
description:
About ElevenLabs

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

Music is becoming a first-class part of ElevenLabs Creative. You’ll own the UI that lets creators make it, working closely with Research to turn new music models into products people use the next day.

The open question is what the best interface for AI music creation looks like. Creators come for video, dubbing or ads, and music is part of that flow. Making a song from scratch, scoring a video and localising a track into other languages each need a different flow. You’ll form a view on the right experience, build it end to end, and make it easy to adopt each new model as it lands.

You’ll take an ambiguous problem, decompose it, and carry it through legal, design, engineering and launch with Growth. You’ll work in a small, high-ownership team across product, research and go-to-market.

Requirements

  • Strong Frontend experience: you’ve shipped complex, production UIs (React/TypeScript or equivalent) and are comfortable on the backend when the work needs it

  • You’ve owned ambiguous, zero-to-one product work from problem definition to launch, without a PM or a prescriptive backlog

  • You’ve worked closely with designers (Figma) and have taste and opinions about UX

  • You’ve worked across functions such as legal, safety, growth and design to ship, and keep stakeholders updated without prompting

  • You weigh trade-offs and make pragmatic decisions with no single right answer, and build so that new models can be swapped in as they land

Bonus

  • Music, audio or creative-tools experience, or music as a hobby (singing, an instrument, production)

  • Experience building media-heavy interfaces such as audio, video or timeline editors

  • Experience working with ML models or research teams

Location

This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in Europe or on the US East Coast, with the ability to operate in Central European timezones required. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in Dublin, London, New York and Warsaw.

title: Data Engineer
description:
Seer Interactive is a digital marketing consultancy that harnesses compassion, data, technology, and AI to make a mark on our communities, our coworkers, our clients, our industry, and our neighbors. We relentlessly pursue (and share) the truth, bringing together millions of data points from quantitative and qualitative sources, enhanced by responsible, human-centered AI. Our purpose is to unlock potential across these communities, envisioning a world where doing the right thing is intuitive and informed.
At Seer, we see AI as a catalyst for innovation, collaboration, and creativity. Regardless of your division or discipline, leveraging AI is a core part of how we deliver smarter, faster, and more strategic outcomes for our clients. Our AI Council drives company-wide integration by focusing on education, purposeful implementation, and continuous learning, ensuring that AI is embedded in how we think, operate, and grow.
If you’re ready to uplift others, challenge your ego, commit to the truth, and be better than yesterday—keep reading.
Seer is a remote-first agency and a Certified B-Corp, with team members across the country. If an office environment is more your style, this position can also sit in our HQ office in Philadelphia. We can only consider candidates based in the US who can work continental US-based hours.

The Role: You're the engineer who builds the platform so it doesn't break overnight, because if it does, it's yours to fix. As our Data Platform Engineer, you'll own the infrastructure underneath Seer's analytics and AI products: the cloud resources, the infrastructure as code, the CI/CD pipelines, and the alerting that tells us something is wrong before a strategist notices. Our data platform is early in its life, and you'll help take it from a set of connected tools to an automated, well-governed system that every team at Seer can rely on. You'd rather write the Terraform module yourself than file a ticket for someone else to, and you measure your work by whether it keeps working.

Role Highlights

Infrastructure as Code

  • Own and modularize the infrastructure behind Seer's data platform in Terraform or OpenTofu, mapping what exists today and designing what it needs to become

  • Manage permissions and access across the platform, including how team members and agents securely reach data through tools like the Seer’s agentic tooling.

Cloud Platform

  • Build and maintain cloud services behind our data products, including BigQuery, Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, Cloud Storage, making the cost and reliability tradeoffs that let us scale without supprises

  • Automate the processes that bring new clients, data sources, and reports into the platform so they flow through without manual intervention

CI/CD and Code Quality

  • Design and maintain GitHub Action pipelines with automated tests, multi-stage deploys, and review gates

  • Take part in pull requests and code review across the engineering team, raising the quality bar for all changes

Reliability and Observability

  • Build the alerting, monitoring, and logging systems that provide insight to the platform’s health, and own what happens when something breaks

  • Define KPIs for the processes you build and set the thresholds that tell us when it's time to review,audit or retire tooling

AI-Powered Engineering

  • Integrate Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents into your daily engineering workflows to design, implement, test, and maintain production systems, with clear ownership of code quality, security, and reliability

Collaboration

  • Partner with the Data Engineering Leads and the Director of Engineering to turn platform needs into a roadmap you help shape
  • Work from requirements gathered by our product and project managers, so your focus stays on building, not on client meetings

Essential Skills

  • You have hands-on experience writing and modularizing infrastructure as code with Terraform or OpenTofu
  • You have deep familiarity with GitHub, including pull requests, code review, and building workflows with GitHub Actions
  • You have built and run production infrastructure on GCP or AWS
  • You have strong programming skills in an object-oriented language such as Python, or TypeScript
  • You have experience designing alerting and monitoring structures, and you understand what it means to own a system when it fails
  • You have a strong working knowledge of SQL and relational databases
  • You are comfortable in the weeds and prefer owning infrastructure yourself over relying on a separate team to handle it
  • You are someone who defines what "good" looks like for a process, sets KPIs against it, and holds yourself accountable to them
  • You feel energized by building something early-stage and helping decide what it becomes as well as overhauling legacy systems to improve stability and functionality
Bonus!
  • You have experience with object-relational mapping (ORM) tools
  • You have built your own AI agents, skills, or workflows to write and review code faster
  • You have worked in an agency, a startup, in a marketing technology or SaaS company
  • You have been part of an on-call rotation for production systems

This might not be the right role for you if...

  • You're used to a separate DevOps or platform team handling infrastructure for you
  • You'd rather hand a system off once it ships than own its lifecycle
  • You prefer a mature platform with defined processes over helping to design and build one
  • You see AI as hype rather than a practical tool

30/60/90 Day Plan

First 30 Days: Learn

  • Complete division training and get oriented in our GCP environment, Terraform codebase, and GitHub workflows

  • Map the current state of platform infrastructure and flag the first gaps you'd close

  • Ship your first reviewed pull request through our CI/CD pipeline

60 Days: Build

  • Own the design and delivery of an infrastructure improvement end to end, such as a module refactor or a new platform component

  • Add or improve alerting for a critical pipeline, with defined KPIs for what healthy looks like

90 Days: Lead

  • Operate independently on platform requests, bringing solutions, not just questions
  • Deliver a visible, scalable improvement to the platform, such as automated client onboarding or bringing a manual area under infrastructure as code
