title: DIRECTOR OF MANUFACTURING OPERATIONS
description:
Director of Manufacturing Operations

Batesville, IN | Full-Time, On-Site

About Wood-Mizer

Wood-Mizer is the world's largest manufacturer of portable sawmills, with more than 100,000 mills sold in over 100 countries. We build a complete line of sawmilling, wood processing, and blade equipment for forestry and timber professionals. We're 100% employee-owned, so every team member has a stake in our success, and we put our people and customers at the center of everything we do.

Position Summary

The Director of Manufacturing Operations leads Wood-Mizer's Batesville, Indiana, manufacturing facility and is accountable for production output, cost, quality, safety, facility maintenance, manufacturing engineering, product release to production, and shipping performance for the plant. The role drives operational efficiency, cost reduction, and automation across the site while sustaining Wood-Mizer's culture of employee engagement and ownership. Working closely with the President, Wood-Mizer Americas, the Director shapes manufacturing strategy, the Annual Operating Plan (AOP), and capital and facility investment for the site. This role leads multiple direct reports, with a total span of control of approximately 225 employees. It is an on-site position at our Batesville facility, and some domestic and international travel may be required.

Essential Functions

  • Owns the facility's cost and efficiency performance, setting and driving a continuous pipeline of cost-savings and productivity initiatives across labor, materials, and overhead.
  • Identifies, justifies, and leads automation projects (equipment, robotics, material handling, controls/software) to reduce manual labor, cycle time, and unit cost.
  • Directs daily manufacturing operations, including manufacturing engineering and the release of new and enhanced products to production in coordination with product development, so production schedules, quality standards, and unit cost targets are consistently met.
  • Leads, coaches, and manages the performance of the plant leadership and shop-floor teams, keeping a visible, engaged presence on the plant floor that builds morale and a positive, high-performance culture.
  • Owns plant safety performance and culture, sustaining low recordable incident rates (TRIR) and ensuring compliance with all applicable safety, quality, and regulatory requirements.
  • Formalizes and leads a Lean/continuous improvement program that delivers measurable productivity, quality, and cost gains.
  • Oversees facility maintenance, including preventive maintenance programs, equipment reliability, and building and grounds upkeep, to reduce downtime and maintenance cost.
  • Oversees logistics and shipping, including outbound scheduling, carrier performance, and inventory accuracy, and works with the SIOP leader to set and maintain inventory goals and operations plans.
  • Leads capital equipment planning and facility infrastructure projects, including automation investments and major expansions, and partners with the President to deliver manufacturing's portion of the AOP, including budget ownership and cost-savings targets.
  • Coordinates with the HR leader on workforce planning, staffing, training, and succession, including labor needs as automation is introduced; represents manufacturing in cross-functional planning with Sales, Engineering, and executive leadership; and hosts customers, dealers, and visitors on plant tours.
  • Follows all Wood-Mizer safety, quality, and company policies and procedures.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience
  • 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience
  • Demonstrated track record of driving cost reduction and productivity improvement in a manufacturing environment, with results measured in real savings and efficiency gains
  • Hands-on experience identifying, justifying ROI for, and implementing manufacturing automation and process technology (e.g., robotics, vision systems, lights-out manufacturing, IoT, collaborative robots, automated workflows)
  • Demonstrated success designing, implementing, leading, and sustaining Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement programs
  • Strong, visible safety leadership track record
  • Experience managing capital projects
  • Leading, developing, and retaining cross-functional manufacturing teams
  • Analytical, budgeting, and organizational skills
  • Verbal and written communication, including presenting to executive leadership
  • Lean / continuous improvement methods
  • Adopting and applying AI and emerging technology in manufacturing
  • Collaborating across a hybrid corporate structure; flexible and open-minded
  • Approachable, engaging leadership style; represents the plant to visitors, customers, and new employees
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed up to 5%

Preferred

  • Experience in industrial equipment, heavy machinery, or metal fabrication environments

Physical Requirements & Work Environment

The physical demands below describe the job as it is performed, with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Frequently stand and walk throughout the plant floor
  • Frequently use a computer and screen
  • Occasionally sit, climb stairs or ladders, bend, stoop, kneel, and reach overhead
  • Occasionally lift, carry, push, or pull up to 50 lbs

Work environment: Office environment; manufacturing/shop floor; noise above 85 dB, moving machinery, dust, or fumes on the plant floor

Required PPE: safety glasses, hearing protection, and safety-toe boots on the plant floor

What We Offer

  • Employee Ownership – Become a true owner through our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) and share directly in Wood-Mizer's growth and success.
  • Retirement Savings – Save for retirement in our 401(k), with a company match contributed to your ESOP account.
  • Performance Incentives – Earn extra rewards tied to your contributions and results.
  • Flexible Pay Options – Choose from multiple pay methods, including Wages On-Demand, which lets you access earned wages daily.
  • PTO Accrual Starts Day One – Start earning paid time off with your first paycheck, plus paid holidays and additional leave for life events such as marriage, birth, or adoption.
  • Free Health Clinic Access – When enrolled in our medical plan, get free care through Marathon Health, with near-site clinics in Indianapolis, IN and Cincinnati, OH and many services available virtually wherever you live.
  • Comprehensive Insurance – Health, dental, vision, and company-paid life insurance, plus supplemental coverage and short- and long-term disability options.
  • Community Impact – Take part in our Workplace Giving Programs and be recognized for serving others through donations and volunteer work.
  • Education Assistance – Use tuition reimbursement to reach your long-term career and learning goals.
  • Annual Allowances – Reimbursement for safety boots and glasses, plus yearly funds for Wood-Mizer apparel and gear.
  • Everyday Perks – Company events and outings, free coffee and fruit, birthday and anniversary gift cards, referral bonuses, discounted shipping, and more.

Benefits eligibility varies by position and employment status.

If you want a career, not just a job, apply today and see how Wood-Mizer employee-owners are making a difference around the world and right here in Batesville, IN.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Wood-Mizer is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. We make employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. This applies to all aspects of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, compensation, training, transfers, leaves of absence, and terminations.

Accommodations

If you need an accommodation during the application or interview process, please let our recruiting team know, and we will be glad to help.

Interview Process & Communications

As part of our hiring process, Wood-Mizer may use AI tools to assist with screening applications, along with on-demand phone, video, and AI-enabled interviewing tools. These tools support our team; people make all hiring decisions. Candidates may opt in to receive text messages about their application. Message frequency varies, and standard message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out or HELP for assistance. Your mobile number will be used only for application-related communications and will not be shared or sold to third parties.

Pre-Employment Screening

Offers of employment may be contingent on a background check and drug test, as permitted by applicable law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered in accordance with applicable law.

Application Status

Due to the volume of applications we receive, please check your ADP candidate profile for the latest status on your application.

Protect Yourself from Hiring Scams

Wood-Mizer will never ask for payment, banking information, or equipment purchases during the application process. Official communication will only come from a Wood-Mizer company email address.

description:

Position Overview: Under the direction of the Team Leader-Licensed or Wellness Clinician-Licensed, provides direct services to individuals to secure and maintain permanent housing, assesses history, current needs and preferences of person’s served in the areas of mental health and substance use. Works with persons served and the team to develop integrated individualized mental health and substance use treatment goals and interventions.


Essential Job Functions

Create and Maintain:

  • A wellness and recovery-oriented environment by using person-first language, respectful documentation, person-centered planning, and evidence-based practices
  • A culture of compliance with internal and external policies, regulations, laws and high ethical and professional standards.

CSS Services:

  • Contribute to the development, implementation, monitoring, and updating of the Individualized Recovery Plan/Individual Recovery Plan (IRP).
  • Perform therapeutic rehabilitative skill development as outlined in the CSS Regulations.
  • Offer services appropriate to meet person’s served needs as identified in the Comprehensive Rehabilitation Needs Assessment (CRNA) and included in each individuals IRP.
  • Perform crisis intervention as indicated
  • Coordinate and manage services in conjunction with the team.
  • Supportive counseling, medication education, mental health education and early crisis intervention
  • Engages people receiving services in the treatment process.
  • Provides medication education.
  • Provide culturally competent services.
  • Provide housing support services to include pre-tenancy, move-in and on-going tenancy supports.
  • Establishes and implements treatment interventions as outlined in IRP’s.
  • Assess individual’s daily living skills, and teach individual’s needed skills in the areas of budgeting, cooking, laundry, cleaning, shopping, personal hygiene and self-advocacy issues
  • Technical assistance and education to members of the team in the area of substance abuse treatment
  • Provides clinical leadership for CSS team in the area of Integrated Dual Disorder Treatment. Provides intensive integrated dual-recovery services, individual and group treatment service, outreach, referral and case management to adults with co-occurring disorders.
  • Perform evidence-based practices that are appropriate for implementing community support services. This may include Motivational Interviewing, Cognitive Behavioral and Educational Strategies, Trauma Informed Care, Career Services, Permanent Supportive Housing, IMR and WRAP.
  • Completes all documentation on-time per the program’s timeline for documentation.
  • Completes statistical reports as assigned related to services and outcomes.
  • Will participate in individual and group supervision as scheduled. Will actively seek individual supervision sessions with a licensed supervisor.

Direct Services for Persons with Co-Occurring:

  • Performs co-occurring intake assessments as needed.
  • Assess individual’s substance use history and current needs. Works with the individual and the team to develop substance abuse treatment goals and interventions
  • Conducts assessments using the ASI, SATS and other tools as needed.
  • Develop and implement a clinical recovery plan based on the assessment’s and include substance use/cooccurring disorder/IDDT materials and strategies for individual and group interventions, in conjunction with the team.
  • Provides intensive integrated dual-recovery services, individual and group treatment service, outreach, referral and case management to adults with co-occurring disorders
  • Provides Stage-Based counseling using motivational interviewing, CBT, 12 Step principles and behavioral interventions.
  • Facilitates range of Co-Occurring recovery groups as indicated.
  • As indicated, assist individuals to identify triggers for relapse and focus on a lifestyle centered on recovery. Refer to co-occurring mental health and substance use disorder treatment services, and recovery support resources, including medication assisted treatment.
  • Educate individuals on the interactive effects of substance use on psychiatric symptoms, social behavior psychiatric and other medications. Encourage and provide practical strategies for alcohol and substance free-living environments.
  • Collect and share self-help recovery and local co-occurring recovery group meeting lists with individuals and accompany them to local groups and/or meetings in order to encourage engagement/attendance.
  • Provides linkage (referral) to appropriate services, i.e., detox., rehab., AA/NA, HIV services etc.

Service Coordination:

  • Acts as a liaison for the persons served as they move through the treatment system. This includes transporting and accompanying individuals to appointments.
  • Maintains contact with other service providers to encourage referrals and insure effective coordination of services.
  • Participates in discharge meetings, etc. and meets with other service providers as necessary to assist in coordinating treatment planning and interventions.
  • Refers to necessary legal services.
  • Coordinates services with the criminal justice system as needed.

Requirements:

Education/Certifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social work, human services, counseling, psychology or criminal justice.
  • Master’s Degree preferred
  • CADC required

Experience:

  • A minimum of 2 years paid, progressive work experience in co-occurring/Integrated Dual Disorder Treatment services or human service experience with strong knowledge of addictions.
  • Experience as a person in recovery preferred.
  • 1-year experience if certified as a Psychiatric Rehabilitation Practitioner

Disclosure:

  • No more than one moving violation within the past 12 months

title: Medellín Data Engineer: Snowflake & Sigma BI
description:
Note: To be eligible for this role, you must be based in Medellín, Colombia and able to work from our office three days per week. Working hours are 10:00 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. (Colombia time), Monday to Friday a schedule designed to provide overlap with our teams across multiple U.S. time zones.

About Deckard Technologies

Deckard Technologies is a GovTech data company helping local governments address residential property-related challenges, with a focus on compliance and tax collection. Founded in 2018, we operate globally with offices in the U.S., Colombia, and Australia.

Trusted by over 400 jurisdictions worldwide, our scalable, cost-effective products leverage patented processes and combine best-in-class data collection with intuitive, AI-powered solutions, transforming how local governments monitor and manage properties.

Joining us means you’ll be working with a diverse group of inspiring people from industry experts and extraordinary technology and data operations teams to innovative product leaders in a down-to-earth and supportive culture.

Role Overview

We are seeking a Data Engineer to join our operational office in Medellín, Colombia. In this role, you will be responsible for monitoring database health, overseeing end-to-end data pipeline flows, and developing scalable analytics tools, dashboards, and operational workflows within Snowflake and Sigma Computing.

You will work closely with cross-functional Implementation, Data, and Client Experience teams to ensure data integrity, streamline business intelligence delivery, and build self-service reporting assets that drive customer value.

Key Responsibilities

  • Database Monitoring & Data Flow Quality/Oversight: Proactively monitor SQL and cloud data warehouse pipelines, staging tables, and automated data ingestion to ensure continuous availability, high performance, and data integrity.
  • Sigma BI Development: Design, build, and maintain interactive dashboards, complex data workbooks, and custom internal and external reporting tools within Sigma.
  • Data Transformation & Modelling: Write efficient, robust SQL queries, data models, and transformation scripts to prepare raw, multi-source datasets for BI consumption.
  • Troubleshooting & Anomaly Detection: Quickly identify, isolate, and resolve pipeline bottlenecks, data synchronisation failures, broken schemas, or report calculation discrepancies.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Implementation Coordinators, Program Managers, and Data Engineers to structure client-specific data workstreams, including legacy records and spatial data assets.
  • Documentation & Standards: Document data dictionary definitions, metric logic, workflow automations, and reporting best practices to support team scalability.

Required Skills, Qualifications & Experience

  • Snowflake and Sigma Computing: Demonstrated practical experience working with cloud data warehouses and building dashboards and calculation models in Sigma Computing or deep expertise in platforms such as Tableau, Power BI, or Looker, with a strong ability to quickly master Sigma. Experience with cloud data warehouse platforms such as Snowflake, BigQuery, PostgreSQL, or Amazon Redshift is valued, with direct Snowflake experience being highly regarded.
  • Experience: 2–4 years of hands-on experience in data engineering, data analysis, BI development, or database monitoring in a production environment.
  • Advanced SQL—Essential: Strong, hands-on SQL capability is essential for this role. Candidates must be proficient in writing and optimising complex queries using CTEs, window functions, joins, and aggregations across cloud data warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery, PostgreSQL, or Amazon Redshift.
  • Data Flow & Pipeline Knowledge: Solid understanding of ETL/ELT principles, database schema design, and tracking data lineage from ingestion through to dashboard display.
  • English and Spanish Language Proficiency: A minimum B2 level of English proficiency, both verbal and written, is required, alongside native or fluent Spanish. This role involves regular communication and collaboration with English-speaking colleagues across the United States and Australia.
  • Problem-Solving: Strong analytical mindset with rigorous attention to detail regarding data accuracy and quality assurance.
  • Analytical & Model Literacy: Comfort working with the outputs of predictive and classification models, such as booked-versus-blocked night inference and occupancy estimates. This includes understanding confidence thresholds, precision and recall trade-offs, known failure modes, and representing predicted values as distinct from observed values in dashboards and client-facing reporting.
  • Data Governance & Confidentiality: Sound judgment when handling sensitive client data and public records containing personally identifiable information, including address-level and parcel-level data. Familiarity with access controls, row-level security, and the principle of exposing only the minimum data a given report or user requires.
  • Communication & Data Storytelling: Ability to explain data limitations, methodology, and confidence levels to non-technical partners, Implementation Coordinators, Program Managers, and client stakeholders in clear terms. You’ll be the person who explains what a number does and does not support and translates a schema change or data gap into what it means for a client’s deliverable.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field such as Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering, or Information Systems—or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • DBT Experience: Experience working with DBT would be an asset, demonstrating exposure to large-scale, modern SQL pipelines and structured data transformation practices.
  • Familiarity with scripting languages for data automation, such as Python, R, or Bash.
  • Experience with GIS or spatial data layers, such as Esri ArcGIS integrations.
  • Prior experience in a SaaS, civic technology, GovTech, or data-intensive analytics start-up environment.
  • Experience working directly with U.S.-based distributed teams.

English-Language Requirement

As this role works closely with colleagues across the United States and Australia, candidates must have a minimum B2 level of English proficiency and be comfortable participating in meetings, discussing technical matters, and communicating clearly in writing.

Equal Opportunity

At Deckard Technologies, we select candidates solely on merit, experience, and suitability for the role, in line with Article 13 of the Political Constitution of Colombia and Law 931 of 2004. The English-language requirement for this position is directly related to the operational responsibilities of the role and the need to collaborate with English-speaking colleagues across the United States and Australia.

We do not discriminate based on age, sex, race, national or family origin, language background, religion, or political or philosophical opinion.


We welcome applications from persons with disabilities and will make reasonable adjustments to our selection process upon request, in keeping with Law 361 of 1997. Deckard is committed to providing a workplace free from harassment and workplace violence, in line with Law 1010 of 2006 and supported by our Comité de Convivencia Laboral.

If you’re interested in this role but don’t meet 100% of the requirements listed, we encourage you to apply anyway.

title: Resident Advisor
description:
Resident Advisor

Salary Range: $21.00

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt Level: Entry

CLASSIFICATION PURPOSE

Performs a variety of administrative and client-centered wellness and safety activities at an assigned interim and family housing sites.


ALLOCATION STANDARDS

Positions allocable to this entry-level class report to a site program manager and perform various administrative, wellness and safety, and client support activities requiring knowledge and understanding of housing first, harm reduction and trauma-informed principles. Position incumbents work independently and carry out assignment responsibilities within an established framework of program policies and operating procedures. Position responsibilities involve regular client interactions requiring the use of good judgment, empathy, compassion, situational awareness, and collaboration in order to address and resolve routine and complex issues surrounding client behavior, medical and housing needs. Position incumbents maintain regular communication with Care Coordinators in order to support their efforts in assisting clients with legal, health, personal, recovery, and other issues, during their assigned shift. Resident Advisors also provide for the general welfare and safety of all persons that visit the interim housing and family site or its grounds and engage in activities that promote positive relationships with neighboring residents, businesses, and organizations.


ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES

  • Conducts inspections at assigned interim and family housing sites in accordance with established procedures in order to identify and address potential security issues, safety hazards, health and fire code violations, and maintenance repair needs.
  • Performs and documents wellness rounds at assigned and family interim housing facilities following established procedures in order to check on client health and safety needs, administer overdose antidotes, monitor and enforce compliance with occupancy agreements.
  • Participates in daily meetings with Program Management, Care Coordinators, and other Resident Advisors at the start of a new shift in order to discuss client activity, behavior and needs, perimeter and wellness check observations, and incident reports.
  • Maintains a welcoming, clean, and supportive environment for clients and visitors by following established protocols in place at the assigned interim and family housing facility.
  • Enforces interim and family housing safety requirements in order to minimize and prevent hazardous or potentially violent conditions that could result in client or structural harm by following pre-approved protocols and methods.
  • Performs regular walks through the surrounding neighborhood at designed interim and family housing facilities in order to build relationships with residents, foster positive relations, and mitigate escalation of community concerns.
  • Ensures compliance with interim and family housing facility policies and rules by monitoring client behavior, addressing violations, and implementing corrective actions as needed to maintain a safe and orderly living environment.
  • Maintains a variety of documents containing client and visitor data following established interim housing facility procedures in order to comply with record keeping requirements.
  • Assists with the orderly and efficient receipt, storage, and distribution of meals to interim housing clients in a manner consistent with operating procedures.
  • Provides as needed administrative and facility set-up assistance in support of volunteer activities at assigned interim housing facilities.
  • Attends on-site and off-site trainings, team meetings, and occasional events as required, in order to participate in discussions and activities, obtain information to enhance professional development, and contribute to the overall effectiveness of interim housing operations.


KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Ability to serve the homeless community with an inherent desire that demonstrates empathy, compassion, and a commitment to supporting their well-being and quality of life.
  • Basic active listening skills in order to understand and engage with clients, visitors, co-workers, and others.
  • Ability to demonstrate empathy in order to understand and share the feelings of clients when interacting on sensitive matters.
  • Ability to demonstrate compassion when interacting with clients so as to recognize and respond to their needs and struggles with kindness and understanding.
  • Ability to discern such things as behavior, body language, and tone in order apply appropriate approaches and de-escalation techniques when interacting with clients on delicate, sensitive or potentially dangerous situations.
  • Ability to assert authority with tact, diplomacy and collaboration in order to effectively address and resolve situations involving client violations of policies and procedures.
  • Ability to remain calm and composed in challenging situations involving client interactions, medical emergencies, and incidents requiring law enforcement intervention.
  • Ability to demonstrate sensitivity to diverse cultural backgrounds, mental health needs, substance use, and other individual circumstances affecting homeless populations in order to engage clients with respect and compassion.
  • Ability to learn and apply new concepts and protocols on a continuous basis in order to adapt to changing requirements.
  • Basic written and oral expression skills in order to effectively communicate in writing and/or via in-person verbal interactions.
  • Basic customer service excellence skills in order to establish and maintain positive, friendly, and professional interactions with guests, visitors, and staff.
  • Basic skill in the application of office software, such as electronic mail, word processing, scanning software (Adobe, PDF) in order to open and respond to email, type or prepare written materials, and scan documents.
  • Basic skill in the operation of office equipment and machines, such as desktop or laptop computers, printers, and scanners.


Essential Physical Characteristics

The physical characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential job duties of this classification. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of a job, on a case-by-case basis.


  • Continuous: walking, standing, bending and twisting of neck, bending and twisting of waist, squatting, simple grasping, reaching above and below shoulder level, and lifting and carrying of materials over 25 pounds.
  • Frequent: sitting, repetitive use of hands to operate computers, printers and copiers. Exposure to outdoor weather, noise, dust, fluctuating temperature, and lighting.


Workplace Hazard Exposure

The workplace hazard exposure conditions described here are representative of those that an employee may likely encounter in the performance of the essential job duties of this classification.

  • Exposure to potential physical and verbal attacks by clients
  • Death threats
  • Exposure to controlled substances and paraphernalia
  • Exposure to fumes from controlled substances
  • Exposure to smoke from cigarettes
  • Exposure to communicable diseases, such as tuberculosis, scabies, lice
  • Exposure to clients using weapons, such as knives and guns
  • Exposure to bed bugs
  • Exposure to the sun and heat
  • Exposure to vicarious trauma
  • Exposure to vehicle traffic conditions
  • Exposure to bodily fluids (urine, blood, saliva, and fecal matter)
  • Exposure to dog bites


EDUCATION, TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE

No experience required.

All new hires are required to complete a 90-day introductory period during which they must complete an initial 40-hour training program. The training will cover Union Station Homeless Services’ housing first, harm reduction and trauma-informed program model, interim and family housing policies and procedures, client wellness and safety protocols, and other key people management policies. All new hires must also complete CPR and Security Guard training within 60-days of their hire date.


HIRING ASSESSMENTS

The hiring process for this classification will consist of two parts. Part I: online assessment to evaluate basic software application, written expression, and customer service skills scored on a pass/fail basis. Part II: oral interview to evaluate interest and motivation to work in the homeless services sector, oral expression, interpersonal effectiveness, empathy, compassion, situational awareness, and problem solving. Applicants must achieve a score of 70% or higher in order to be placed on the hiring list.


PREEMPLOYMENT BACKGROUND CHECK

Following an offer of employment, all candidates will be required to pass background check consisting of a criminal and references check.

This role coordinates individual learning plans with site training personnel, performs periodic compliance audits, and leads the onboarding of project resources to ensure alignment with learning plan requirements and site access, safety, and system access standards.

The Project Manager in the Utilities industry is responsible for leading and overseeing complex projects from initiation through completion, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and regulatory requirements. The Project Manager will serve as the primary point of contact for stakeholders, facilitating communication and collaboration across cross-functional teams. Ultimately, this position ensures that all project deliverables meet the expected standards and contribute to the operational efficiency and sustainability of utility services.

Understanding the project life cycle allows the Project Manager to guide projects through each phase methodically, from initiation to closure. Preferred skills like advanced software knowledge and stakeholder management enhance the ability to lead complex projects and communicate effectively with diverse teams and external partners.

title: Senior Member Services Rep
description:
YMCA OF GREATER HARTFORD JOB DESCRIPTION

Job Title: Senior Member Service Representative (Senior MSR)
FLSA Status: Non-Exempt
Job Grade:
Primary Department: Membership
Reports to: Membership Director
Revision Date: 09/04/2026
Leadership Level: Leader

Note: May require Evenings and Weekends.


The YMCA of Greater Hartford is an association open to all committed to helping people reach their potential in spirit, mind, and body. Our commitment is based on the belief that the purpose of this three-fold development is to live out the values of Caring, Honest, Respect and Responsibility.

POSITION SUMMARY:

Under the supervision of the Membership Director, the Senior Member Service Representative (Senior MSR) provides exceptional customer service and supports the daily operations of the Welcome Center and Membership Department. The Senior MSR serves as a senior resource and role model for Member Service Representatives (MSRs), assists with training and onboarding, processes membership transactions and changes, supports membership acquisition and retention efforts, and helps ensure a welcoming and positive experience for all members and guests.

The Senior MSR is responsible for supporting the smooth operation of the Welcome Center during assigned shifts, assisting MSRs with questions and member concerns, completing administrative responsibilities, and supporting membership initiatives that contribute to the overall success of the branch.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  1. Knowledge of YMCA of Greater Hartford procedures, rules, regulations, guidelines, membership policies, and branch procedures.

  2. Serve our diverse communities equitably and act with an inclusive, anti-racist lens at all times; promote a brave, respectful culture at the Y.

  3. Provide exceptional customer service and create a welcoming, positive experience for all members, prospective members, and guests.

  4. Serve as a senior resource and role model for Member Service Representatives by providing guidance, support, and assistance with questions and situations that arise.

  5. Assist with the training and onboarding of new MSRs, including Welcome Center procedures, membership processes, customer service expectations, YMCA policies, and applicable systems.

  6. Lead the Welcome Center during assigned shifts, ensuring smooth daily operations, appropriate staff coverage, and adherence to established procedures.

  7. Perform the standard responsibilities of an MSR, including greeting members and guests, answering questions, processing transactions, enrolling members in programs and classes, and providing information about YMCA services and membership benefits.

  8. Process membership changes and related documentation, including membership holds, cancellations, transfers, payment authorizations, and program registrations.

  9. Assist with financial assistance application approval and reverification by ensuring members provide required documentation while maintaining confidentiality.

  10. Ensure accurate cash handling, daily transactions, reports, and front-desk procedures.

  11. Maintain a clean, professional, organized, and welcoming Welcome Center environment.

  12. Ensure all necessary Welcome Center supplies and inventory are stocked and alert the Membership Director of items that need to be ordered or replenished.

  13. Support membership retention efforts by identifying member needs, addressing concerns, and connecting members with appropriate programs, services, and resources.

  14. Support membership termination prevention and retention efforts by running reports and proactively contacting members with pending future terminations to address concerns, identify retention opportunities, and encourage continued membership.

  15. Assist with termination recovery efforts by contacting former members and identifying opportunities to re-engage them with the YMCA.

  16. Assist with membership promotions, follow-up calls, outreach, and other initiatives designed to increase membership acquisition, engagement, and retention.

  17. Give cause-driven tours to prospective members and effectively communicate the YMCA's mission, programs, services, and membership benefits.

  18. Meet or support budgeted membership acquisition, revenue, and net unit goals each month.

  19. Utilize Daxko Engage to create and implement member engagement initiatives designed to increase member acquisition and retention.

  20. Assist new members with onboarding, including downloading the YMCA app and providing instruction on how to access class schedules, program schedules, and register for group exercise classes.

  21. In conjunction with the Membership Director, monitor Net Promoter Score (NPS) feedback and follow up with member concerns in a timely and appropriate manner.

  22. Identify opportunities to improve member engagement and provide ideas and recommendations to the Membership Director.

  23. Help ensure consistent enforcement of YMCA policies, including facility access, membership, guest, age, and safety policies.

  24. Communicate important member, staffing, facility, and operational issues to the Membership Director and appropriate leadership.

  25. Work collaboratively with the Membership Director and Marketing Department to assist with social media management and membership-related promotional initiatives.

  26. Collaborate with other departments to promote programs, services, events, and opportunities that enhance member engagement and support membership goals.

  27. Assist the Membership Director with administrative tasks, reporting, projects, and other duties as assigned.

  28. Participate in staff training, meetings, annual campaign activities, special events, and other branch or Association initiatives as required.

  29. Maintain confidentiality of member and organizational information in accordance with YMCA policies and applicable regulations.

  30. Act as a positive role model for MSRs and contribute to a collaborative, team-oriented work environment.

  31. Perform other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Strong customer service, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with diverse populations and provide inclusive, equitable service.
  • Ability to multitask, prioritize responsibilities, and remain organized in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to work independently while also functioning effectively as part of a team.
  • Ability to provide guidance and support to fellow team members.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately complete administrative and financial transactions.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality when handling member information and financial assistance documentation.
  • Experience with membership software, point-of-sale systems, customer relationship management (CRM) systems, or similar software preferred.
  • Ability to learn and utilize Daxko and other YMCA systems effectively.
  • Professional, dependable, positive, and service-oriented demeanor.
  • This position may be authorized to have access to protected Health Information (PHI) to perform specific job duties.
  • Ability to represent the YMCA professionally and support the mission and values of the YMCA of Greater Hartford.
  • CPR/AED and First Aid certification required or must be obtained within 90 days of hire.

EDUCATION:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • College coursework or degree in business, recreation, hospitality, communications, or a related field preferred.

EXPERIENCE:

  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience in customer service, membership, sales, hospitality, front-desk operations, or a related field preferred.
  • Previous experience in a YMCA or membership-based organization preferred.
  • Previous experience training or providing leadership to staff preferred.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENT:

  • Ability to sit, stand, walk, bend, stoop, and move throughout the Welcome Center and YMCA facility for extended periods.
  • Ability to lift and carry supplies and equipment weighing up to 25 pounds.
  • Ability to use a computer, telephone, point-of-sale system, and other office equipment.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with members, guests, staff, and leadership in person, by telephone, and through electronic communication.
  • Ability to respond appropriately and calmly to member questions, concerns, and potentially stressful situations.
  • Ability to move throughout the YMCA facility and access various program and service areas as needed.
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as required by branch operations.
  • Ability to perform duties in a fast-paced environment while maintaining a high level of customer service and professionalism.

Medical, Dental, Vision

403b

Paid Time Off

Long Term Disability, Life Insurance

EAP

Tuition Reimbursement program

title: Senior Political Coordinator
description:
Senior Political Coordinator

UFCW Legislative and Political Action Department

www.ufcw.org

Organization:

United Food and Commercial Workers International Union (UFCW) is North America’s neighborhood union; standing together to improve the lives and livelihoods of workers, families and communities. Our members work primarily in the retail food, meatpacking, poultry, food processing and manufacturing and retail store industries.


Location:

Washington, DC, Little Falls, NJ and Media, PA

Position Description:

The Senior Political Coordinator in coordination with local unions, is responsible for building out electoral, legislative, fundraising and activist programs under the direction of the Director.


The Senior Political Coordinator also assesses candidate viability, priority races, and meets with potential

candidates to ensure they understand UFCW’s issues in collaboration with local unions. This position is also assigned to work with locals on building out their electoral programs and legislative priorities.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Include the following. Other duties may be assigned. This list is not exhaustive and may be supplemented.

Writes thorough state electoral plans for targeted local unions and races, as well as keeps up to date on

competitive races in their assigned region to provide analysis on fundraising, polling, relevant campaign

issues and endorsements.


Works closely with local unions on priorities including low-dollar fundraising, running member-to-member electoral and legislative campaigns, engaging in federal grassroots and grasstops legislative campaigns and other priorities as assigned.


Executes the International Union’s program priorities in their assigned region. Responsible for running a

multifaceted program in multiple states that will include canvassing, worksite organizing, voter registration in collaboration with phone banking, and peer-to-peer texting and social media outreach. This encompasses building out a work management system in multiple states which allows for timely reporting and a field feedback loop.


Works with rank-and-file member organizers to run electoral programs in targeted states. Responsible for

running well-organizing onboarding, regular team meetings, trainings and conducting one-on-one coaching to ensure member organizers are reaching program goals. Acts in a timely manner and uses discretion when dealing with a member organizer consistently not reaching goals or fulfilling program duties.


Responsible for keeping up to date on Federal campaign giving laws, as well as be a resource on state and

local giving laws. Responds to fundraising requests from local unions in a time sensitive manner.



Develops, updates, and maintains state and local specific training materials that cover fundraising, electoral work and legislative work and coaches the local union political staff person to successfully run trainings, fundraising drives and regular fundraising orientations for new staff representatives from local unions.


Responsible for customizing training to meet audience needs – local union staff, stewards, member

organizers, and rank-and-file members. Responsible for making sure that legal information in presentations is accurate such as state voter registration laws and early vote laws.


Works with the Director and Legislative team to execute an endorsement process at the federal, state and

local levels that involves viability assessments of races and candidates, candidate interviews, candidate

questionnaires and where possible member, engagement in the endorsement process.


Develops briefing materials for local union presidents on the value of political giving and what is at stake in their state.


Represents the UFCW at in-state coalition tables from time to time. Manages these relationships with

discretion and not undermine local union relationships. Responds to requests from candidate campaigns in

a timely manner and ensure that the UFCW endorsement process is being followed.


Builds relationships with the local union political and legislative contacts and ensure they are up to date on any in-state developments the International Union is tracking.


Keeps up to date on new tactics and technologies that enables the UFCW to reach members using diverse

tactics such as relational organizing, peer-to-peer texting, click to call tools, social media, worksite and door to door work and other outreach tactics. Responsible for specific technical tools in the UFCW toolbox and if they are not familiar with the tools, will undergo onboarding and will have expectations of technical tool administration.


Keeps an up-to-date sharable and assessable database of local union, political and coalition contacts.

Duties, responsibilities and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned at any time, in the UFCW’s discretion. UFCW employees function as a team and, occasionally, and on a temporary basis, employees may be required to perform tasks usually performed by others. This might occur if a team member is absent or unavailable to complete a project and the team is responsible for the deadline. Because employees are required to work as a team, you are required to step up and fill in for a team member who is absent or needs assistance from time to time.



QUALIFICATIONS:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education and/or Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Political Science or related field or equivalent related experience. Minimum of 3 years in grassroots organizing experience with a labor or progressive organization required. Minimum of four to six years’ experience, ideally in a labor organization with fundraising and/or political organizing experience



Computer/Software Skills

Proficiency with Microsoft Office suite and ability to use all functions in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. Ability to put together comprehensive reports in Excel and written reports without errors or typos. Experience using online databases like NGP-VAN for analysis, virtual phone banks canvasses and activist engagement. Must be able to review documents like mail and digital content for messaging and ensure that the content is factual. Must be comfortable resolving minor tech issues with iPhones, tablets and laptops.

Communication, Analytical and Leadership Skills

Excellent oral and written communication skills are required.

Must be able to work with discretion, handle sensitive situation and recognize when to refer to a higher level.

Must be able to work with people from different aspects of political work, Presidential candidates and staff, local union presidents and staff, as well as rank and file members.

Must demonstrate strong technical, policy, analytical and strategic abilities, and skills.

Must be able to make effective oral presentations to groups or individuals.

Must be able to take critical feedback and improve work products on a consistent basis with accuracy. Must have ability to adapt to the best way to reach out to specific local union contacts.


Other Knowledge/Skills/Abilities Required

Must have strong written and oral skills. Must be able to write documents without typos and keep in mind audience needs.


Must be able to present information to union audiences in a clear, concise way that connects on the issues

UFCW members care about.


Must have an understanding of FEC laws and regulations concerning PAC and their interactions with state election and financial disclosure laws. Must be able to quickly learn their interaction with labor organizations.


Must have an understanding of Federal Campaign Finance and experience researching state and local

campaign finance laws.


Must have the ability to work independently. Must have initiative.


Must have the ability to canvass and run a canvass.


Demonstrated understanding of the labor movement and culture.


Multilingual speaking ability is a plus.

Personal Characteristics

Commitment and dedication to the UFCW’s mission to fighting for our members.





Job Demands

Ability to work well under pressure and meet deadlines. Must be able to handle multiple priorities and work projects for completion in a timely manner. Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment. Must be able to respond to emails, texts and phone calls in a timely manner. Work requires long and irregular hours, including nights and weekends. Extensive travel required across the U.S. in both planes and cars. Ability to perform long-term assignments for weeks or months at a time.


Working Conditions

The work is performed in a normal office environment or may be performed at various designated work

locations throughout the United States. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Attendance at meetings or events off-site and after normal working hours is often required. The work

atmosphere is fast-paced and deadline-oriented.

Physical Demands

The position involves, but is not limited to, written and oral communications skills, use of computer

keyboard, close vision, sitting for long periods, stooping, bending and reaching. Covering extensive

geographic areas on foot for canvassing.


This is an exempt position under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA).

Reasonable accommodations will be provided pursuant to state and federal laws.

COMPENSATION

The UFCW provides a very generous benefits package, including:

title: User Acceptance Testing Specialist
description:
Position Summary

The User Acceptance Testing (UAT) Specialist at SUMURI is responsible for validating new software

builds, updates, and features for RECON ITR, RECON LAB, and PALADIN before they are released to

customers. This role tests builds received from the Development team against established requirements

and acceptance criteria, identifies defects and usability issues, and delivers clear, actionable feedback to

drive product quality and reliability. The UAT Specialist works closely with the Development team

throughout the build-and-feedback cycle, verifying fixes, performing regression testing, and ensuring that

SUMURI's digital forensics software meets a high standard of functionality and user experience prior to

release. Because the majority of SUMURI's products and workflows run on macOS, experience working

within a macOS environment is strongly preferred. Success in this position requires strong attention to

detail, analytical thinking, clear written communication, and the ability to evaluate software from the

perspective of the end user.


Key Responsibilities

• Receive new software builds, updates, and release candidates for RECON ITR, RECON LAB, and

PALADIN from the Development team and execute structured User Acceptance Testing (UAT) prior to

release.

• Develop and maintain UAT test plans, test cases, and checklists based on product requirements, user

stories, and acceptance criteria.

• Leverage AI-assisted tools to support UAT activities—such as generating and refining test cases,

analyzing logs and defects, and accelerating regression testing—while applying human judgment to

verify results and ensure forensic accuracy.

• Test new features, enhancements, and bug fixes across RECON ITR, RECON LAB, and PALADIN to

confirm they function as intended and meet quality and usability standards.

• Identify, document, and report defects, inconsistencies, and usability issues with clear, reproducible

steps and supporting evidence (screenshots, logs, sample data).

• Provide timely, detailed, and constructive feedback to the Development team on build quality,

functionality, and overall user experience.

• Re-test and verify resolved issues and bug fixes to confirm successful resolution before sign-off and

release.

• Perform regression testing to confirm that new changes do not introduce defects into existing

functionality.

• Collaborate with Development and Product teams to clarify requirements, prioritize reported issues, and

track defects through to resolution.

• Maintain organized, accurate records of test results, defect logs, and build approval status within JIRA.

• Evaluate software from an end-user perspective, flagging workflow, usability, or design concerns that

may affect customer experience.

• Participate in ongoing learning to stay current on SUMURI's product line, digital forensics workflows,

and industry trends in order to test with informed, real-world context.

• Assist customers as needed, including providing technical support and supporting the Sales team.

• Other duties as assigned.


Qualifications & Skills

• Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or

equivalent practical experience.

• Prior experience in software testing, quality assurance, or user acceptance testing preferred.

• Experience with macOS strongly preferred, as the majority of SUMURI's products and testing workflows

are conducted in a macOS environment.

• Familiarity with RECON ITR, RECON LAB, or PALADIN, or with digital forensics tools more broadly, is

a plus.

• Strong attention to detail with the ability to identify inconsistencies, edge cases, and unexpected

behavior.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills for documenting and reporting findings to a technical

audience.

• Solid understanding of the software development lifecycle and common testing methodologies.

• Familiarity with JIRA for tracking and reporting defects is a plus.

• Ability to manage multiple test cycles and meet release deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

title: D110 1st Assistant Operator 1st Shift
description:
Position Overview:

The D110 1st Assistant Operator is responsible for supporting the safe, efficient, and high-quality operation of the D110 machine center. This role serves as the lead support to the Operator and must be capable of setting up and running the machine to standard with minimal oversight. The 1st Assistant Operator ensures compliance with all quality checks, sampling plans, safety procedures, and data-entry requirements while contributing to the overall performance of the crew.

The successful candidate must be able to operate independently when required, provide direction to other team members, and demonstrate full working knowledge of key machine systems including hot melt units, cold glue units, ejector systems, Marsh printing units, and Straub taper units.

Key Responsibilities

- Machine Setup & Operation

· Assist in and independently perform machine setups to meet production standards for quality, safety, and speed.

· Run the D110 machine according to established specifications and customer requirements.

· Make mechanical and process adjustments as needed to maintain optimal performance.

· Operate autonomously in the absence of the primary machine operator.

- Quality Control & Compliance

· Perform all required box checks, sampling procedures, and documentation per plant quality standards.

· Monitor product quality throughout the run and initiate corrective actions as needed.

· Ensure proper machine calibration, glue application, and folding accuracy to meet customer specifications.

- Safety & Housekeeping

· Follow all facility safety policies and procedures, including lockout/tagout and PPE requirements.

· Maintain a clean and organized work area in accordance with 5S and TPM practices.

· Immediately report safety concerns, mechanical issues, or product defects to supervision.

- Team Leadership & Communication

· Assist in training and directing crew members in safe and efficient machine operation.

· Communicate production status, challenges, and corrective actions to the Operator and Supervisor.

· Support a positive, collaborative, and productive work environment.

- Equipment Knowledge & Technical Competence

· Demonstrate working knowledge of machine components including:

o Hot melt units

o Cold glue systems

o Ejector units

o Marsh printers

o Straub tapers

· Perform basic troubleshooting and minor repairs as directed.

Required Education, Skills & Qualifications

· Strong understanding of standard box plant processes and converting operations.

· Ability to think in spatial/three-dimensional terms to understand and troubleshoot complex folding patterns.

· Mathematical proficiency, including conversion to decimals and measurement accuracy.

· Reasonable mechanical and tool-use skills.

· Ability to perform basic computer functions related to data entry, machine documentation, and system navigation.

· Strong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

· Previous experience as a machine assistant in corrugated converting operations.

· Demonstrated ability to lead small teams or direct support personnel.

· Familiarity with TPM, 5S, or continuous improvement programs.

Physical Requirements

· Ability to stand, walk, bend, and lift up to 50 lbs. for extended periods.

· Manual dexterity and the ability to operate hand tools and machine controls.

· Ability to work in a fast-paced, high-volume manufacturing environment

title: Applied Scientist II, International and Emerging Stores Payments
description:
Do you want to translate cutting-edge science into products that expand financial access for millions? At International and Emerging Stores Payments (IESP), we build payment solutions for communities and geographies that Amazon's selection and prices do not yet reach because of payment barriers. These markets make up roughly 80% of the world's countries and 85% of its population.

As an Applied Scientist II on our team, you will design, build, and ship machine learning and generative-AI solutions that remove those barriers and advance financial inclusion, working at the intersection of research and production alongside scientists, engineers, and economists. If you are a curious, self-motivated researcher who turns ambiguity into clarity, we would like to hear from you.

What you will work on:

• Build models that recommend the most suitable payment method for each customer—for example installments, cards, or local payment options—and identify the right customers to reach, balancing customer preference, cost, and risk.
• Take models to production behind a real-time, low-latency personalization layer that serves live shopping traffic at scale.
• Build multi-agent generative-AI systems that turn unstructured inputs—customer feedback, documents, and operational data—into reliable, decision-ready insight, with verification that guards against model hallucination.
• Help customers discover and adopt installments and alternative payment methods.
• Design and analyze large-scale online experiments and causal measurement to validate real customer and business impact.


Key job responsibilities
• Design, develop, and evaluate machine learning and deep learning models, and deploy production-ready solutions to complex customer and business problems.
• Conduct rigorous scientific research: form hypotheses, run experiments, evaluate model performance, and iterate on approaches within your domain of expertise.
• Write clean, maintainable, and efficient code that integrates smoothly into larger systems and meets a high bar for operational excellence.
• Partner with engineering to take your models to production, and with scientists across related payments ML teams to solve shared, complex problems.
• Contribute to team roadmaps, priorities, and technical direction; mentor peers and provide constructive feedback on research and code.
• Publish at peer-reviewed venues and file patent applications where appropriate.

A day in the life
You will start your day reviewing experiment results and refining model architectures based on new insights. Throughout the day you will alternate between writing research code, analyzing data, and discussing technical approaches with teammates, working closely with engineering to build your ideas and take them to production. You will regularly present findings and propose new ideas, and you may write research papers and submit patent applications.

About the team
We are the science team for International and Emerging Stores Payments. We build solutions that directly shape how customers pay and that drive conversion across Amazon's fast-growing international markets—and there is no shortage of hard science and engineering problems, since these markets span most of the world's countries and the majority of its customers. We value scientific rigor, creative problem-solving, and a genuine commitment to learning and growth. If you are excited about building impactful solutions and advancing financial inclusion through applied science, we would love to have you join us.

title: MRO PURCHASING SPECIALIST
description:
MRO PURCHASING SPECIALIST

Department: Procurement

Reports To: Material Manager

Location: Cincinnati, Ohio

Employment Type: Full-Time

FLSA Status: Salary Non-Exempt

Position Summary

The MRO Purchasing Specialist is responsible for the timely, cost-effective, and compliant procurement of maintenance, repair, and operating (MRO) materials and services that support safe, reliable chemical manufacturing operations. This role partners closely with Maintenance, Engineering, Operations, Reliability, Safety, Finance, and storeroom personnel to ensure critical parts and services are available when needed while optimizing inventory, supplier performance, total cost, and working capital.

The position manages related MRO purchases negotiation from request for proposal requisition through confirmation order to delivery and invoice resolution, with particular attention to plant-critical equipment, product specification, planned outages, emergency repairs, hazardous-area requirements, and site procurement controls.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Purchasing and Order Management

  • Purchase MRO materials, spare parts, consumables, equipment, rentals, and repair services in accordance with approved requisitions, specifications, budgets, and delegated authority.
  • Create, issue, expedite, revise, and close purchase orders; confirm pricing, quantities, delivery dates, freight terms, lead times, warranties, and documentation requirements.
  • Support urgent and after-hours plant needs by rapidly sourcing critical items while maintaining required approvals and transaction records.
  • Coordinate purchasing for preventive maintenance, capital projects, turnarounds, shutdowns, and outage work to reduce schedule and production risk.
  • Resolve order discrepancies, damaged shipments, returns, credits, invoice exceptions, and three-way match issues with suppliers, Accounts Payable, and internal stakeholders.

Strategic Sourcing and Supplier Management

  • Comply with procurement policy through solicit competitive quotations, analyze total cost, negotiate commercial terms, and recommend sourcing decisions based on price, quality, service, risk, and lifecycle value.
  • Develop and maintain qualified supplier relationships for mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, piping, safety, laboratory, and general industrial categories.
  • Monitor supplier performance, including on-time delivery, quality, responsiveness, lead-time reliability, and corrective actions.
  • Identify opportunities for consolidation, standardization, blanket purchase orders, consignment, vendor-managed inventory, and alternative sourcing.
  • Maintain awareness of market conditions, supply constraints, obsolete items, and single-source risks; develop mitigation plans for critical materials.

Inventory and Storeroom Support

  • Partner with Maintenance, Reliability, and storeroom teams to establish and maintain appropriate min/max levels, reorder points, critical-spare designations, and stocking strategies.
  • Review usage, excess, obsolete, inactive, and duplicate inventory and recommend actions that improve availability while reducing working capital.
  • Ensure accurate item descriptions, manufacturer and part numbers, units of measure, lead times, supplier records, and other purchasing master data.
  • Support cycle counts, physical inventory activities, material reservations, and investigation of inventory variances as needed.

Chemical Manufacturing Compliance and Safety

  • Purchase materials and services that meet approved engineering specifications, site standards, applicable codes, and hazardous-location requirements.
  • Obtain and retain required documentation such as safety data sheets, certificates of analysis or conformance, material test reports, insurance certificates, warranties, and technical data.
  • Support contractor and supplier compliance with site safety, environmental, security, and quality requirements, including prequalification and onboarding processes.
  • Follow purchasing controls, authorization limits, segregation-of-duties requirements, contract terms, and applicable regulatory and corporate policies.
  • Actively support the site's safety culture and promptly raise concerns involving product substitution, counterfeit parts, specification deviations, or supply risks.

Systems, Analytics, and Continuous Improvement

  • Use the ERP/EAM or CMMS system to manage requisitions, purchase orders, supplier records, master data material, receipts, and purchasing reports.
  • Track and communicate key performance indicators such as purchase price variance, cost savings, supplier delivery, emergency buys, open orders, stockouts, and inventory value.
  • Maintain complete and auditable purchasing records and support internal, customer, and regulatory audits.
  • Participate in cross-functional improvement projects involving procure-to-pay, inventory optimization, maintenance planning, and supplier quality.

Qualifications

Required

  • Associate degrees in supply chain, business, procurement, operations, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • Three or more years of purchasing, materials, inventory, or supply chain experience, preferably supporting manufacturing, maintenance, or industrial operations.
  • Working knowledge of MRO materials and services, purchasing practices, supplier negotiation, inventory controls, and procure-to-pay processes.
  • Experience using an ERP, EAM, or CMMS platform and proficiency with Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft 365 applications.
  • Ability to interpret purchase specifications, bills of material, technical descriptions, and vendor quotations.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and urgent plant needs.
  • Demonstrated attention to detail, sound judgment, ethical conduct, and commitment to safety and compliance.
  • Proven SAP proficiency is must have


Preferred

  • Bachelor's degree in supply chain management, business, engineering, or related discipline.
  • Experience in chemical, petrochemical, pharmaceutical, food, refining, or other process manufacturing environments.
  • Familiarity with mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, piping, valves, pumps, motors, PPE, and industrial safety supplies.
  • Professional certification such as CPSM, CPIM, CSCP, or equivalent.

Core Competencies

  • Customer and operational focus
  • Commercial judgment and negotiation
  • Planning, prioritization, and follow-through
  • Supplier relationship management
  • Data accuracy and analytical thinking
  • Cross-functional collaboration
  • Continuous improvement
  • Safety and compliance mindset

Work Environment and Physical Requirements

This position is in both an office setting and an operating chemical manufacturing facility. The employee may occasionally enter production, maintenance, warehouse, laboratory, and outdoor areas where noise, temperature variation, moving equipment, chemicals, and other industrial hazards may be present. Required personal protective equipment and all site safety rules must be followed.

  • Ability to sit and work at a computer for extended periods and regularly communicate by phone, email, and in person.
  • Ability to walk through plant and warehouse areas, climb stairs, and inspect or identify materials as needed.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to [insert site requirement] pounds occasionally.
  • Ability to respond to urgent procurement needs outside normal business hours when business conditions require.
  • Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Disclaimer

This job description summarizes the primary responsibilities and qualifications of the position. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties. Responsibilities may change based on business needs. Employment remains subject to applicable company policies and law.

title: Change Enablement Governance Analyst
description:
At Derivco, we build the technology behind some of the world’s leading iGaming experiences, and every change we release lands in regulated markets across the globe. Moving fast matters to us. So does getting it right.

As our Change Enablement Governance Analyst, you’ll make sure technology and system changes are introduced in a controlled, compliant and low-risk way, without slowing the business down. Working within our ITSM standards and continuous delivery practices, and under senior governance oversight, you’ll keep our change enablement framework running smoothly across multiple entities and jurisdictions. You’ll protect the systems our partners depend on and help teams across the organisation navigate change with confidence.

What You'll Do

  • Set up and maintain governance controls that check adherence to policy through reporting, dashboards and regular checks.
  • Analyse trends in change data to find process gaps and bottlenecks, then recommend and implement improvements that cut manual effort.
  • Review change documentation against regulatory requirements to support risk assessment and compliance evaluation, spotting control gaps before they become problems and keeping us audit ready.
  • Support audits by gathering change evidence from our ITSM systems, organising documentation for external auditors and assisting with compliance investigations.
  • Keep the ITSM change module healthy by supporting workflow configuration, monitoring data quality and reporting tool limitations that need senior attention.
  • Be a go-to support point for the framework: answer process queries, deliver training and share guidelines so teams can self-serve with confidence.
  • Coordinate across change, technical and business teams, relaying information and tracking actions to support successful changes, and escalate issues to governance leadership when needed.
  • Find where manual effort can be reduced and support automation and streamlining initiatives.
  • Create and maintain process guides, approval criteria references and training content that codify how change works at Derivco.
  • Cross-skill across all core functional areas of the team so the business always has continuity.


What You'll Bring

  • A bachelor’s degree in information technology or business administration (or equivalent experience).
  • 4 to 6 years of progressive experience in IT change management, IT service management, process coordination or compliance support, with evidence of managing change processes and supporting governance frameworks.
  • Intermediate knowledge of ITSM change enablement processes and ITIL principles, with experience processing change requests, assessing change impact and applying change governance standards across multiple functions.
  • An understanding of multi-jurisdictional regulatory requirements affecting technology change, with the ability to turn them into practical change controls.
  • Experience setting up or taking over governance controls: using reporting, dashboards and checks to monitor policy adherence, and analysing trends to find gaps and strengthen those controls.
  • Practical experience with enterprise ITSM platforms, including configuring workflows and monitoring data quality.
  • Confidence engaging stakeholders across technical and business teams: delivering training, answering process queries, coordinating work and knowing when to escalate to governance leadership.
  • An improvement mindset. You spot manual effort, back automation and streamlining, and are willing to cross-skill across all core functional areas.
  • Strong documentation skills, sharp attention to detail and a practical, problem-solving approach.


Who You'll Work With

This is a global role with a broad, international view. Day to day, you'll partner with Product and Delivery Managers, Engineering and Development teams, IT Operations and Service Management, DevOps and Release Management, and our Compliance and Risk teams. Externally, you'll work with external auditors on evidence requests.

Why Derivco

Your work here directly protects revenue-generating systems, keeps our partners' trust and supports our competitive edge. You'll shape how change is done, not just follow the process, by feeding real operational insight into how our framework and tooling evolve. And you'll help build a culture where teams understand change governance and own it themselves.

title: Director, Automation & Data Engineering
description:
Full-time, Permanent Paris or Montpellier (Hub-based, Hybrid)

Director, Automation & Data Engineering

About SeqOne

SeqOne is a fast-growing B2B software scale-up building the leading cloud platform for clinical next-generation sequencing (NGS) analysis.

What is clinical NGS, and why does it matter?

Next-generation sequencing has revolutionised medicine by making it possible to read a patient's genetic code quickly and affordably. But raw sequencing data is meaningless on its own—it must be processed, filtered, annotated, and interpreted before a clinician can act on it. This interpretation step is now the bottleneck in precision medicine: labs are drowning in data while patients wait for answers.

SeqOne exists to solve this. Our cloud-based software platform helps molecular laboratories and hospitals analyse, interpret, and report genetic data—faster, more accurately, and at scale. We combine advanced bioinformatics pipelines, AI-powered decision support, and intuitive clinical workflows into a single SaaS solution, enabling labs to focus on what matters: delivering actionable insights to patients and their care teams.

With 170+ customers across 32 countries, SeqOne supports cancer diagnostics, rare disease diagnosis, pharmacogenomics, and newborn screening—anywhere precision medicine is needed.

But here's what we're really doing:

We're compressing the time between a patient's uncertainty and their answer.

A child waiting for a rare disease diagnosis. A cancer patient waiting to learn if a targeted therapy might work. A family waiting to understand. The sequencers are not the bottleneck anymore—interpretation is. That's the problem SeqOne exists to solve.

Our north star is a 10x reduction in human time from "case ready for review" to "report signed." Every click is a cost. Every manual step is a bug we haven't fixed yet. Every repeated pattern is a failure of automation.

If we build SeqOne right, labs will one day struggle to remember how they ever did this work without it.

The organization context:

  • Total Technology & Engineering headcount: ~45 people across Platform, Stream-aligned, Subsystem, and Enabler teams
  • CTO Organization: ~30 people including Engineering FullStack (~12), Engineering QA (~7), Platform Infrastructure (~4), Biocore (~4), BioOps (~3)
  • Your Platform team: 5 people (3 existing: Senior Bioinformatician for data curation + Automation Engineer for N8N/SeqOne Flow, 1 public API architect), 1 to hire: Data Engineer, 1 prospective nearshore resource

Our Values

  • Unstoppable Positivity – We approach challenges with energy, resourcefulness and a solution-first mindset, turning constraints into opportunities instead of getting stuck in complaints. We value people who learn from setbacks, iterate quickly and keep moving forward even when things are ambiguous or hard.
