title: QA Product and Process Technician
description:
QA Product & Process Technician (2nd Shift)

Location: Stanley, North Carolina
Schedule: Monday – Friday, 3:00 PM – 11:00 PM
Department: Quality Assurance
Reports To: QA Engineer

Join Our Team

We are seeking a detail-oriented and proactive QA Product & Process Technician to support our quality assurance and manufacturing operations. In this role, you will play a key part in ensuring product quality, driving continuous improvement initiatives, analyzing production processes, and partnering with cross-functional teams to maintain the highest standards of performance and customer satisfaction.

This is an excellent opportunity for a quality-focused professional who enjoys problem-solving, data analysis, process improvement, and hands-on involvement in a manufacturing environment.

What You'll Do

  • Inspect and test products throughout various stages of the manufacturing process.
  • Perform product, process, and component failure analysis to identify root causes and corrective actions.
  • Support production by troubleshooting quality-related issues and driving continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Analyze statistical data and generate quality performance reports, including Cpk, LTA, and BDK reports.
  • Process internal, supplier, and customer quality concerns, including investigation, corrective action, and follow-up.
  • Manage non-conforming materials through established quality processes.
  • Coordinate production trials for new products, components, and manufacturing process improvements.
  • Recommend improvements to manufacturing specifications, product drawings, testing methods, and acceptance standards.
  • Initiate and support Change Request Processes (CRP) related to product quality, tooling, gauges, scrap reduction, and process improvements.
  • Conduct work center audits and employee qualification assessments.
  • Train supervisors, team leaders, and production associates on quality systems and product quality standards.
  • Collaborate with Production, Engineering, Materials, Warehouse, Customer Service, and Supplier Quality teams to ensure consistent product quality.
  • Maintain accurate documentation and complete administrative activities associated with quality systems.

Qualifications

Required

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Minimum of 3 years of quality assurance or related experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
  • Strong understanding of quality control principles and manufacturing processes.
  • Ability to read and interpret blueprints, technical drawings, and specifications.
  • Experience using precision measuring equipment such as calipers and micrometers.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

Preferred

  • ASQ Certified Quality Technician (CQT) certification.
  • Completion of a Department of Labor-approved apprenticeship program with an emphasis in Industrial or Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent combination of training and experience.
  • Experience with Statistical Process Control (SPC) and quality improvement methodologies.
  • Familiarity with SAP and quality management software systems.

Knowledge & Skills

Successful candidates will demonstrate:

  • Knowledge of ISO 9000 quality standards and manufacturing best practices.
  • Understanding of statistical analysis and quality measurement techniques.
  • Experience with corrective and preventive action processes.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality excellence.
  • Ability to analyze data and present findings clearly to various audiences.
  • Effective time management and prioritization skills.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical information effectively across departments.

Why Join Us?

  • Stable Monday–Friday schedule
  • Collaborative team environment
  • Opportunity to contribute to continuous improvement initiatives
  • Professional growth and development opportunities
  • Meaningful impact on product quality and customer satisfaction

Schedule: This is a 2nd Shift position working Monday through Friday from 3:00 PM to 11:00 PM.

Apply today and become part of a team dedicated to quality, innovation, and continuous improvement.


Benefits

Blum USA believes in offering their employees an excellent benefits package that includes:


  • Salaried position
  • Possible bonus opportunities
  • Health (Medical and Dental)
  • 401(k) with employer matching
  • Flexible Spending plans to cover eligible out of pocket health, dental and vision expenses
  • Competitive PTO Package
  • Term life insurance equal to annual salary at no cost to employee



Company Overview

For more than 60 years Blum has been manufacturing superior quality hinge systems, drawer runners, and lift systems that create emotion and enhance user convenience in the kitchen. With every product, we strive to develop solutions to ensure that cabinet doors and drawers open with ease, close softly and effortlessly, and make workflow and everyday kitchen use easier.

Over the decades our product range has grown and so has the company. Today, Blum has eight production plants in Austria, and manufacturing sites in Brazil, Poland and the United States. Approximately 9000 Blum employees all over the world concentrate on the vision of “perfecting motion” to satisfy the specific requirements of the end user, whether it is in the kitchen or in another living area of the home. This prerequisite is the source of all our product development and innovation

title: In Season Trader
description:
Role purpose:

The In-Season Trader plays a critical role within Supply chain. The primary responsibility is to optimize sales, profitability, and inventory levels throughout the season by making real-time trading decisions. The In-Season Trader monitors sales performance, analyses market trends, and collaborates with cross-functional teams to drive sales and maximize the commercial success of the product assortment.


The key duties and responsibilities of the role are as follows:

  1. Sales and Inventory Analysis: Monitor daily and weekly sales performance, inventory levels, and sell-through rates across product categories, channels, and locations. Analyse sales data, market trends, and customer insights to identify opportunities and risks.
  2. Trading Strategy: Develop and execute an in-season trading strategy aligned with the overall Banner & business objectives. Collaborate with the buying, planning & Operation teams to adjust inventory levels and promotional activities based on market dynamics.
  3. Inventory Management: Work closely with the buying and planning teams to ensure optimal inventory levels across stores and e-commerce channels. Make recommendations for replenishment, transfers, and markdowns to optimize stock levels and minimize stockouts or excess inventory.
  4. Assortment Optimization: Collaborate with the buying and planning teams to analyse the performance of individual products and categories. Recommend assortment adjustments, product substitutions, or exit strategies to optimize sales and meet customer demand.
  5. Manage Inventory Intake: Work closely with Supply chain administration, to monitor & manage inventory intake from Suppliers.
  6. Market and Competitor Analysis: Stay informed about market trends, competitor activities, and customer preferences. Conduct regular competitor analysis to identify opportunities and react to market changes effectively.
  7. Cross-functional Collaboration: Collaborate with various teams, including buying, planning, marketing, logistics & retail operations to align trading strategies with overall business goals. Provide insights and recommendations based on real-time market intelligence to drive cross-functional decision-making.
  8. Seasonal and Weekly Reporting: Prepare and present regular reports on sales performance, inventory metrics, and promotional effectiveness. Provide actionable insights and recommendations to senior management and cross-functional teams.
  9. Continuous Improvement: Stay updated with industry best practices, new technologies, and trading methodologies. Continuously identify opportunities to improve trading processes, tools, and systems for more efficient and effective trading operations.


KPIs:

  • Total Sales & Revenue Growth.
  • GP.
  • Sell through Rate.
  • Markdown %
  • Stock Turnover.
  • Excess & Terminal Stock.
  • DIFOT.


Core competencies, knowledge, and experience:

  • Degree/Diploma in business, marketing, fashion merchandising, or a related field is a plus.
  • 2 years of experience in fashion retail trading, planning, or a similar role within the fashion industry.
  • Strong knowledge of fashion trends & customer behaviour.
  • Excellent analytical and numerical skills, with the ability to interpret data and trends.
  • Proficiency in planning and inventory management systems. Knowledge of pricing tools and analytics software is a plus.
  • Strong business acumen, understanding of retail operations, and inventory management.
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate and build relationships with cross-functional teams.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Familiarity with Retail Planning, product lifecycle, and fashion retail processes is a plus.

title: A&E Handling/Storage,Transportation Lead
description:
Position Title

A&E Handling / Storage, Transportation Lead

Position Classification

Non-Exempt

Position Type

FULL-TIME - This position is scheduled to work standard shift hours as required to support Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) operations, to include early-morning magazine operations and split-shift warehouse hours. Overtime and after-hours recall may be required to support ammunition transport, training evolutions, and emergent operational requirements.

Work Location

Strategic Weapons Facility Pacific (SWFPAC) / Marine Corps Security Force Battalion (MCSFBN), Naval Base Kitsap, Bangor, WA, with occasional travel to outlying ranges in Pierce and Yakima Counties and other locations within Washington State.

Position Description

The A&E Handling / Storage, Transportation Lead is responsible for the overall daily supervision, safety, coordination, and management of Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) handling, storage, and transportation operations in support of SWFPAC and MCSFBN. This role oversees the receipt, storage, issue, sentencing, and accountability of Hazard Class/Division 1.1 through 1.4 explosives and ammunition; leads and schedules qualified, certified, and properly licensed ammunition transportation personnel and vehicles supporting on- and off-station live-fire training and qualification ranges; and ensures compliance with Navy, Marine Corps, and DOD ammunition safety, security, and handling regulations. The incumbent serves as a designated Functional Area Lead and reports program status and compliance in writing to the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR).

Essential Position Functions

  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience related to A&E storage, accountability, and transport, in accordance with PWS Section 3.1.3.
  • Provide daily overall coordination, management, control, oversight, and supervision of A&E Handling / Storage, Transportation functional area personnel to ensure proper, effective, and complete performance of PWS requirements.
  • Establish and maintain a Qualification/Certification (Qual/Cert) Program in accordance with OPNAVINST 8023.24 (series) and AA&E Screening and Medical certification requirements under OPNAVINST 5530.13 (series) / MCO 5530.14 (series); maintain personnel physical and certification folders for all employees handling A&E.
  • Certified to handle Hazard Class/Division 1.1 through 1.4 explosives; ensure proper storage, segregation, and security of ammunition across up to seven (7) magazines, storing up to sixteen (16) DODIC types, in accordance with NAVSEA OP 5, NAVSUP P-724, and applicable physical security policy manuals.
  • Provide and schedule a minimum of six (6) qualified, certified, and properly licensed ammunition transportation personnel and three trucks to transport A&E to on- and off-station live-fire ranges throughout Washington State, including Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM) and Yakima.
  • Ensure two (2) dedicated Ammunition Transport vehicles (minimum GVWR 12,500 lbs. / payload 7,180 lbs.) are maintained and available, with a third vehicle cross-utilized for Defense Logistics Agency disposition/deliveries, facility deliveries, and transport of personnel for facility inspections when a third transport vehicle is required.
  • Prepare and deliver a rolling two-month Ammunition Transport Schedule (CDRL A011) reflecting planned and conducted transports, delivery locations, estimated number of vehicles required, and overtime needs, supporting an estimated 150 ammunition transports annually (approximately 80 within a 25-mile radius, 65 within a 100-mile radius, and 5 within a 250-mile radius of Base).
  • Oversee entry of receipt, replenishment, and issue transactions into the Ordnance Information System (OIS)/Total Ammunition Management Information System (TAMIS); ensure a minimum of two personnel are trained as primary and alternate OIS Database Administrator (DBA).
  • Oversee ammunition sentencing actions for 2T and 0T Cognizant (COG) ammunition in accordance with NAVSUP P-805 and coordinate related training with the Government TA/COR.
  • Verify incoming material and ammunition against receipt documentation (NSN, part number, condition, quantity, NALC, and lot number); screen A&E for applicable Notices of Ammunition Reclassification (NARs) and update OIS records accordingly.
  • Ensure ammunition issues to authorized Security Force personnel do not exceed 20 weekly / 80 monthly, and are made only with appropriate Government authorization.
  • Prepare and deliver required CDRLs, including the Explosives Safety Qualifications/Standards Report (A009), A&E Hazard Class/Division 1.1-1.4 Annual Inventory Report (A010), Ammunition Expenditure Report (A012), Ammunition Monthly Inventory Results (A013), and Ammunition Non-Combat Allowance Status Report (A014).
  • Coordinate monthly and annual A&E inventories with Government-appointed Inventory Officials and independent inventory teams; report discrepancies to the SWFPAC/MCSFBN AA&E Officer immediately upon discovery.
  • Maintain compliance with all applicable Military and DOT regulations for the loading, blocking, bracing, and transport of explosives; perform DD Form 626 transport vehicle inspections.
  • Current, or the ability to obtain, a Secret security clearance level.
  • Advanced Office Automation computer/PC keyboarding skills.
  • Advanced Microsoft Office Suite experience.
  • Advanced office management/assistant skills.
  • Valid Commercial Driver's License (CDL) Class A with Hazmat endorsement preferred.
  • Bachelor's degree preferred; equivalent combination of military or civilian ammunition/explosives handling experience may substitute for formal education.

Competencies for the Role

The A&E Handling / Storage, Transportation Lead demonstrates strong leadership, safety, and regulatory compliance skills within a high-consequence explosives handling environment. This role requires sound judgment in supervising certified personnel, meticulous attention to inventory accountability and documentation, effective coordination with Government representatives (COR/TA), and the ability to plan and execute ammunition transport schedules while maintaining strict adherence to DOD, Navy, and Marine Corps A&E safety and security directives.

Physical Requirements for the Role

This position requires the ability to lift and move ammunition and explosive containers of varying weight (up to 50 lbs. or more with assistance/equipment), stand, walk, bend, and climb into and operate transport vehicles for extended periods, and work outdoors in varying weather conditions, including early-morning magazine operations. The role also requires the ability to wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and to operate a vehicle transporting DOT Class 1.1 through 1.4 explosives.

Reports To

Project Manager

Supervisory Responsibilities

Supervises A&E Handling / Storage, Transportation functional area personnel, including ammunition transportation drivers and warehouse/magazine support staff.

Work Environment

Work is performed primarily at ammunition magazines, warehouses, and staging/loading areas at Naval Base Kitsap, Bangor, WA, with regular travel to firing ranges throughout Western and Eastern Washington State. The environment involves exposure to explosives and hazardous materials requiring strict adherence to safety protocols, security procedures, and applicable DOD/Navy/Marine Corps regulations. Shift work, early-morning magazine operations, and after-hours recall may be required.

Security Clearance Requirements

Secret

Travel Requirements

Travel is anticipated to be 10%-25% within Washington State, including outlying ranges in Pierce and Yakima Counties, to support ammunition transport and training evolutions.

Compensation

Commensurate with experience and qualifications, and in accordance with the applicable Service Contract Act (SCA) Wage Determination for the Armory Lead/Ammo & Explosive Driver classification.

title: Senior Frontend Engineer (Analytics Product Lead)
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Frontend Engineer (Analytics Product Lead) based in the United States.

We are seeking a highly experienced Senior Frontend Engineer to lead frontend development for an advanced analytics platform serving the global financial markets. In this role, you will shape technical direction, build scalable and intuitive user interfaces, and help transform complex financial data into powerful user experiences. You will work closely with product managers, backend engineers, and engineering leaders to deliver reliable, high-performance applications using React, TypeScript, and GraphQL. As a technical lead, you will influence frontend architecture, establish engineering standards, mentor teammates, and champion accessibility, testing, and code quality. You will also explore and promote AI-assisted and agentic coding tools to improve development efficiency without compromising security or maintainability. This remote opportunity offers a collaborative engineering environment where innovation, ownership, continuous improvement, and measurable product outcomes are highly valued.

Accountabilities

  • Frontend technical leadership: Serve as the frontend technical lead for the DataLab product, helping guide the Mission Control team's engineering priorities and technical direction across the Western Hemisphere.

  • Application development: Design, develop, and maintain complex, scalable, and performant web interfaces using React and TypeScript for enterprise financial applications.

  • Frontend architecture: Guide architectural decisions, component design, reusable UI patterns, and implementation standards to improve consistency, scalability, and maintainability.

  • Cross-functional collaboration: Partner with product managers, backend engineers, and other stakeholders to translate business requirements into effective technical solutions, contributing wherever necessary to achieve the best product outcomes.

  • Engineering quality: Promote high standards for code quality, security, accessibility, performance, and maintainability throughout the development lifecycle.

As a Quality Specialist in our Durable Goods Manufacturing company, you will play a crucial role in ensuring that our products meet the highest standards of quality. title: Software Engineer - Genesys Architect| IVR and Backend Tools Development
description:

The ideal candidate will have deep expertise in Genesys or similar Contact Center platforms, with a strong focus on architecture, integration, and backend development. This role will play a critical part in enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency by delivering scalable and robust solutions.

1. IVR Design and Development:
Design, develop, and implement IVR solutions using Genesys or other Contact Center platforms.
Collaborate with stakeholders to gather requirements and translate them into effective IVR call flows.
Optimize IVR systems to improve customer experience, reduce call handling time, and enhance self-service capabilities.
Ensure IVR solutions are aligned with business goals and comply with industry standards.

Develop and maintain backend tools and integrations to support Contact Center operations.
Build APIs and middleware to enable seamless communication between systems (e.g., CRM, WFM, telephony platforms).

Monitor and maintain Genesys and other backend systems to ensure high availability and performance.

5. Collaboration and Stakeholder Management:
Work closely with business stakeholders, operations teams, and IT to understand requirements and deliver solutions.
Act as a subject matter expert (SME) for Genesys and other Contact Center tools, providing guidance and support as needed.
Communicate technical concepts and solutions to non-technical stakeholders in a clear and concise manner.

6. Documentation and Training:
Create and maintain detailed documentation for IVR call flows, system architecture, and backend tools.

Hands-on experience with Genesys Engage, Genesys Cloud, or other Contact Center platforms.
Experience in backend development, API integration, and middleware solutions.

Technical Skills:
Proficiency in Genesys tools (e.g., Composer, Designer, Interaction Routing Designer, SIP Server).
Strong programming skills in languages such as Java, Python, or C#.
Experience with APIs, web services (REST/SOAP), and database technologies (SQL, NoSQL).
Familiarity with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure) and containerization (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) is a plus.
Knowledge of telephony protocols (e.g., SIP, VoIP) and Contact Center metrics.

Soft Skills:
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Attention to detail and a commitment to delivering high-quality solutions.

System Architecture and Design
IVR Development

API Integration
Collaboration and Teamwork
Problem-Solving

title: GROUNDS PERSON
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

The Grounds Person is responsible for safely directing crane operations during the lifting, moving, and placement of precast panels. This role uses rigging equipment, communicates continuously with the crane operator, and ensures panels are properly handled, stored, and shipped in a safe and efficient manner.

Salary range $25.12/Hour.

SAFETY IS OUR HIGHEST PRIORITY. Safety is our highest priority. We believe a safe workplace is built on mutual respect, care, and accountability. Every team member is empowered and expected to follow safety practices, look out for one another, and speak up about potential risks. Together, we create an environment where everyone goes home safely each day.

WHY JOIN OUR TEAM?

At Wells, you’re part of a team that takes pride in building something that lasts. Whether you’re in operations, a manufacturing facility, or out in the field, your work plays a direct role in creating quality structures that support our communities. We value hard work, reliability, and teamwork because getting the job done right requires teamwork. With a strong focus on safety, collaboration, and ingenuity, we create an environment where you can build your experience, contribute to meaningful work, and make an impact.

WHAT WE OFFER
Wells provides a competitive benefits package designed to support employees’ health, financial well-being, and work-life balance. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance, company-paid disability and life insurance, wellness incentives, paid holidays, PTO, flexible spending accounts, HSA options, a 401(k) with profit sharing, access to Nice Healthcare, employee assistance resources, pet insurance, and additional voluntary coverage such as critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity plans.

  • Health and family care leave is available to both union and non-union employees.
  • Union employee benefits are provided through separate collective bargaining agreements

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Responsible for signaling the crane operator during panel lifting and placement.
  • Uses rigging devices for the transportation, storage, and shipping of precast panels.
  • Hooks and unhooks lifting cables, ring clutches, and spreader bars.
  • Guides the cranes and is to always remain in constant communication via two-way radio with the crane operator as they guide the crane around blind spots.
  • Place dunnage used to store panels in racks or trailers for shipping to customers.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

The ideal candidate is safety-focused, highly alert, and communicates clearly while working in a fast-paced production environment. They work well on a team, remain attentive to surroundings, and are comfortable working at heights and around heavy equipment.

IDEAL CANDIDATES WILL HAVE

  • High school diploma or equivalent is preferred but not required.
  • Have the ability to work as part of a team and have effective communication skills.
  • Must always remain alert to your surroundings.
  • Maintains good housekeeping and always follows the safety policies and procedures.
  • Ability to climb ladders, man-lifts and scaffolding and work from heights.
  • Other duties may be assigned as needed.

WORKING CONDITIONS/PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Ability to perform physically demanding work, including lifting up to 75 lbs occasionally and frequent bending, climbing, kneeling, twisting, squatting, crawling, and repetitive hand/arm use
  • Capable of standing, walking, and moving throughout the facility for extended shifts of up to 12 hours
  • Comfortable working at heights using ladders, scaffolding, swing stages, and man lifts frequently
  • Ability to work safely in a production or field environment with moderate to high exposure to safety risks and hazards

  • Ability to wear all required PPE, including but not limited to safety boots, safety glasses, hearing protection, high visibility vest, hard hat, and other PPE as required by the task, department, or work area.

This profile summarizes key duties and expectations but does not list every possible job task. Employees must follow all job-related instructions and duties assigned by supervisors.

Wells is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including Veterans and Individuals with Disabilities. Wells participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your I-9 Form information to confirm you are authorized to work in the U.S.

title: Director, Legal & Compliance
description:
About the Company:

At Call the Car, we believe everyone deserves access to the healthcare they need without barriers. Our company was founded after identifying a critical gap in care that prevented many individuals from attending important medical appointments. By recognizing the need for reliable transportation and addressing key Social Determinants of Health (SDoH), we set out to create solutions to help people reach the care they deserve.

Our mission is to redefine Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT) as not just a ride, but as a pathway to healthier lives, stronger communities, and greater healthcare equity. Guided by our core values of Compassion, Empower, Flexible, and Caring, we are committed to delivering service that is not only reliable, but also respectful, supportive, and centered on the unique needs of every member we serve.

We are looking for passionate individuals to join us in making a meaningful impact. Together, we can help address barriers to healthcare, provide peace of mind through every ride, and create connections that move our communities toward better health, greater independence, and brighter futures.


Basic Job Purpose: Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, with a dotted-line reporting relationship to the Chief Executive Officer for compliance program matters, the Director of Legal and Compliance leads Call the Car's legal, contractual, insurance, and regulatory compliance activities and serves as the organization's designated Compliance Officer. The position reviews, drafts, and administers contracts across health plan clients and the transportation subcontractor network; coordinates insurance claims, litigation, and outside counsel; administers the compliance program, including delegation oversight, audits, and corrective action; monitors regulatory requirements affecting both brokerage and fleet operations; and partners with business leaders to identify and reduce risk. The position has direct and unrestricted access to the Chief Executive Officer and the governing body on compliance matters and may raise compliance concerns without retaliation. Success in this role requires sound judgment, careful analysis, clear communication, discretion, and the ability to translate legal and compliance requirements into practical business guidance.


RESPONSIBILITIES/DUTIES:

  1. Reviews, drafts, and coordinates contracts, amendments, confidentiality agreements, business associate agreements, vendor terms, and other business documents within delegated authority.
  2. Maintains an organized contract lifecycle process, including intake, review status, approvals, signature routing, renewal dates, notice requirements, insurance obligations, and retention.
  3. Identifies material legal, financial, operational, privacy, insurance, and compliance risks in proposed agreements and communicates recommended revisions to internal stakeholders.
  4. Coordinates contract negotiations with business owners, vendors, health plans, brokers, and outside counsel, as appropriate.
  5. Supports the intake, documentation, investigation, monitoring, and resolution of insurance claims, including automobile, general liability, professional liability, property, and other covered matters.
  6. Serves as a liaison among internal departments, insurance brokers, carriers, third-party administrators, adjusters, and outside counsel; tracks deadlines, requests, reserves, and matter status.
  7. Maintains legal and claims files, litigation holds, supporting evidence, correspondence, and privileged or confidential materials in accordance with applicable requirements.
  8. Serves as the organization's designated Compliance Officer; administers and maintains the compliance program, including the Code of Conduct, conflict of interest disclosures, annual compliance training, the confidential reporting hotline, and periodic compliance reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and the governing body; and monitors applicable federal, state, contractual, and healthcare requirements affecting non-emergency medical transportation brokerage and fleet operations.
  9. Assists with compliance assessments, internal reviews, audits, corrective action plans, regulatory inquiries, and responses to client or government requests.

title: Performance Video Editor (Meta DTC Ads) — Remote (CET ±2h), Full-time Contract
description:
Performance Video Editor (Meta DTC Ads) — Remote (CET ±2h), Full-time Contract

Our client is a US-based DTC wellness brand selling natural supplements directly to customers and growing through paid social. Meta is its main growth channel right now. The company is bringing creative production in-house, so this is a long-term, full-time role, not another short freelance gig.

Why this role is worth a look

  • Your ads run in a real ad account and get tested. You see which ones win, and winning ads earn a bonus.

  • You work directly with the VP of Growth. Feedback is fast, and there are no agency layers between you and the person making decisions.

  • The full toolkit is provided, including Adobe and AI tools like Higgsfield.

  • Volume is realistic, about 6 videos per month, so there’s time to do each ad properly.

  • The creative team is growing: you’ll be the second full-time editor.

What you’ll do

  • Edit short-form ads (up to 1–2 minutes) for Meta: UGC-style ads, AI voiceover ads and AI-generated animated ads

  • Turn scripts and raw assets into ads that hold attention: strong hooks, pacing, music and sound design

  • Generate AI voiceovers and, where needed, AI scenes

  • Make sure captions match the script exactly

  • Take feedback, apply it, and carry it into the next video

Volume is about 6 videos per month, depending on format. We care more about quality and learning from feedback than about speed.

How we work

  • You report directly to the VP of Growth

  • Tasks come through ClickUp with all assets provided. After onboarding, you work independently

  • We provide all tools, including Adobe and Higgsfield

  • Remote, with at least 4 hours of overlap with 9:00–16:00 CET

  • Full-time (40h/week), independent contractor agreement

  • Performance bonus for winning ads

What we’re looking for

  • A portfolio of real DTC paid social ads, ideally for Meta. This matters more than years of experience or a title

  • Experience with UGC ads. AI voiceovers or AI animation is a strong plus

  • Storytelling instinct: you know when to cut, when to change the rhythm and when sound does the work

  • Attention to detail

  • English good enough to work comfortably on Slack and proofread captions

Nice to have

  • Supplement or health/wellness ads

  • Experience with US-market brands

  • Hands-on experience with AI video tools (Higgsfield, Kling, Runway or similar)

Not a fit if your background is mainly YouTube or long-form editing without paid ads.

Process: a short intro call, then a paid trial on real projects.

To apply, send a link to your portfolio with ad examples and briefly note your role in each: edited, concept, AI work, etc.

title: Director of Product Development & Innovation

To be successful in this role, you must have a drive and passion for product along with an entrepreneurial spirit that thrives in an incredibly fast paced environment.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for the vision of designated brands. This includes driving the development and execution of products that align with the assigned brands/programs and where necessary, working with licensing team through strategic partnerships, and pivoting and re-positioning products and brands based on changing market environments.
  • Oversee the creative product development process, enforcing key milestones from product conceptualization to merchandising pass-off; working alongside senior cross-functional leadership in merchandising, design, sourcing, compliance and sales.
  • Drive new product execution while maintaining existing portfolio of products; lead white space due diligence efforts with product development to identify growth avenues.
  • Mentor creative development team on consistent connection between ideation and marketability and bottom-line sales generation & profitability.
  • Work alongside merchandising teams to ensure all projects align with divisional strategic goals, whether in brand extensions, category expansion, direct sourcing initiatives and/or parallel category diversification.
  • Strategize with sales and merchandising leads on quantifying and prioritizing new category growth opportunities; balancing with corporate initiatives and core competencies.
  • Collaborate with design and engineering team members to generate and execute new product and packaging concepts.
  • Communicate with overseas offices on all existing brands, new product development and global sourcing initiatives; Lead strategic sourcing/negotiations efforts as necessary in projects surrounding new product categories, partnering with merchandising, sourcing and Shanghai teams. Collaborate with sourcing teams to identify needs outside of existing vendor matrix in order to develop incremental subcategories for volume-driving innovation projects.
  • Proactively work alongside product safety and compliance teams to ensure a consistently high level of quality for all kids product categories.
  • Lead regular competitive landscape reports across major channels of distribution, identifying key market and product gaps and opportunities.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to prepare for retail presentations and industry trade shows.
  • Partner with merchandising leads on strategic costing negotiations in collaboration with global sourcing and overseas merchandising teams; ideate and innovate with an eye towards costing goals while maintaining the integrity of the product.
  • Understand POS data and identify plans to capitalize on trending products and categories; as well as identify gaps in distribution and retail laddering.
  • Collaborate across the organization to lead product vision alongside design execution, and provide product development leadership to all segments of the business.
  • Professionally train, develop and mentor members of the product development & innovation team.

What You’ll Bring:

  • At least 8 years of product development/merchandising/brand management experience, ideally within a very fast-paced, quick turnaround industry. Toy, Tween or Craft experience is HIGHLY preferred.
  • Experience with custom product development is required.
  • Must be a dynamic, passionate leader with ability to multi-task amidst shifting priorities.
  • Must have strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to effectively present in front of large audiences.
  • Must have the ability to work in a hybrid capacity from our New Providence, NJ office at least twice per week.

title: Brownfield Redevelopment Project Manager

For over 70 years Fishbeck has been building. As a 100% employee-owned firm, every team member has a stake in what we build together—our work, our reputation, and our future. Now we need to add a Brownfield Redevelopment Project Manager to help us keep building.
Working with our environmental team, you will lead Brownfield Redevelopment projects supported by private investment, EGLE grants and loans, USEPA grants, and other programs. Public speaking and stakeholder engagement are required.

The Benefits Verification Specialist is responsible for conducting outbound calls to insurance payers to complete Pharmacy Benefit Manager (PBM) and Medical Management (MM) benefit verifications, with no inbound call responsibilities. Extensive knowledge in specialized functions with a wide and comprehensive acquaintance with and understanding of both general and specific aspects of the job and their practical application to complex problems and situations ordinarily encountered.

  • Educate patients, prescribers, and others regarding program requirements, and facilitate referrals. Maintain good housekeeping techniques, adhering to quality and production standards and comply with all applicable company, state, and federal safety and environmental programs and procedures.


Desired Skills and Qualifications:

title: Radiation Test Engineer
description:
Radiation Test Engineer

Houston, TX

About Intuitive Machines:

Intuitive Machines is an innovative and cutting-edge space company making cislunar space accessible to both public and private customers. Our mission is to further science and exploration, communications, and economic progress from the Earth to the Moon and beyond. With multiple NASA lunar missions in development and additional private missions on our manifest, we pride ourselves in supporting NASA, our customers, and the nation in paving the way to return humans to the surface of the Moon. Our world-class team includes experts in all aspects of spacecraft subsystems design, development, and test, on-orbit operations, and safety.

About the Position:

We are seeking a radiation test engineer for the Intuitive Machines NOVA-C / NOVA-D Lunar Lander and Altus Lunar Satellite programs. The role will serve as the technical authority for defining mission-based radiation environments, providing hardware design implementations to handle those environments, establishing test programs to evaluate the hardware solutions, coordinating with test facilities to execute these test programs, and analyzing the test results to quantify the hardware solutions’ ability to meet the mission objectives in the environments.

Your work will have a direct impact on program success, supporting spacecraft builds, payload integration, mission rehearsals, and full end-to-end system tests. This is a hands on, high ownership role at the center of spacecraft and payload integration. Reports to Avionics Director.

Responsibilities:

  • Define radiation environments per mission,
  • Define tests based on those environments, including these support tasks”
  • Create functional block & harness diagrams for the tests
  • Design test cables
  • Design (Altium) test PCBs
  • Perform cross section / probabilistic analyses on test results.
  • Develop test plans and test procedures for payload and spacecraft system testing
  • Track risks, integration issues, and system limitations; drive mitigation strategies
  • Manage configuration changes as flight hardware and payloads evolve over the program lifecycle
  • Ensure safe operations, access control, and hardware handling discipline
  • Define program requirements based on radiation environment.
  • Help standing up Radiation hardness program for IM. We are starting to come up on 5years of our initial testing and we are still banking on parts being the same. There are industry techniques to help mitigate this w/o having to retest every single part.
  • Be familiar with Radiation mitigation strategies in hardware or firmware, in an effort to mitigate / redirect usage for hardware that may have initially failed testing.
  • General SME consulting about radiation, parts selection, etc. Become familiar with our missions, devices, vehicle architecture, etc. to provide guidance internally to the design and development engineers.
  • Own test campaigns from start to finish, coordinating with engineers for designing test bench's, documenting dry runs, and test logistics. IM test conductor for all radiation tests, making real time decisions during irradiation. Follow up on test reports, implications from test data, and proper design mitigations.
  • Negotiates contracts for beam time for Proton and Heavey Ion test facilities.
  • Performs radiation analysis and supports engineering with recommended mitigation tactics.
  • Conducts experiments to evaluate total ionizing dose (TID), displacement damage dose (DDD), single-event effects (SEE), and dose rate effects on microelectronics and semiconductor devices.
  • Works with outside customers to define mission radiation requirements.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or Physics, or related field with applicable experience.
  • 5+ years relevant experience (3+ with MS)
  • Handson experience with spacecraft subsystems, avionics, or hardware-in-the-loop(HWIL) testbeds
  • Ability to interpret electrical schematics, system diagrams, and interface definitions
  • Experience with test planning and test procedure development
  • Strong understanding of spacecraft power systems, communications, C&DH, and ground interfaces
  • Ability to work effectively in fast paced, evolving technical environments
  • U.S. citizenship

Preferred Requirements:

  • Scripting experience (Labview, python, JavaScript, VBA).
  • Experience designing or operating Flatsat, HWIL, or spacecraft system testbed
  • Background in high reliability or mission critical systems
  • Experience supporting environmental tests or mission readiness/rehearsals

US EEO Statement:

Intuitive Machines is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Loads Engineer
description:
Help Build Europe's Hypersonic Capability
At Hypersonica, we’re redefining what’s possible in European defence technology. We exist to deliver speed, resilience, and technological independence at a pace that sets a new standard. We are a small, elite team working on problems that matter, and solving them fast.
By joining Hypersonica, you’re not stepping into a predefined role. You’re joining a talent dense environment where every individual shapes the direction of the company. Our philosophy is to hire a small number of exceptional people with broad, deep technical capability, strong judgement, and the ability to operate autonomously.
We hire for talent, not rigid boxes. This role represents a business need, but the way it evolves will be shaped by the individual. If you’ve achieved what others said was impossible, or you bring a unique combination of skills that doesn’t fit a traditional mould, we want to hear from you. The work you do here directly contributes to Europe’s technological independence.

What you'll do

  • Load Analysis & Definition: Calculate and establish static and dynamic design load cases for all flight and ground phases, including transportation, launchpad operations, engine ignition, atmospheric ascent (aerodynamic loads), staging, re-entry, and landing.

  • Coupled Loads Analysis (CLA): Build and execute complex mathematical simulation models by coupling launch vehicle and payload models to predict critical flight environments and transient events.

  • Modeling & Simulation: Develop and optimize finite element models (FEM) and perform structural dynamics analyses, including transient, sinusoidal, random vibration (PSD), gusts, and acoustic response analyses.

  • Testing & Validation: Design, oversee, and analyze data from physical tests (e.g., modal surveys, vibration, and shock testing) and correlate simulation models with actual flight telemetry data.

Who you are

  • Education: University degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field with a strong focus on structural dynamics or continuum mechanics.

  • Experience: Proven experience in structural loads definition, structural dynamics, or aeroelasticity, ideally within the development of launch vehicles, satellites, or missiles.

Technical Skills:

  • Deep understanding of structural dynamics, vibe/shock environments, and acoustic phenomena.

  • Proficiency with commercial FEA solvers (Optistruct) and pre-/post-processors (HyperMesh).

What we offer

  • A mission driven environment with the opportunity to work on one of Europe’s most consequential defence challenges, with direct impact on sovereign capability and security.
  • Daily collaboration with top experts across engineering, operations, and defence, with real opportunity to learn from the best, contribute, and grow.
  • High ownership and autonomy; no time tracking, no micromanagement, just clear objectives and accountability for outcomes.
  • A fast paced environment where good ideas are implemented quickly, and feedback from test and flight drives real decisions.
  • A culture that values clarity, integrity, and excellence, and supports people who take initiative and push boundaries responsibly.
  • Competitive compensation and real share options aligned to responsibility and impact, not tenure or hierarchy.
At Hypersonica, every hire raises the bar. We are deliberately small, intensely capable, and deeply mission-driven. If this role feels like a strong fit, or if you believe you bring something exceptional that goes beyond the description, we encourage you to apply.
Hypersonica is an equal-opportunity employer and assesses candidates solely on merit, capability, and potential.
You can apply directly to this role or reach out to Nathan Sweeney, Head of Talent. We review every application and aim to respond to all candidates within two weeks, whether the answer is yes or no.

title: Propulsion Engineer - Liquid Rocket Engines
description:
Propulsion Engineer – Liquid Rocket Engines

Houston, TX

About Intuitive Machines:

Intuitive Machines is an innovative and cutting-edge space company making cislunar space accessible to both public and private customers. Our mission is to further science and exploration, communications, and economic progress from the Earth to the Moon and beyond. With multiple NASA lunar missions in development and additional private missions on our manifest, we pride ourselves in supporting NASA, our customers, and the nation in paving the way to return humans to the surface of the Moon. Our world-class team includes experts in all aspects of spacecraft subsystems design, development, and test, on-orbit operations, and safety.

About the Position:

We are seeking a Propulsion Design Engineer to support the development of next-generation liquid rocket engines and propulsion hardware. This role is primarily focused on the design, analysis, fabrication, and testing of liquid rocket engine injectors and associated combustion hardware. The successful candidate will play a key role in developing injector architectures, combustion devices, and additively manufactured engine components through rapid design-build-test iterations.

The successful candidate will work closely with propulsion analysts, thermal engineers, structures engineers, manufacturing personnel, and test engineers to develop flight and development hardware from initial concept through hot-fire testing. This is a hands-on engineering role requiring deep technical engagement with hardware design, analysis, fabrication, and test execution.

Responsibilities:

  • Design liquid rocket engine components including injectors, combustion chambers, manifolds, feed system hardware, and associated propulsion components.
  • Develop detailed 3D CAD models, assemblies, drawings, and manufacturing documentation
  • Perform engineering analyses supporting propulsion hardware design, including structural, thermal, fluid, and manufacturability assessments.
  • Develop propulsion hardware optimized for additive manufacturing processes, including complex internal flow features, integrated manifolds, cooling circuits, design-for-additive-manufacturing considerations, and post-processing requirements.
  • Work closely with internal machine shop, additive manufacturing, and fabrication teams to mature designs from concept to hardware.
  • Support component assembly, development testing, hot-fire testing, post-test hardware evaluations, and data analysis.
  • Investigate hardware anomalies and implement design improvements based on test results and lessons learned.
  • Collaborate with structures, thermal, manufacturing, test, and systems engineering teams throughout the hardware development lifecycle.
  • Support rapid design-build-test iterations in a fast-paced development environment.

Requirements:

  • BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or related engineering discipline.
  • Minimum 3-5 years of design, fabrication, and testing of liquid rocket engines and related components
  • Experience designing and testing injectors or cooled combustion chambers for liquid rocket engines.
  • Proficiency with Creo, SolidWorks, or equivalent CAD software.
  • Strong understanding of fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, heat transfer, and combustion fundamentals.
  • Experience creating manufacturing drawings, tolerance schemes, and engineering documentation for fabricated hardware.
  • Ability to develop engineering analyses and communicate technical recommendations.
  • Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary engineering teams.

Preferred / Differentiating Experience:

  • Experience developing cryogenic propulsion systems or hardware.
  • Experience evaluating injector performance, atomization, combustion efficiency, combustion stability, or related combustion device characteristics.
  • Experience with combustion chamber heat transfer, vacuum nozzles, electric pumps or turbomachinery, internal manifolding, or feed system hardware.
  • Experience with additive manufacturing of metallic aerospace hardware and design-for-additive-manufacturing (DfAM) principles.
  • Experience supporting component-level or engine-level hot-fire testing.
  • Experience performing CFD, thermal, structural, combustion, or multidisciplinary analyses supporting propulsion hardware development.
  • Experience working closely with machine shops, additive manufacturing facilities, and propulsion test organizations.
  • Experience developing hardware for aerospace, launch vehicle, spacecraft, or defense applications.

US EEO Statement:

Intuitive Machines is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Staff Front End Engineer (Web Core)
description:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

We at Pleo are on a mission to make spend management surprisingly effective and empowering. We build a product used by thousands of companies across Europe, and our web app is a core part of that experience.

We’re hiring a Staff Engineer to join Web Core — our frontend platform team. The Web Core team exists to enable product engineers across Pleo to build and ship high-quality web software. We own the foundations of the web stack (tooling, patterns, architecture, reliability of the developer workflow), and we partner closely with product teams to make delivery faster, safer, and more consistent.

What Web Core does

  • Build and maintain a web platform that teams use to efficiently deliver excellent web experiences.

  • Drive technical excellence across Pleo’s web applications (architecture, patterns, quality, performance, accessibility).

  • Improve developer experience (DX) through tooling, CI reliability, and fast feedback loops.

  • Steward shared web foundations (libraries, conventions, golden paths) and support adoption.

  • Facilitate and contribute to the broader frontend community at Pleo.

What you’ll be doing

As a Staff Engineer in Web Core, you will be a force multiplier. You’ll work across teams and systems to remove constraints and raise the bar for how we build and run web software.

  • Set technical direction for parts of our web platform, and drive alignment across teams.

  • Identify the biggest leverage opportunities for web engineering at Pleo (quality, delivery speed, reliability) and execute on them.

  • Partner with product engineers and leads to design solutions that fit the wider ecosystem.

  • Build and evolve internal tooling, frameworks, and golden paths that scale across teams.

  • Improve the reliability and usability of our CI and local developer workflows.

  • Coach and mentor engineers, and help grow technical leadership in the frontend community.

  • Contribute hands-on in code. This role blends strategy and execution. You should expect to be coding a meaningful part of the time.

You’ll bring solid experience with

  • Building and maintaining complex web applications at scale.

  • TypeScript and modern frontend engineering (React experience is a plus).

  • Designing maintainable systems (including frontend-facing APIs and platform boundaries).

  • Testing practices and tooling (unit, integration, end-to-end) and a strong quality mindset.

  • CI/CD and developer productivity improvements (faster, more reliable feedback loops).

  • Observability and monitoring practices for web systems (metrics, logging, tracing, alerting).

  • Working effectively across teams and stakeholders, and communicating tradeoffs clearly.

Your colleagues would say you

  • Lead by example and raise the bar with pragmatism and care.

  • Communicate clearly, listen well, and bring people along in decisions.

  • Enjoy breaking down complex problems, gathering input, and driving to a solution.

  • Coach others and create space for people to grow.

  • Prefer progress over perfection, while still caring deeply about quality.

Show me the benefits

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Lunch is on us - with catering in our Lisbon, Copenhagen and London offices or a monthly lunch allowance paid directly together with your salary in other markets

  • Private health insurance to ensure you’re fit in body and mind to do your best work

  • Wellbeing days - fully paid days off designed for a slower pace, allowing you to take time to recharge and prioritise self-care

  • We provide access to MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and wellbeing support with great success so far

  • Access to LinkedIn Learning - acquire new skills, stay abreast of industry trends and fuel your personal and professional development continuously

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

About your application

  • English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

  • A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

  • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

  • Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.

  • Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

  • Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

  • Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

title: Quality Management System Specialist
description:

REXA is growing, and this is an exciting time to join our team. As we expand into our new headquarters and manufacturing facility at 200 Canopy Drive in Middleborough, MA, we are looking for talented, hands-on people who want to build their careers with a company investing in its future, its people, and the local community. title: Appliance Logistics Scheduler
description:
Scheduler / Dispatcher

Job Description

Position Summary

The Scheduler/Dispatcher is responsible for coordinating and managing the scheduling, communication, routing, and daily invoicing of delivery and installation orders. This position serves as a key communication link between customers, sales, warehouse personnel, and field delivery and installation teams. The Scheduler/Dispatcher must be highly organized, detail-oriented, responsive, and able to effectively manage changing priorities while maintaining excellent customer service.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Scheduling & Customer Communication

  • Schedule all delivery and installation orders through email, call checks, and direct phone conversations.
  • Schedule pre-site visits for applicable orders.
  • Contact customers promptly when delivery or installation schedules change and clearly communicate updated information.
  • Accept and respond to customer calls regarding order scheduling and make scheduling adjustments as needed.
  • Maintain professional and courteous communication with customers throughout the scheduling process.
  • Communicate all changes in delivery or installation dates back to the appropriate sales team, even when the customer has already been contacted regarding the change.

Dispatch & Ticket Management

  • Print tickets for the warehouse and clearly highlight important information, special instructions, and changes.
  • Upload, organize, and route all tickets through DispatchTrack.
  • Send appropriate customer and internal notifications through DispatchTrack.
  • Communicate with delivery and installation personnel in the field to adjust routes and assignments as needed.
  • Monitor field progress and assist with routing decisions throughout the day.
  • Keep the Excel scheduling calendar current and accurate, reflecting all scheduled deliveries and installations.

Invoicing & Administrative Responsibilities

  • Invoice all completed tickets daily.
  • Ensure tickets are invoiced promptly and do not remain on hold unnecessarily.
  • Maintain accurate scheduling and ticket records.
  • Ensure changes, updates, and special instructions are documented and communicated to the appropriate departments.

Field & Department Communication

  • Maintain consistent communication with delivery and installation teams in the field.
  • Monitor and communicate information regarding product damage, delivery issues, or other concerns.
  • Relay damage and field-related information to the appropriate sales personnel promptly.
  • Communicate regularly with Shayne and Jade regarding field performance and scheduling.
  • Notify Shayne and Jade when trucks or routes are falling behind schedule so that corrective action can be taken to minimize unnecessary overtime and keep operations running efficiently.
  • Work closely with sales, warehouse, delivery, and installation teams to ensure a smooth and coordinated operation.

Qualifications & Skills

  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to effectively communicate with customers, sales personnel, warehouse employees, and field teams.
  • Ability to remain calm and professional when schedules change or unexpected issues arise.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and other computer-based scheduling systems.
  • Ability to learn and effectively utilize DispatchTrack.
  • Strong sense of urgency and follow-through.
  • Customer-service oriented with a professional and positive attitude.

Key Performance Expectations

The Scheduler/Dispatcher is expected to maintain accurate schedules, communicate changes promptly, keep tickets and invoices current, and provide ongoing support to field teams. Success in this position requires proactive communication, attention to detail, and the ability to anticipate and resolve scheduling or operational issues before they negatively impact customers or the field team.

The overall goal of this position is to keep deliveries and installations organized, customers informed, field teams supported, and daily operations running efficiently while minimizing delays and unnecessary overtime.

title: Senior Global Environmental Compliance Specialist
description:
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives. Our wearable technology and personalized insights help people optimize recovery, sleep, training, and overall health. As we continue to expand globally, ensuring our products meet evolving environmental regulations is critical to delivering innovative hardware to members around the world.

We’re looking for a Senior Global Environmental Compliance Specialist to lead WHOOP’s global environmental product compliance. In this role, you’ll own the strategy, execution, and continuous evolution of our environmental compliance framework, ensuring our products meet global regulatory requirements throughout the product lifecycle while enabling rapid innovation and worldwide market access.

Responsibilities

  • Ensure WHOOP’s products meet environmental compliance standards in all current and planned global markets, including regulations such as RoHS, REACH, California Proposition 65, SCIP, POPs, battery, and packaging requirements.

  • Lead regulatory reporting, product declarations, and data submissions to ensure timely and accurate compliance across global markets.

  • Partner with Hardware, Operations and other cross-functional teams to ensure environmental compliance requirements are considered throughout product development, from concept through end of life.

  • Collaborate with Global Supply Management and suppliers to communicate evolving regulatory requirements, collect compliance documentation, and improve supplier readiness.

  • Monitor the global regulatory landscape, assess business impact, and provide recommendations that proactively address emerging environmental requirements.

  • Develop and improve compliance processes, documentation, and operational procedures that scale with WHOOP’s product portfolio.

  • Manage environmental compliance data and documentation within compliance management systems, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency through automation.

  • Develop and maintain Bio-compatibility testing standards as appropriate for wearable products. Ensure the team understands requirements applicable to each product and incorporates appropriate bio-compatibility tests early in development.

  • Partner with cross functional teams to satisfy Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) obligations across global markets, including WEEE, Battery, and Packaging waste management registration, data reporting, and Producer Responsibility Organization (PRO) management.

  • Support company initiatives related to voluntary environmental standards and sustainability programs.

Qualifications

title: Construction Project Manager
description:
OVERVIEW
The Construction Project Manager is responsible for the successful execution of foodservice equipment projects from contract award through project closeout. This role serves as the primary point of contact between Singer Equipment, owners, general contractors, consultants, manufacturers, subcontractors, and internal departments to ensure projects are completed on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with contract requirements.
The Construction Project Manager coordinates all phases of project execution including submittals, procurement, scheduling, installation coordination, issue resolution, customer communication, and project closeout.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
Project Execution & Coordination

Assume ownership of projects upon contract award and manage all aspects of project execution through completion.
Serve as the primary GC contact throughout the life of the project.
Coordinate with general contractors, consultants, architects, engineers, manufacturers, installers, and internal departments.
Lead project coordination calls, and status update meetings.
Monitor project schedules and identify potential risks, delays, or conflicts.
Develop and maintain project documentation and tracking systems.

Submittal & Technical Management

Review contract documents, specifications, drawings, and project requirements.
Assemble, review, and submit equipment submittal packages for customer approval.
Coordinate revisions and responses to consultant and customer comments.
Work with design, estimating, purchasing, and manufacturing partners to ensure compliance with project requirements.
Review equipment layouts, utility requirements, and installation details for accuracy.

Procurement & Vendor Management

Coordinate equipment procurement activities with purchasing and manufacturers.
Follow production schedules, lead times, deliveries, and shipping logistics.
Resolve vendor-related issues that could impact project schedules or customer expectations.
Manage change orders and scope modifications throughout the project lifecycle.

Installation & Field Support

Coordinate installation schedules with contractors, field personnel, and customers.
Support field teams during installation and commissioning activities.
Address jobsite issues, equipment discrepancies, and scheduling conflicts.
Facilitate punch list completion and project closeout activities.

Financial & Administrative Responsibilities

Monitor project budgets, costs, and profitability.
Review project expenditures and identify potential cost impacts.
Assist with change order pricing and documentation.
Maintain accurate project records and correspondence.

Customer Relationship Management

Maintain strong working relationships with contractors, consultants, and manufacturers.
Communicate project status, issues, and resolutions in a professional and timely manner.
Represent Singer Equipment in project meetings and customer interactions.
Ensure a high level of customer satisfaction throughout the project lifecycle.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelors Degree is preferred, but not required.
Must have 1 -2 years previous experience in project management
Strong project management and organizational skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and contract documents.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and project management software.
Ability to work effectively with customers, contractors, consultants, manufacturers, and internal teams.

Impact on Business Operations
Project Managers play a critical role in protecting project profitability, maintaining customer relationships, ensuring successful project execution, and supporting company growth. The position directly influences customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, project outcomes, and long-term business development opportunities.

title: Propulsion Test Engineer
description:
Propulsion Test Engineer

Houston, TX

About Intuitive Machines

Intuitive Machines is an innovative and cutting-edge space company making cislunar space accessible to both public and private customers. We believe our mission is to further research, communications, and exploration beyond low lunar orbit. With multiple NASA lunar missions in the making and additional private missions on our manifest, we pride ourselves in supporting NASA, our customers, and the nation in paving the way to return humans to the surface of the moon. Our world-class team includes experts in all spacecraft subsystems design, development, and test, on-orbit operations, and safety.

About the Role

We are seeking a Test Engineer to support the design, operation, and continual improvement of propulsion and integrated vehicle test capabilities across multiple programs. This role is responsible for developing test infrastructure, designing and operating propulsion test stands, planning and executing development and qualification testing, and supporting large-scale system verification including spacecraft hot fires and environmental testing.

The position supports both cryogenic and storable propulsion systems and contributes across the full test lifecycle, from facility and test stand development through test planning, execution, data review, anomaly resolution, and continuous improvement. Depending on experience, this role may be filled at multiple engineering levels, with responsibilities and ownership scaling accordingly.

Responsibilities:

  • Design, develop,operate, and improve propulsion test stands, facility infrastructure, and ground support equipment.
  • Plan and execute development, qualification, acceptance, and integrated system testing of spacecraft, propulsion systems, engines, and associated hardware.
  • Develop test plans, operating procedures, hazard analyses, and test readiness documentation.
  • Support large-scale verification activities including spacecraft hot fires, propulsion system testing, vibration testing, and other integrated system tests.
  • Define instrumentation and data acquisition requirements and ensure high-quality test execution and data collection.
  • Analyze test results, troubleshoot anomalies, and implement corrective actions to improve hardware, facilities, and procedures.
  • Collaborate with propulsion, structures, avionics, manufacturing, facilities, safety, and operations teams throughout the test lifecycle.
  • Support design reviews, test readiness reviews, and post-test reviews.
  • Depending on experience, lead major test campaigns and mentor junior engineers.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or related Engineering discipline.
  • Strong fundamentals in fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, heat transfer, and structural mechanics.
  • Experience designing, building,operating, or supporting engineering test systems or complex mechanical systems.
  • Experience developing engineering test procedures and technical documentation.
  • Experience reducing, interpreting, and communicating engineering test data.
  • Familiarity with pressure systems, fluid systems, instrumentation, valves, regulators, piping, and mechanical hardware.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, cross-disciplinary engineering environment.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple parallel tasks.
  • Willingness to support test campaigns and mission operations schedules whenrequired.
  • Alignment with Intuitive Machines' core values: Respect, Integrity, Dedication, and Excellence.

Preferred / Differentiating Experience

  • Experience with propulsion, spacecraft, launch vehicle, or aerospace development testing.
  • Experience designing or operating propulsion test stands, ground support equipment, or hazardous test facilities.
  • Experience supporting cryogenic and/or storable propulsion systems.
  • Experience with integrated system testing including hot fire, vibration, thermal vacuum, or environmental testing.
  • Experience with instrumentation, data acquisition, LabVIEW, or automated test systems.
  • Proficiencywith MATLAB, Python, or similar engineering analysis tools.
  • Experience using Creo, SolidWorks, or equivalent CAD software.
  • Familiarity with NASA, DoD, or aerospace test and safety standards.

EEOC Statement

Intuitive Machines is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Job Title: YRC04G – REMS Auditor

Brief Description: The Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy [REMS] Auditor provides core compliance functions and project support for the REMS Stakeholder audit group. The REMS Auditor acts as a liaison with stakeholders such as healthcare settings, pharmacies, and wholesalers/distributors. This involves reviewing audit questionnaires, examining supporting documentation, and documenting all related information within project-specific applications. Through these efforts, the REMS Auditor ensures the smooth execution of audits while maintaining compliance standards and fostering effective communication with stakeholders. When necessary, this role involves supporting training for new hires, facilitating communication between the audit team and other internal and external teams and entities.

Specific job duties:

  • Conduct document reviews to ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance with REMS program standards.
  • Ensure timely follow-up on audit documentation deficiencies and actions as per client timelines, communicate via phone or email for outstanding documentation.
  • Identify, evaluate, and address any audit findings, and articulate results to stakeholders.
  • Accurately complete audit review forms to verify adherence to REMS program requirements.
